kunikma: Understand the advantages of farming on a river plain (nearby water, fertile soil)
usul: Remember what crops need to grow (water, fertile soil) and find which of these the river provides.

variantlar.savol:
The Zarafshan River flows across a plain. Along the river, farmers grow wheat and vegetables.
Which is one ADVANTAGE of farming along a river?
javoblar: Water for irrigating the crops is close by.
You can catch fish in the river.
You can wash clothes in the river water.
Crops along a river never get diseases.

yechim.ovoz: Crops need water, fertile soil and sunlight to grow.
If the river is close, it is easy to irrigate the fields through ditches.

yechim.doska: Fishing, washing clothes — nothing to do with farming
yechim.ovoz: Catching fish or washing clothes has nothing to do with growing crops.
So the correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B wrote a different benefit of the river, but catching fish has nothing to do with farming.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C chose a household benefit, but the question is about growing crops.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D chose a false statement: crops along a river can get diseases too.

variantlar.maslahat: What does a river give crops so they can grow?

variantlar.savol:
Every spring, when the water rises, the Amu Darya leaves silt (tiny particles of soil) on its banks. Farmers plant cotton, melons and other field crops there.
Which is one ADVANTAGE of farming along a river?
javoblar: There are a lot of stones along a river.
You can swim in the river.
Many birds fly along a river.
The silt brought by the river makes the soil fertile, so crops grow well.

yechim.ovoz: River water carries tiny particles of soil, called silt, down from the mountains.
The silt settles on the fields and makes the soil rich in substances that are good for plants.
In fertile soil, crops grow well and give a big harvest.
So the correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought stones are useful, but it is hard to grow crops on stony ground.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B wrote a benefit for leisure, which has nothing to do with farming.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C chose birds, but this does not explain how the harvest is helped.

variantlar.maslahat: Besides water, what else does the river bring to the fields?

kunikma: Understand the disadvantages of farming on a river plain (flooding, water pollution)
usul: Think about what dangers a river can pose to fields and farmers: flooding or pollution; do not confuse a benefit with a disadvantage.

variantlar.savol:
On the plain along the Syr Darya, farmers grow rice and corn.
Which is one DISADVANTAGE of farming along a river?
javoblar: The soil along a river is very fertile.
If the river freezes in winter, it is dangerous to walk on it.
After heavy rain or melting snow, the river can overflow and flood the crops.
The river has enough water to irrigate the crops.

yechim.doska: Disadvantage — something that harms the fields
yechim.ovoz: We need something that harms farming.

yechim.doska: Heavy rain, melting snow $\rightarrow$ river overflows
yechim.ovoz: In spring, when snow melts in the mountains or heavy rain falls, the river can rise and overflow its banks.

yechim.doska: Flood $\rightarrow$ crops end up under water
yechim.ovoz: Floodwater can cover the fields and destroy the crops.
Fertile soil and enough water are advantages. So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A confused an advantage with a disadvantage: fertile soil is a benefit.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B wrote a danger of the river, but walking on ice has nothing to do with farming.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D again chose an advantage: enough water is good for crops.

variantlar.maslahat: How can a river harm the fields?

variantlar.savol:
Farmers spray fertilizers and pesticides on fields along the Kashkadarya River.
Which is one DISADVANTAGE of farming along a river?
javoblar: You can catch fish in the river.
Rainwater can wash the fertilizers and pesticides from the fields into the river and pollute the water.
It is easy to irrigate the fields with river water.
Trees along the river give shade.

yechim.ovoz: We are looking for the harm that farming along a river can cause.

yechim.doska: Rain $\rightarrow$ fertilizers and pesticides $\rightarrow$ into the river
yechim.ovoz: When it rains, the fertilizers and pesticides on the fields are washed by the water into the nearby river.

yechim.doska: River gets polluted $\rightarrow$ harm to fish and people
yechim.ovoz: Such water harms the fish in the river and the people who use that water.
So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A chose a benefit of the river, but the question is about a disadvantage.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C confused an advantage with a disadvantage: easy irrigation is a benefit.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D chose the shade of the trees, which is not a disadvantage.

variantlar.maslahat: Where can the pesticides on the fields go after it rains?

kunikma: Know which foods are rich in a nutrient the body needs (a mineral, protein)
usul: Find which substance the question names and what it is needed for, then recall the food group that is rich in that substance.

variantlar.savol:
Calcium is a substance that makes bones and teeth strong.
Which of these foods contains the most calcium?

yechim.ovoz: Our bones and teeth need calcium.

yechim.doska: Rich in calcium: milk, yogurt, cheese, cottage cheese
yechim.ovoz: Milk and dairy products contain the most calcium.
Bread, apples, and salt contain very little calcium.
So the correct answer is milk.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought that filling food is also rich in calcium; bread mainly provides starch.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought “fruit is healthy, so it must have a lot of calcium too”; apples have little calcium.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused table salt with calcium because salt is a mineral; salt is sodium chloride.

variantlar.maslahat: Think of which drink, and the foods made from it (yogurt, cheese), are good for bones.

variantlar.savol:
Protein is needed for our body to grow and for our muscles to be strong.
Which of these contains the most protein?

yechim.ovoz: Our body needs protein to grow and to build muscles.

yechim.doska: Rich in protein: eggs, meat, fish, chickpeas, mung beans
yechim.ovoz: Eggs, meat, fish, chickpeas, and mung beans are rich in protein.

yechim.doska: Sugar — carbohydrate, butter — fat, apple — vitamins
yechim.ovoz: Sugar is mostly carbohydrate, butter is mostly fat, and apples contain vitamins.
So the chicken egg contains the most protein.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought any food that gives energy is protein; sugar is a carbohydrate.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B relied on the idea that “fruit is healthy”; apples contain very little protein.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought butter is rich in protein because it is made from milk; it is mostly fat.

variantlar.maslahat: Think of which animal product people eat more of to help their muscles grow.

kunikma: Know how an animal's body structure (a bird's feet) is adapted to its habitat and way of life
usul: Find where the bird lives and what it does (swims, catches prey, walks on the ground), then choose the foot structure that suits that job best.

variantlar.savol: A bird lives on Lake Aydarkul and spends a lot of time swimming in the water. What are its feet most likely to look like?
javoblar: Long toes with sharp, hooked claws
A thin web of skin between the toes
Two toes pointing forward and two pointing backward
Short toes with blunt claws, good for scratching the ground

yechim.ovoz: This bird spends much of its time swimming in the water.

yechim.doska: For swimming: webs between the toes
yechim.ovoz: The web between the toes pushes the water like a paddle.
Ducks and geese have feet like this.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) A thin web of skin between the toes
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A picked the feet of a bird of prey (an eagle); hooked claws are for catching prey.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C picked the feet of a tree-climbing bird (a woodpecker).
xatolar.3: A student who chose D picked the feet of a ground-walking bird such as a chicken; they are not suited for swimming.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about how a foot should be shaped like a paddle to push water well.

variantlar.savol:
An eagle lives in the mountains. It grips mice and rabbits tightly with its feet.
What are the eagle's feet most likely to look like?
javoblar: A thin web of skin between the toes
Short toes with blunt claws, good for scratching the ground
Very long, thin legs with spread-out toes

yechim.doska: An eagle catches prey with its feet
yechim.ovoz: An eagle grabs its prey with its feet.
Sharp, curved claws keep the prey from escaping.

yechim.doska: Web — swimming, blunt claws — scratching the ground
yechim.ovoz: Webbed feet are for swimming, and blunt claws are for scratching the ground.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) Large, sharp, hooked claws
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A picked the feet of a swimming bird (a duck).
xatolar.1: A student who chose B picked the feet of a bird like a chicken that scratches the ground for grain.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C picked the feet of a bird that wades in shallow water (a stork, a crane).

variantlar.maslahat: Think about what kind of claws are needed to hold on tightly to an animal that is trying to escape.

kunikma: Know practical ways not to waste fresh water (turning off the tap, stopping drips)
usul: For each option, check whether water flows away for nothing; choose the option in which water is used only when it is needed.

variantlar.savol:
In many parts of the world, including Uzbekistan, there is not enough drinking water.
Which habit helps save water?
javoblar: Leaving the tap running while brushing your teeth
Turning off the tap while brushing your teeth
Washing dishes under running water for a long time
Washing the yard with a hose every day

yechim.doska: Saving water = no water running for nothing
yechim.ovoz: Saving water means not letting it run for nothing.

yechim.doska: A, C, D — a lot of water runs away
yechim.ovoz: A running tap, long washing, and washing the yard every day waste a lot of water.

yechim.doska: B — water runs only when needed
yechim.ovoz: If the tap is turned off, water is used only for rinsing your mouth.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) Turning off the tap while brushing your teeth
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A did not read the question to the end; water from a running tap is wasted.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought “clean dishes are important,” but running water wastes a lot.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused cleanliness with saving water; washing with a hose every day uses a lot of water.

variantlar.maslahat: Find the situation in which water runs away without anyone needing it.

variantlar.savol:
The kitchen tap dripped all night.
What is the best thing to do to save water?
javoblar: Put a bucket under the tap and pour the water out in the morning
Do nothing, because a drip is very little water
Turn the tap on fully once a day

yechim.doska: Drop + drop + … = a lot of water
yechim.ovoz: Each drop is small, but in one day they add up to buckets of water.
The water is dripping because the tap is broken.
If we have the tap repaired, no water is wasted at all.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) Have the tap repaired
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought collecting the water is enough, but pouring the collected water away is also a waste.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B did not consider that small drops add up to a large amount over a long time.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought turning on the tap solves the problem; it lets even more water run.

variantlar.maslahat: Find the action that removes the cause of the dripping.

kunikma: Know another practical way to save water (reusing water, water-saving irrigation)
usul: For each option, compare whether the water is used once and wasted, or used a second time for something useful (or less of it is used).

variantlar.savol:
Nilufar wants to save water. She is looking for a way to reuse water.
In which activity is water reused and saved?
javoblar: Watering the base of a tree with water used to wash fruit
Filling the bathtub, bathing, and pouring the water out right away
Drinking water from the street ditch without boiling it
Washing the car with lots of water every day

yechim.doska: Reusing = using water a second time
yechim.ovoz: Reusing means using water again after it has been used once.

yechim.doska: A: water from washing fruit → to the tree
yechim.ovoz: Water used to wash fruit is clean, so it can be poured on a tree.

yechim.doska: B, D — waste; C — dangerous to health
yechim.ovoz: Pouring out bath water and washing the car every day are wasteful, and drinking ditch water is dangerous.

yechim.doska: Answer: A) Watering the base of a tree with water used to wash fruit
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B picked bathing as a useful activity, but the water is poured away without being reused.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought using ditch water saves water; unboiled water can cause disease.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused cleanliness with saving water.

variantlar.maslahat: Find the option in which water that has been used once is useful again.

variantlar.savol:
Jasur's grandfather waters the trees in the garden.
Which method uses the least water?
javoblar: Watering with a hose during the day, in the scorching heat
Flooding the whole garden with water
Wetting the paths and walls as well
Drip watering at the base of each plant

yechim.doska: The plant's roots need the water
yechim.ovoz: A plant takes in water through its roots.

yechim.doska: Drip watering: water goes only to the roots
yechim.ovoz: With drip watering, the water falls right at the roots.

yechim.doska: In the heat, by flooding, on walls — water evaporates or is wasted
yechim.ovoz: With the other methods, most of the water evaporates or runs off to places where it is not needed.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) Drip watering at the base of each plant
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A did not consider that water evaporates quickly in the heat.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought “more water means a better harvest”; flooding wastes a lot of water.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C did not think about the fact that a plant needs water only at its roots.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about which method puts water only where the plant needs it.

kunikma: Know that the size of the pupil changes with the amount of light, and draw a conclusion from a picture about the conditions outside
usul: Compare the size of the pupils in the pictures: in bright light the pupil gets smaller, in the dark it gets larger; temperature does not change the pupil in this way.

variantlar.savol:
The pictures show Jasur's eyes in two different places.
Which statement is correct?

javoblar: Picture 1 was taken in a dark room, and Picture 2 in a sunny yard
Picture 1 was taken in a sunny yard, and Picture 2 in a dark room
It was warmer where Picture 1 was taken
It was warmer where Picture 2 was taken

yechim.doska: Bright → small pupil; dark → large pupil
yechim.ovoz: When a lot of light enters the eye, the pupil gets smaller; in the dark it gets larger.
In the first picture the pupil is large, so that place is dark.
In the second picture the pupil is small, so that place is bright.

yechim.doska: Answer: A) Picture 1 was taken in a dark room, and Picture 2 in a sunny yard
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B remembered the rule backward: they thought the pupil gets larger in bright light.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought the pupil changes with heat; it is light that changes it.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D also linked the pupil to temperature; temperature does not affect the size of the pupil.

variantlar.maslahat: The pupil controls how much light enters the eye. In which picture is it blocking more light?

variantlar.savol:
Malika is sitting in a room. At first her eye looked like Picture 1; after a while it looked like Picture 2.
What could have changed in the room?

kunikma: Know that animals come only from parents of their own kind (from eggs), and apply the life cycle to a new situation

They formed from dust in the air

kunikma: Know that heat moves from a hot object to a cold object, and predict how the temperatures of two objects will change

javoblar: The water cools down, and the yogurt warms up
The water warms up, and the yogurt cools down
The water temperature does not change, and the yogurt warms up

yechim.ovoz: The water in the bowl is warm, and the yogurt is cold.
Heat always moves from the warmer object to the colder object.

yechim.doska: Water gives off heat — cools down; yogurt takes in heat — warms up
yechim.ovoz: The water gives off heat and cools down, and the yogurt takes in heat and warms up.

yechim.doska: Answer: A) The water cools down, and the yogurt warms up

The water warms up, and the spoon cools down

Heat moves from the hot spoon to the cold water.

yechim.doska: The spoon cools down, the water warms up
yechim.ovoz: The spoon gives off heat and cools down, and the water takes in heat and warms up.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about what happens to the object that gives off heat and to the object that takes in heat.

kunikma: Explain that day and night happen because the Earth rotates on its axis

javoblar: The Sun moves around the Earth
The Earth moves around the Sun
The Earth rotates on its axis

yechim.doska: Earth rotates on its axis once = 1 day
yechim.ovoz: The Earth rotates on its axis once every 24 hours.

yechim.doska: Side facing the Sun — day, opposite side — night
yechim.ovoz: It is day on the side of the Earth facing the Sun and night on the opposite side.
The Earth's trip around the Sun takes a year; it does not cause day and night.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) The Earth rotates on its axis
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought the Sun moves around the Earth because it “travels” across the sky.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B confused the Earth's two motions; a trip around the Sun takes one year.

variantlar.maslahat: Recall the motion of the Earth that takes place in one day.

The Earth moves around the Sun
The Sun rotates on its axis
The Earth rotates on its axis

yechim.ovoz: It looks to us as if the Sun is moving across the sky.

yechim.doska: In fact, the Earth rotates on its axis

yechim.doska: We are on the side facing the Sun — day; on the opposite side — night
yechim.ovoz: When we turn to the side facing the Sun, it is day; when we turn to the opposite side, it is night.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) The Earth rotates on its axis
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is D.

kunikma: Read thermometers and compare temperatures (find the hottest or coldest water)

yechim.ovoz: There is an arrow from the lizard to the snake. So the snake hunts the lizard.

yechim.doska: grass is a plant; it cannot be a predator
yechim.ovoz: Grass does not eat anything; it makes its own food. That is why B is wrong.
The correct pair is option D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A understood the direction of the arrow backward: in fact, the snake eats the lizard, not the other way around.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought a plant can also be a predator; grass does not eat animals, it is only food.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C found the right pair but swapped their roles: the eagle eats the snake.

variantlar.maslahat: Notice which animal the arrow points to — that animal is the one eating.

variantlar.savol:
The diagram shows a food chain in and around a lake. The arrows show what is food for what.
Which pair correctly shows a predator and its prey?

yechim.doska: algae → mosquito larva → small fish → pike → pelican
yechim.ovoz: Let's read the chain: the larva eats algae, the small fish eats the larva, the pike eats the small fish, and the pelican eats the pike.
There is an arrow from the larva to the small fish. So the small fish eats the larva: it is the predator, and the larva is the prey.
There is no arrow directly between the pelican and the algae; the pelican does not eat algae.

yechim.doska: Answer: A) small fish (predator) – mosquito larva (prey)
yechim.ovoz: The correct pair is option A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B read the arrow backward: in fact, the pelican eats the pike.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought algae can also be a predator; algae are plants, and they do not eat anything.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D connected the start and the end of the chain; the pelican does not eat algae, and there is no arrow between them.

variantlar.maslahat: A predator and its prey are next to each other in the chain and are joined by a single arrow.

kunikma: Know that condensation is the change of a substance from a gas (water vapor) into a liquid
usul: Recall the names of the changes of state: melting (solid → liquid), freezing (liquid → solid), evaporation (liquid → gas), condensation (gas → liquid).

variantlar.savol: Which of these correctly describes condensation?
javoblar: a liquid changing into a gas
a gas changing into a liquid
a liquid changing into a solid
a solid changing into a liquid

yechim.doska: melting: solid → liquid;  freezing: liquid → solid
yechim.ovoz: First, let's recall the processes we know: ice melts, and water freezes.
When water is heated, it turns into vapor. This is evaporation.
When vapor cools, it turns back into drops of water. This is condensation.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) a gas changing into a liquid
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A confused condensation with evaporation — they are opposite processes.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C confused condensation with freezing.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused condensation with melting.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember what appears on a cold mirror when you breathe “haaa” onto it.

variantlar.savol: What is it called when water vapor cools and turns into drops of water?

yechim.doska: water vapor — gas,  water drop — liquid
yechim.ovoz: Water vapor is a gas, and the drops are a liquid.
So here a gas is changing into a liquid.
A gas changing into a liquid is called condensation.
The correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A picked the opposite process: in evaporation, liquid water turns into vapor.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B picked melting, but in melting a solid (for example, ice) turns into a liquid.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D picked freezing, but in freezing liquid water turns into ice.

variantlar.maslahat: First find which state the water is changing from and which state it is changing to.

kunikma: Understand that a predator's long, sharp canine teeth are used to grab, pierce, and tear prey, and apply this knowledge to a new animal
usul: Look at the shape of the tooth: a long canine with a sharp point is not for chewing; it is adapted to sink into prey, hold it tightly, and tear meat.

variantlar.savol:
A wolf eats meat. At the front of its mouth it has four long, sharp canine teeth.
What does the wolf use its canine teeth for?
javoblar: to grind and chew food well
to hold prey tightly, pierce its body, and tear its meat
to cut grass off at the bottom

yechim.doska: Canine: long, with a sharp point
yechim.ovoz: First, let's look at the shape of the tooth: it is long with a sharp tip, just like the tip of a knife.

yechim.doska: Sharp tip → pierces, long → holds tightly
yechim.ovoz: The sharp tip pierces the prey's skin, and the length holds the prey so it cannot escape.

yechim.doska: Chewing — the job of flat teeth
yechim.ovoz: Grinding food needs wide, flat teeth, which are at the back of the mouth.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) to hold, pierce, and tear prey
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought all teeth are for chewing; the flat teeth at the back of the mouth grind food.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C remembered the teeth of plant-eating animals; but a wolf does not eat grass — it is a predator.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D did not consider the link between the shape of a tooth and what the animal eats; teeth are not needed for drinking water.

variantlar.maslahat: A long, sharp tooth is better suited to something other than chewing — picture a predator catching its prey.

variantlar.savol:
The snow leopard lives in the high mountains of Uzbekistan and hunts mountain goats. It has long, sharp canine teeth in its mouth.
What does the snow leopard use its canine teeth for?
javoblar: to crush bones into small pieces
to dig in the snow and make a den
to hold on to prey, sink its teeth into it, and tear its meat

yechim.ovoz: The snow leopard hunts mountain goats, so it is a predator.
Its canine teeth are long with sharp points.

yechim.doska: Sharp tip → sinks in;  long → holds
yechim.ovoz: A tooth like this sinks deep into the prey and keeps it from escaping, and then it helps tear the meat.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) to hold prey, sink teeth in, and tear
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A confused canine teeth with crushing teeth; the flat teeth at the back of the mouth crush and grind.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B remembered the front teeth of rodents; the snow leopard does not eat bark.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C looked for the main job of the teeth in something other than eating; cats do not dig dens with their teeth.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about what the animal eats and the shape of its teeth together.

kunikma: Understand that the large front cutting teeth of rodents are used to gnaw hard food into small pieces, and apply this to a new animal
usul: The front teeth of rodents have sharp edges like a chisel: they do not grind and chew food, but gnaw hard things little by little, biting off small pieces.

variantlar.savol:
A field mouse eats wheat grains, hard seeds, and plant stems. At the front of its mouth it has large cutting teeth with sharp edges.
What does the field mouse use these front teeth for?
javoblar: to hold prey and tear its meat
to grind and chew food inside its mouth
to gnaw hard grains and seeds into small pieces

yechim.ovoz: A field mouse eats grains, seeds, and stems. These are hard foods.

yechim.doska: Front teeth: a sharp edge like a chisel
yechim.ovoz: Its front teeth are like a chisel: the edge is sharp and cuts.

yechim.doska: Gnawing = biting off a hard thing little by little
yechim.ovoz: With these teeth, the mouse gnaws through the hard husk of a grain and breaks it into small pieces.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) to gnaw hard grains and seeds
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A confused cutting teeth with the canine teeth of predators; a field mouse does not hunt prey.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought the front teeth are chewing teeth; the flat teeth at the back of the mouth grind and chew.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D did not see the link between the shape of a tooth and the type of food; teeth are not needed for drinking water.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about which part of the mouth the front teeth are in and how they look like a chisel.

variantlar.savol:
The porcupine (an animal a bit like a hedgehog whose body is covered with long quills) belongs to the rodent group. It eats tree bark, hard roots, and the rinds of melons and other field crops. It has large cutting teeth at the front of its mouth.
What does the porcupine use these front teeth for?
javoblar: to gnaw and bite off hard bark and roots
to defend itself from enemies and drive them away
to grind and crush food inside its mouth
to grab prey and kill it

yechim.ovoz: The porcupine eats bark, roots, and hard rinds. These are very hard foods.
The edges of its cutting teeth are sharp, just like a chisel.

yechim.doska: Gnawing: biting off hard food little by little
yechim.ovoz: With these teeth, the porcupine gnaws hard bark and bites it off piece by piece.

yechim.doska: Defense — the job of the quills
yechim.ovoz: The porcupine defends itself with the quills on its body, not with its teeth.

yechim.doska: Answer: A) to gnaw hard bark and roots
yechim.ovoz: The correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B confused the porcupine's means of defense — its quills — with its teeth.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought the front teeth are chewing teeth; the flat teeth at the back of the mouth crush food.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused cutting teeth with a predator's canine teeth; the porcupine eats plants.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember what the porcupine eats, and think about how hard food can be eaten with front teeth.

kunikma: Identify the type of energy that household appliances need to work — electrical energy
usul: Find what the appliances have in common: they all connect to an outlet through a cord and plug, so they all run on the same kind of energy.

variantlar.savol:
A refrigerator, a vacuum cleaner, and a television all connect to an outlet through a cord.
What kind of energy do these appliances run on? Write one or two words.
variantlar.javob: electricity|electrical energy|electric energy|electric current|current|electric power|electrical power|by electricity|with electricity

yechim.ovoz: All three appliances connect to an outlet through their cords.
Electric current flows from the outlet to the appliance.

yechim.doska: Unplugged from the outlet → does not work
yechim.ovoz: If we pull the plug out of the outlet, none of them will work.
So these appliances run on electrical energy.

xatolar.umumiy: Some students write what the appliance does: “cold” for the refrigerator, “light” or “sound” for the television. But the question asks what makes the appliance work — all three run on electrical energy.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about what happens if we unplug the appliances from the outlet.

variantlar.savol:
An electric kettle, a hair dryer, and a washing machine need to be plugged into an outlet to work.
What kind of energy do these appliances use? Write one or two words.
variantlar.javob: electricity|electrical energy|electric energy|electric current|current|electric power|electrical power|by electricity|with electricity

yechim.doska: Kettle, hair dryer, washing machine → outlet
yechim.ovoz: All three appliances plug into an outlet.
The outlet gives them electrical energy.
The kettle changes electrical energy into heat, but the energy that runs it is electrical.
So these appliances use electrical energy.

xatolar.umumiy: Many students write “heat energy” because the kettle heats water. Heat is the result; the appliance runs on electrical energy that comes from the outlet.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember what all three appliances are connected to.

kunikma: Draw conclusions from pairwise comparisons on a balance scale and order objects by weight
usul: In each weighing, the cube in the pan that went down is heavier. Write the results as “heavy > light” and combine them into one row.

variantlar.savol:
Jasur has four cubes made of different materials: 1, 2, 3, and 4. He put two cubes on a balance scale at a time and weighed them three times. The results are shown in the picture.
What can you conclude about Cube 3?

xatolar.3: A student who chose D misread Weighing 3 and took Cube 2 as heavier than Cube 1.

Malika has four cubes made of different materials: 1, 2, 3, and 4. She put two cubes on a balance scale at a time and weighed them three times. The results are shown in the picture.
What can you conclude about Cube 3?

kunikma: Understand that an object's weight depends not only on its size but also on the material it is made of, and give a reasoned argument against a wrong idea
usul: If you can find an example of an object that is large but light (or small but heavy), you can see that the idea “a bigger object is always heavier” is wrong.

variantlar.savol:
The teacher placed three objects on the table in order of size, from largest to smallest: a large pillow stuffed with cotton, a brick, and an apple.
Sardor said, “A bigger object is always heavier.”
Which statement is correct?
javoblar: Sardor is right: the pillow is the biggest, so it is the heaviest.
Sardor is not right: the smallest object is always the heaviest.
Sardor is right: the apple is the smallest, so it is the lightest, and this proves his idea.
Sardor is not right: the pillow is lighter than the brick even though it is bigger, because weight also depends on the material an object is made of.

yechim.ovoz: The objects are arranged in this order by size.

yechim.doska: Inside the pillow — cotton and a lot of air
yechim.ovoz: The pillow is big, but it is filled with light cotton and air.
The brick is smaller than the pillow, but if we pick it up, it is much heavier.

yechim.doska: Weight also depends on the material
yechim.ovoz: So a big object is not always heavy — Sardor's idea is wrong.
The correct explanation is option D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought size and weight are the same thing and did not consider what the pillow is made of.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B correctly disagreed with Sardor but made up a new wrong rule: the apple is the smallest, but it is not the heaviest.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C treated one example that fits as proof of the whole rule and did not compare the pillow with the brick.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about which would be heavier if you picked up the pillow and the brick.

variantlar.savol:
Nilufar placed three objects on the table in order of size, from largest to smallest: a large piece of foam plastic, a stone, and a cherry.
Nilufar's younger brother said, “A bigger object is always heavier.”
Which statement is correct?
javoblar: Her brother is not right: the stone is heavier than the foam even though it is smaller, because an object's weight also depends on the material it is made of.
Her brother is right: the foam is the biggest, so it is the heaviest.
Her brother is not right: there is never any connection between size and weight.
Her brother is right: the cherry is the smallest and the lightest, and this proves his idea.

yechim.ovoz: The objects are arranged in this order by size.

yechim.doska: Foam plastic has many tiny air bubbles inside
yechim.ovoz: The foam is big but very light, because it is full of air bubbles.
The stone is smaller than the foam, but much heavier.

yechim.doska: Weight also depends on the material
yechim.ovoz: So a big object is not always heavy, and her brother's idea is wrong.
The correct explanation is option A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought size and weight are the same thing and did not consider that foam is a very light material.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C went too far: among objects made of the same material, the bigger one is heavier, so it is not true that there is no connection at all.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D treated one example that fits as proof of the rule and did not compare the foam with the stone.

variantlar.maslahat: Imagine which would be heavier if you picked up the foam and the stone.

kunikma: Know that the Earth receives light and heat energy from the Sun
usul: During the day the Sun lights up and warms everything around. Think of these two things, and name the type of energy that comes from the Sun.

variantlar.savol:
The Sun gives the Earth light. In summer, the sand in the Kyzylkum Desert gets very hot during the day.
Besides light, what other energy does the Sun give the Earth? Write one or two words.
variantlar.javob: heat|heat energy|thermal energy|warmth|heat from the Sun|solar heat|thermal

yechim.ovoz: The Sun lights up the Earth — this is light energy. But the question asks about another kind of energy.

yechim.doska: The sand heats up during the day
yechim.ovoz: When the Sun comes out, the sand heats up, and when we stand in the sun, our body gets warm.
The energy that warms things is heat energy.
So the Sun also gives the Earth heat energy.

xatolar.umumiy: Some students write “light,” but that is already given in the question. Others write “solar energy” — that is the source of the energy, and its type is heat.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember what happens to things that stand in the sun during the day.

variantlar.savol:
Plant leaves get energy from the Sun to make food. That is why we put a houseplant next to the window.
What kind of energy do plant leaves get from the Sun? Write one or two words.
variantlar.javob: light|light energy|sunlight|light from the Sun|solar light|rays|sunshine|light rays

yechim.ovoz: We put the flower next to the window, because sunlight falls there.
The leaf makes food with the help of sunlight. This is called photosynthesis.

yechim.doska: In the dark, a plant wilts
yechim.ovoz: If it stays in a dark room for a long time, the plant cannot make food and wilts.
So leaves get light energy from the Sun.

xatolar.umumiy: Some students write “water” or “air” — plants need these, but they do not come from the Sun and are not types of energy. Writing “the Sun” is not enough either: you need to name the type of energy (light).

variantlar.maslahat: Think about why we put a flower next to the window and not in a dark corner.

kunikma: Apply the ideas that light travels in straight lines and that a shadow forms on the side of an object opposite the light source
usul: Draw a straight line from the light source through the object: the shadow lies along the continuation of this line, on the side of the object away from the source.

variantlar.savol:
In a dark room, Aziz placed a burning candle and a bowl on a table. The picture shows the table from above.
Along which line will the bowl's shadow fall?

yechim.ovoz: The candlelight spreads in all directions in straight lines.
The bowl blocks the light, so the shadow forms on the side of the bowl opposite the candle.

yechim.doska: Candle top right → shadow bottom left
yechim.ovoz: The candle is in the top right corner, so the shadow falls toward the bottom left — this is line C.
The correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A knew the shadow is opposite the light but did not continue the straight line and chose a line off to the side.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought the shadow forms on the side of the light source — in fact, that side is lit up.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D considered only the “downward” direction but reversed left and right.

variantlar.maslahat: Draw a straight line from the candle through the bowl and continue it past the bowl.

In the evening the Sun is low, near the horizon. There is an upright pole in the middle of a field. The picture shows the field from above, and the side the Sun is on is marked.

yechim.ovoz: Sunlight travels in a straight line, and the pole blocks it.

yechim.doska: Shadow — on the side opposite the Sun
yechim.ovoz: That is why the shadow falls on the side of the pole away from the Sun.

yechim.doska: Sun on the left → shadow on the right
yechim.ovoz: The Sun is on the left, so the shadow stretches to the right — this is line A.
The correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought the shadow falls toward the Sun — in fact, that side is lit up.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C did not consider that the shadow is opposite the light source and chose a line off to the side.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D also did not consider that the shadow lies along the continuation of the Sun–pole line.

kunikma: Know that the direction a river flows depends on the slope of the land — water flows from high to low
usul: Because of gravity, water always flows from higher ground to lower ground. That is why the slope of the land determines the direction of flow.

variantlar.savol: What does the direction a river flows depend on?
javoblar: the kind of stones on the riverbed
the position of the Sun in the sky

yechim.doska: Water flows from high to low
yechim.ovoz: Think of water coming down a mountain or flowing along a sloping gutter: water always flows downhill.
Water flows in the direction in which the land gets lower.

yechim.doska: Width, stones → affect the speed of flow, not its direction
yechim.ovoz: The width of a river or the stones on its bed can slow the water down, but they do not determine its direction.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) the slope of the land
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A linked the size of the river to the direction of flow; both wide and narrow rivers flow downhill.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought the stones on the bed control the flow; they can slow the water, but they do not determine its direction.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C linked the movement of the Sun to the river's flow; the Sun changes position during the day, but a river always flows the same way.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember which way water flows from a hill.

variantlar.savol:
The Chirchik River begins in the high mountains and flows toward the plain below.
Why does the river flow in exactly this direction?
javoblar: Because water always flows from higher ground to lower ground.
Because river water always flows north.
Because the wind pushes the water toward the plain.
Because there is sand and gravel on the riverbed.

yechim.ovoz: The Chirchik River begins in the high mountains, and the plain is much lower.

yechim.doska: Water flows from high to low
yechim.ovoz: Water always flows from higher ground toward lower ground.

yechim.doska: The slope of the land determines the direction
yechim.ovoz: That is why the river flows from the mountains toward the plain.
The correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought rivers flow toward a particular compass direction; rivers flow in different directions, but always downhill.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought the wind causes the flow; wind makes waves, but it does not determine the river's direction.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought things on the riverbed cause the flow; sand and gravel do not determine the direction of the water.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about which is higher — the mountains or the plain.

kunikma: Know that sea and ocean water is salty, so it must be desalinated before drinking
usul: Sort natural bodies of water into fresh water (rivers, springs, glacier water) and salt water (seas, oceans); only salt water needs desalination.

variantlar.savol: Which water must have most of its salt removed before you can drink it?

yechim.ovoz: Mountain spring water, glacier water, and river water are fresh water; they contain very little salt.
Ocean water is very salty; it contains a lot of salt.

yechim.doska: Salt water is not safe to drink
yechim.ovoz: You cannot drink salt water; first the salt must be removed.
So the correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought spring water is salty because it comes from underground; mountain spring water is usually fresh.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B did not know how glacier water forms; a glacier forms from snow, and its water is fresh.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought a river is salty because it flows into the sea; river water is fresh water.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember which body of water tastes salty.

variantlar.savol:
In some hot countries there is little fresh water. There, much of the drinking water is produced at desalination plants.
Where do these plants usually get their water from?

yechim.ovoz: A desalination plant removes the salt from water.
The water with a lot of salt is sea and ocean water.
Rain, river, and spring water are fresh; they do not need to be desalinated.
The correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought rainwater is salty; rain forms from evaporated water and is fresh.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought river water is salty; river water is fresh and only needs to be cleaned.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D did not pay attention to the words “produced at plants”; mountain spring water is fresh and does not need to be desalinated.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about what the plant removes from the water and where water like that is plentiful.

kunikma: Know how animals develop: the young of some look like the adults, while others (insects, frogs) completely change their shape as they develop
usul: Recall what each animal looks like when it is young: if a caterpillar, larva, or tadpole hatches from the egg, it does not look like the adult; the young of mammals look like small copies of the adults.

variantlar.savol: The young of which of these animals looks most like the adult?

yechim.doska: Silk moth: egg → caterpillar → pupa → moth
yechim.ovoz: A caterpillar hatches from the silk moth's egg, and it looks nothing like a moth.
A young frog is a tadpole. It looks like a fish: it has no legs and has a tail.
A mosquito larva lives in water and does not look like the adult.
A lamb, though, looks just like a little sheep: the same legs, wool, and head.
So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A did not consider that the silkworm and the moth are the same animal but look very different.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B forgot that a young frog is a tadpole and does not look like the adult.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D did not know that a mosquito larva lives in water and does not look like the adult.

variantlar.maslahat: Picture what the young of each animal looks like.

variantlar.savol: The young of which of these animals looks most like the adult?

yechim.doska: Dragonfly: its larva lives in water and has no wings
yechim.ovoz: A dragonfly larva lives under water and has no wings.
A legless maggot hatches from a housefly's egg.

yechim.doska: Cabbage butterfly: egg → caterpillar → pupa → butterfly
yechim.ovoz: A young butterfly is a caterpillar, and it does not look like a butterfly.
A camel calf, however, looks like a little camel from the moment it is born.
The correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B did not know that a dragonfly larva lives in water and has no wings.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C did not consider that a young housefly is a legless maggot.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D forgot that a young butterfly is a caterpillar and does not look like the adult.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about which animal's young is not a caterpillar or a larva.

kunikma: Understand that animals need a male and a female to reproduce, and reason that a species will die out if only animals of one sex are left
usul: For these kinds of animals, both a male and a female of the same species are needed for young to be born. If one of them is missing, there will be no new generation, and the remaining animals will grow old and die.

variantlar.savol:
The goitered gazelle is a rare animal listed in Uzbekistan's Red Book. Suppose that only female gazelles were left in the world, and there were no male gazelles at all.
What is most likely to happen next?
javoblar: The female gazelles will mate with goats or rams and give birth to young gazelles.
The female gazelles will give birth only to female young.
No new gazelles will be born, and the gazelles will die out.
The female gazelles will mate with each other and give birth to new gazelles.

yechim.doska: For young: male + female (of the same species)
yechim.ovoz: For a young gazelle to be born, both a male gazelle and a female gazelle are needed.
Since there are no male gazelles left, no new young will be born.

yechim.doska: Another species → no gazelle is born
yechim.ovoz: A young gazelle cannot be born from a different animal.

yechim.doska: The rest grow old → the species dies out
yechim.ovoz: Over time, the gazelles that are left grow old and die, and as a result the gazelles die out.
The correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought any two animals can have young; young gazelles are born only from gazelles.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought a female can have young by herself without a male; this does not happen in gazelles.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D did not consider that a male and a female are needed to reproduce.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about who is needed for a young gazelle to be born.

variantlar.savol:
The Bukhara deer is a rare animal protected in the Zarafshan Nature Reserve. Suppose that only male Bukhara deer were left in the world, and there were no females at all.
What is most likely to happen next?
javoblar: No new deer will be born, and the Bukhara deer will die out.
The male deer will mate with cows and produce young Bukhara deer.
The male deer will mate with each other and produce new deer.
The male deer will produce only male young.

yechim.doska: For young: male + female (of the same species)
yechim.ovoz: For a fawn to be born, both a male deer and a female deer are needed.
The female deer gives birth to the fawn. Since there are no females left, no new deer will be born.

yechim.doska: The rest grow old → the species dies out
yechim.ovoz: When the male deer grow old and die, these deer will die out.
The correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought young of one species can be born from animals of different species; young Bukhara deer are born only from Bukhara deer.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C did not consider that a male and a female are needed to reproduce.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought a male animal can produce young by himself; only females give birth.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember who gives birth to a fawn.

kunikma: Identify animals by their main features (internal or external skeleton, number of legs, feeding young with milk, soft body) and match them to descriptions
usul: Check each description separately: if it feeds its young with milk, it is a mammal; an external skeleton and three pairs (6) of legs, an insect; if it has neither a skeleton nor a hard shell, it is a soft-bodied animal.

yechim.ovoz: An animal that feeds its young with milk is a mammal. Here it is the camel. The lizard lays eggs.
The bee is an insect: its body is covered with a hard outer covering, and it has six legs.
The earthworm has no bones and no shell; its body is soft.
Let's write all three in order.
The correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought any animal with an internal skeleton feeds its young with milk; the lizard is a reptile, and it lays eggs.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B swapped descriptions 2 and 3: the earthworm has no legs and no skeleton.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought the lizard has an external skeleton because its skin has hard scales; in fact, the lizard has an internal skeleton and four legs.

variantlar.maslahat: Find the most important feature in each description: milk, six legs, soft body.

yechim.ovoz: Even though the bat flies, it is a mammal: it feeds its young with milk. The swallow is a bird, and it lays eggs.
The grasshopper is an insect; it has six legs. The spider has eight legs.
The leech has no bones and no shell; its body is soft.
Let's write all three in order.
The correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A mixed up the flying animals: the swallow is a bird, and it does not feed its young with milk.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought the spider is an insect; the spider has four pairs of legs (8).
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought the spider has a soft body; the spider also has a hard external skeleton.

variantlar.maslahat: Count the legs: remember how many legs an insect has.

kunikma: Know how the degree of grinding (particle size) of a substance affects how fast it dissolves in water, and choose the correct conclusion and its reason
usul: Find which substance is in smaller pieces: small particles touch the water on more sides, so they dissolve faster. Check both the answer and the reason.

variantlar.savol:
Malika poured the same amount of warm water into two identical glasses. She put one sugar cube in Glass 1 and the same weight of granulated sugar in Glass 2, and stirred both in the same way (see the picture).
Which statement is correct, and why?

javoblar: The sugar cube dissolves faster, because it is heavier and sinks into the water faster.
Both dissolve in the same time, because they have the same weight.
The granulated sugar dissolves faster, because it is made of tiny grains and more of it touches the water.
The granulated sugar dissolves faster, because granulated sugar is sweeter than a sugar cube.

yechim.ovoz: In both glasses the water, the amount of sugar, and the stirring are the same. Only one thing is different.

yechim.doska: Difference: cube — large, granulated sugar — tiny grains
yechim.ovoz: The difference is the size of the sugar: one is a single large cube, and the other is tiny grains.

yechim.doska: Tiny grains → touch more water → dissolve fast
yechim.ovoz: The water surrounds the tiny grains on all sides, so they dissolve faster.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) The granulated sugar dissolves faster
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is C: the granulated sugar dissolves faster because it is in tiny grains.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought a large, heavy piece dissolves faster; in fact, only the surface of a large piece touches the water, and the inside stays undissolved for a long time.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B looked only at the weight and did not consider that the size of the pieces affects how fast they dissolve.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D correctly knew that the granulated sugar dissolves faster but gave the wrong reason: sweetness does not determine how fast something dissolves.

variantlar.maslahat: Find what is the same and what is different in the two glasses.

variantlar.savol:
Jasur poured the same amount of cold water into two identical glasses. He put a spoonful of fine table salt in Glass 1 and a large lump of rock salt of the same weight in Glass 2, and stirred both in the same way (see the picture).
Which statement is correct, and why?
variantlar.rasm: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 360 230"><g font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14"><text x="100" y="20" text-anchor="middle">Fine salt</text><ellipse cx="100" cy="58" rx="24" ry="8" fill="none" stroke="#222"/><line x1="124" y1="58" x2="150" y2="44" stroke="#222" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="88" cy="55" r="1.8" fill="#222"/><circle cx="94" cy="51" r="1.8" fill="#222"/><circle cx="100" cy="54" r="1.8" fill="#222"/><circle cx="106" cy="50" r="1.8" fill="#222"/><circle cx="112" cy="55" r="1.8" fill="#222"/><circle cx="97" cy="47" r="1.8" fill="#222"/><circle cx="104" cy="46" r="1.8" fill="#222"/><circle cx="91" cy="58" r="1.8" fill="#222"/><circle cx="109" cy="58" r="1.8" fill="#222"/><circle cx="100" cy="58" r="1.8" fill="#222"/><path d="M50 80 L56 200 Q100 212 144 200 L150 80" fill="none" stroke="#222" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M52 110 Q100 118 148 110 L144 200 Q100 212 56 200 Z" fill="#e8f1ff" stroke="none"/><path d="M50 80 L56 200 Q100 212 144 200 L150 80" fill="none" stroke="#222" stroke-width="2"/><text x="100" y="226" text-anchor="middle">Glass 1</text><text x="260" y="20" text-anchor="middle">Rock salt</text><rect x="244" y="34" width="32" height="32" fill="#fde9c8" stroke="#222"/><line x1="244" y1="50" x2="276" y2="50" stroke="#222" stroke-width="0.6"/><line x1="260" y1="34" x2="260" y2="66" stroke="#222" stroke-width="0.6"/><path d="M210 80 L216 200 Q260 212 304 200 L310 80" fill="none" stroke="#222" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M212 110 Q260 118 308 110 L304 200 Q260 212 216 200 Z" fill="#e8f1ff" stroke="none"/><path d="M210 80 L216 200 Q260 212 304 200 L310 80" fill="none" stroke="#222" stroke-width="2"/><text x="260" y="226" text-anchor="middle">Glass 2</text></g></svg>
javoblar: The fine salt dissolves faster, because its particles are small and the water quickly surrounds them on all sides.
The rock salt dissolves faster, because it is large and takes up more of the water.
Both dissolve in the same time, because both are table salt.
The fine salt dissolves faster, because it looks whiter and lighter.

yechim.doska: Same type of salt, same weight, same water
yechim.ovoz: Both glasses have the same salt and the same water. The only difference is the size of the salt particles.

yechim.doska: Glass 1: tiny particles;  Glass 2: one large lump
yechim.ovoz: The salt in the first glass is fine, and in the second it is one large lump.

yechim.doska: Tiny particles → touch more water → dissolve fast
yechim.ovoz: Water touches each of the tiny particles, but only the outside of the large lump touches the water.

yechim.doska: Answer: A) The fine salt dissolves faster
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is A.

xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought that if the substance is the same, the dissolving time is the same too, and did not consider particle size.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D correctly found which dissolves faster but gave the wrong reason: color does not affect how fast something dissolves.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about which salt the water can touch in more places at the same time.

kunikma: Know that metals conduct heat well while wood and plastic conduct it poorly, and use this to explain an everyday event
usul: Think about which object is touching something hot and which material heat passes through more easily. Do not confuse conducting heat with conducting electricity.

variantlar.savol:
At a teahouse, Nilufar put an aluminum spoon and a plastic spoon into hot tea. A few minutes later, the handle of the aluminum spoon was hotter than the handle of the plastic spoon.
What is the reason for this?
javoblar: Aluminum is always hotter than plastic.
Aluminum conducts heat better than plastic.
Aluminum conducts electricity better than plastic.
The aluminum spoon heats the tea faster than the plastic spoon.

yechim.doska: Both spoons are in hot tea
yechim.ovoz: Both spoons are standing in the same hot tea.
Heat moves from the tea all the way to the handle of the spoon.

yechim.doska: Metal (aluminum) — conducts heat well; plastic — poorly
yechim.ovoz: Metal conducts heat well, and plastic conducts it poorly. That is why the aluminum handle heats up quickly.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) Aluminum conducts heat better
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought metal is hot by itself; in fact, at room temperature both spoons are equally warm.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C confused electric current with heat: there is no current here; the question is about heat.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D mixed up cause and effect: the spoon does not heat the tea; the tea heats the spoon.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about which way heat moves — from the tea to the spoon, or from the spoon to the tea.

variantlar.savol:
Many pots and pans have wooden handles. That way, holding the handle while cooking does not burn your hand.
Why is wood chosen for the handle?
javoblar: Wood is light, so the pot is easy to lift.
Wood conducts heat poorly, so the handle does not get hot.

yechim.doska: The pot heats up on the fire
yechim.ovoz: The pot is on the fire and gets very hot.
Heat tends to move from the pot into the handle.
Wood conducts heat poorly, so the handle does not get hot and your hand does not get burned.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) Wood conducts heat poorly
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A remembered that wood is light, but the question is about not burning your hand — and that has to do with heat.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B confused conducting electricity with conducting heat: it is heat, not electric current, that burns your hand.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought the handle affects the food; the handle does not touch the food — its job is to protect your hand from heat.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about what could burn your hand and how wood prevents it.

kunikma: Know events that show sunlight is made of different colors (a rainbow, a prism)
usul: Among the options, find the event in which white sunlight is seen split into several colors. Events that are only about light, shadows, or reflections do not show colors.

variantlar.savol: Which of these events shows that sunlight is made of different colors?
javoblar: A rainbow appearing in the sky when the sun comes out after rain
Seeing the Moon in the sky at night
Seeing our reflection in a mirror
A mulberry tree casting a shadow on the ground during the day

yechim.doska: Sunlight looks white, but it contains many colors
yechim.ovoz: Sunlight looks white to us, but in fact it is made of many colors.

yechim.doska: Raindrops split light into colors → rainbow
yechim.ovoz: When sunlight passes through raindrops, it splits into colors, and we see a rainbow.

yechim.doska: Moon, reflection, shadow — no splitting into colors
yechim.ovoz: In the other events, light does not split into colors.
So the correct answer is A, the rainbow.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B remembered that the Moon reflects sunlight, but the light does not split into colors when this happens.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C knew that a mirror reflects light, but an ordinary mirror does not split light into colors.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D linked shadows to light, but a shadow shows that light is blocked, not that it has colors.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember which event shows many colors at the same time.

variantlar.savol: Which of these shows that sunlight is made of different colors?
javoblar: Sunlight coming in through a window and lighting up a room
Seeing the reflection of a tree in the water of a ditch
Sunlight passing through a triangular glass prism and making a colored band on the wall
Snow melting in the sunlight in spring

yechim.ovoz: Even though sunlight looks white, it contains red, yellow, green, blue, and other colors.

yechim.doska: A prism splits light into colors → a colored band on the wall
yechim.ovoz: A glass prism splits light into colors, and a colored band like a rainbow appears on the wall.

yechim.doska: Lighting up, reflection, melting snow — no colors seen
yechim.ovoz: In the other events, light does not split into colors.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) A prism makes a colored band on the wall
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A confused light passing through glass with a prism: an ordinary flat windowpane does not split light into colors.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought a reflection in water is light splitting into colors; a reflection only shows light bouncing back.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D remembered that sunlight gives heat, but that is not about colors.

variantlar.maslahat: Find the case in which several colors appear instead of white light.

kunikma: Know that a chick needs warmth to develop inside an egg
usul: Remember that warmth is the most important condition for a chick to develop inside an egg, and choose the option that matches.

variantlar.savol: On a poultry farm, a special box called an incubator is used to hatch chicks from chicken eggs. What does an incubator provide for the eggs above all?

yechim.doska: Incubator — takes the place of the hen
yechim.ovoz: An incubator works in place of a hen sitting on the eggs.

yechim.doska: The hen warms the eggs → the incubator warms them too
yechim.ovoz: A hen warms the eggs with her body. An incubator also keeps the eggs at a steady warmth.

yechim.doska: The chick gets food from inside the egg
yechim.ovoz: The food the chick needs is in the egg itself, so it is not given food or water from outside.
So the correct answer is B, warmth.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A carried over the idea that plants need light to the egg; for a chick in an egg, the main thing is warmth, not light.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought the chick gets food from outside; in fact, the food it needs is inside the egg.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D also thought the chick inside the egg must be given water from outside; you cannot pour water inside an eggshell.

variantlar.maslahat: What does a hen give the eggs when she sits on them?

variantlar.savol: In spring, a dove laid two eggs in its nest in a tree. The father and mother doves take turns sitting on the eggs. If both of them stay away from the nest for a long time, what might happen to the eggs?
javoblar: The eggs get cold, and the chicks inside stop developing.
The chicks hatch from the eggs sooner.
Nothing happens, because the shell protects the egg.
The eggs grow bigger, and their shells get thicker.

yechim.doska: The dove sits on the eggs → warms the eggs
yechim.ovoz: A bird sits on its eggs and warms them with the heat of its body.

yechim.doska: A chick needs warmth to develop
yechim.ovoz: A chick inside an egg grows only when it is kept warm.

yechim.doska: Bird does not return → egg cools → chick does not develop
yechim.ovoz: If the bird does not return for a long time, the egg cools down and the chick cannot develop.
So the correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought the chick hatches faster on its own without its mother; in fact, without warmth the chick does not develop at all.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought the shell protects against everything; the shell cannot keep the egg from getting cold.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought an egg grows after it is laid; the size and shell of the egg do not change.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember what a bird gives its eggs when it sits on them.

yechim.doska: Iron — a metal, conducts current; glass, cotton, wood — do not
yechim.ovoz: Iron is a metal, so it conducts current. Glass, dry cotton, and dry wood do not conduct current.
