javoblar: Absorbing minerals from the soil through roots

yechim.ovoz: The picture shows a yeast cell and a small bud growing out of it.
A fungus has no chlorophyll, and a single cell has neither a heart nor roots.
The bud grows larger and separates from the parent cell; this is how yeast reproduces.
Reproduction is necessary for the species to survive, so the correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought fungi are plants; fungi have no chlorophyll and do not photosynthesize.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C transferred animal organs to a single-celled organism; a single cell has no heart.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused yeast with a plant; yeast has no roots and takes in substances through its cell surface.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about why the small part growing out of the yeast cell in the picture is needed.

kunikma: Read from a graph of changes in two populations the year in which the required population was largest
usul: Use the legend to identify the line for the required population, find its highest point, and read the year for that point on the horizontal axis.

variantlar.savol:
Field mice and eagle owls live on an island. The eagle owls have no natural enemies on this island.
From 1950 to 2010, scientists counted both animals every year and showed the results on a graph.
In which year was the number of mice the greatest?

yechim.ovoz: First, we find the mice line in the legend: it is the solid line with white circles.
This line has two peaks; the second one is higher, above 400.
The highest point is on the middle gridline between 1990 and 2000, that is, in 1995.
So the number of mice was greatest in 1995.

xatolar.umumiy: Many students write the peak of the eagle owl line (1999) or the first, lower peak of the mice line (1965) as the answer.

variantlar.maslahat: First identify the required line from the legend, then look for its highest point.

variantlar.savol:
Hares and lynxes live in a northern forest. The lynxes have no natural enemies in this forest.
From 1900 to 1960, scientists counted both animals every year and showed the results on a graph.
In which year was the number of hares the greatest?

yechim.ovoz: According to the legend, the hares are shown by the solid line with white circles.
This line has three peaks, and the middle one is the highest, at almost 360.
The highest point is on the middle gridline between 1930 and 1940, which is 1935.
So the number of hares was greatest in 1935.

xatolar.umumiy: A typical mistake is writing the year of the lynx line's peak (around 1939) or choosing another, lower peak.

variantlar.maslahat: Find the symbol used for hares in the legend and look at the highest point of that line.

kunikma: Use a graph to explain the relationship between changes in the sizes of predator and prey populations
usul: Compare the peaks and dips of the two lines: which one rises and falls first? Connect this with who hunts whom.

variantlar.savol:
Marmots and wolves live in a mountain pasture. The wolves have no natural enemies in this pasture.
From 1940 to 2000, scientists counted both animals every year and showed the results on a graph. Wolves hunt marmots.
How are the changes in the numbers of the two animals related?
javoblar: After the number of marmots increases, the number of wolves also increases a little later, because they have more food; after the wolves increase, the number of marmots decreases.
When the number of wolves increases, the number of marmots also increases, because the wolves protect the marmots from other enemies.
The number of wolves always increases before the number of marmots, and the marmots increase after them.
The numbers of the two animals change randomly, independently of each other.

yechim.ovoz: On the graph, the number of marmots reaches its peak first, and a few years later the number of wolves reaches its peak.

yechim.doska: Many prey → more food for predators → predators increase
yechim.ovoz: When there are many marmots, the wolves have enough food and their numbers grow.

yechim.doska: Many predators → prey decrease → then predators decrease too
yechim.ovoz: As the wolves increase, they hunt many marmots and the marmots decrease; then, without enough food, the wolves decrease too.
This process repeats, so the correct answer is option A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B did not understand the predator-prey relationship; wolves do not protect marmots, they hunt them.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C read the order on the graph backwards: the marmots increase first, then the wolves.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D did not notice the repeating pattern in the lines: both numbers change with the same rhythm, a few years apart.

variantlar.maslahat: Notice which line peaks first and which peaks later.

variantlar.savol:
Rats and jungle cats live in a riverside tugai forest. The jungle cats have no natural enemies here.
From 1960 to 2020, scientists counted both animals every year and showed the results on a graph. Jungle cats hunt rats.
According to the graph, which statement about the changes in the numbers of the two animals is correct?
javoblar: The numbers of both animals always rise and fall at the same time and by the same amount.
When the number of jungle cats increases, the number of rats also increases, because the cats leave food for the rats.
After the number of rats increases, the number of cats increases a few years later; once the cats have multiplied, the number of rats decreases.
As the number of rats increases, the number of jungle cats always keeps decreasing.

yechim.ovoz: On the graph, the cats' peak comes a few years after the rats' peak.

yechim.doska: Many rats → more food for cats → cats increase
yechim.ovoz: When the rats multiply, the cats have more food and multiply too.

yechim.doska: Many cats → rats decrease → cats decrease too
yechim.ovoz: The growing number of cats hunt many rats, the rats decrease, and then, without enough food, the cats decrease too.
So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A saw the general similarity between the two lines but ignored the gap in years between the peaks and the different sizes of the numbers.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B mixed up who hunts whom; the cats eat the rats, they do not leave food for them.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D read the graph incorrectly: after the period when the rats multiply, the number of cats does not decrease; on the contrary, it increases.

variantlar.maslahat: Look at which way the cat line goes after the years when the rats multiplied.

kunikma: Use a chemical formula to find the number of atoms of each element in a molecule
usul: The subscript after each chemical symbol in a formula shows the number of atoms of that element; if no subscript is written, there is one atom.

variantlar.savol:
The formula of a phosphoric acid molecule is $\mathrm{H_3PO_4}$.
Which row correctly shows the number of atoms of each element in this molecule?

yechim.ovoz: The hydrogen symbol H is followed by the subscript 3, so there are 3 hydrogen atoms.
The phosphorus symbol P has no subscript after it, so there is one phosphorus atom.
Oxygen, O, is followed by the subscript 4, so there are 4 oxygen atoms.
So the correct row is option D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A ignored the subscripts completely and counted each element as one atom.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought the subscript 3 after H also applies to the next element, phosphorus; a subscript applies only to the symbol before it.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C read the subscripts shifted by one symbol: gave the 4 to phosphorus and took oxygen as one.

variantlar.maslahat: Look at which symbol each subscript sits at the lower right of.

variantlar.savol:
The formula of washing soda (sodium carbonate) is $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$.
Which row correctly shows the number of atoms of each element in the formula of this substance?

yechim.ovoz: The sodium symbol Na is followed by the subscript 2, so there are 2 sodium atoms.
The carbon symbol C has no subscript after it, so there is one carbon atom.
Oxygen, O, is followed by the subscript 3, so there are 3 oxygen atoms.
So the correct row is option A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought the subscript 2 applies to the symbol after it, carbon; a subscript applies to the symbol before it.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C counted the subscript 2 after Na as applying to both sodium and carbon.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D ignored the subscripts and counted one atom of each element.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember how many atoms an element has when no subscript is written.

kunikma: Apply the condensation of water vapor in the air on a cold surface to explain an everyday event
usul: Think about where the droplets came from: air always contains invisible water vapor; when it touches a cold surface, it cools and turns into liquid droplets (condensation).

variantlar.savol:
On a hot summer day in a teahouse, ice-cold ayran was poured into a glass. A few minutes later, tiny water droplets appeared on the OUTSIDE wall of the glass. The glass is whole and not cracked anywhere.
How did these droplets form?
javoblar: The ayran seeped through the glass wall to the outside.
Water vapor in the air touched the cold surface of the glass, cooled, and turned into liquid droplets (condensation).
The warm air on the surface of the glass evaporated and turned into droplets.
The cold inside the glass came out through the wall and turned into water.

yechim.doska: The glass is whole → the ayran inside cannot get out
yechim.ovoz: The glass is not cracked and glass does not let liquid through, so the droplets did not come from inside.
Warm air always contains water vapor that cannot be seen.

yechim.doska: Water vapor + cold surface → liquid water (condensation)
yechim.ovoz: The vapor touches the ice-cold surface of the glass, cools, and turns into liquid droplets; this is condensation.
So the correct answer is option B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought the droplets came from inside; glass does not let liquid through, and besides, the droplets are clean water, not ayran.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C confused evaporation with condensation: in evaporation a liquid turns into vapor, but here the opposite happened, vapor turned into liquid.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought "cold" is a substance; in fact, heat moves from the air to the glass, and the vapor in the air cools.

variantlar.maslahat: Keep in mind that the droplets are clean water, not ayran: which part of the air could this water come from?

variantlar.savol:
On a winter day, Aziz came into a warm room from the cold street. Right away, the lenses of his glasses fogged up and became cloudy: tiny water droplets appeared on them.
Which statement correctly explains this?
javoblar: The cold air from the street stayed on the surface of the lenses and turned into water.
An invisible layer of ice on the surface of the lenses melted and turned into droplets.
Water vapor in the warm room air touched the cold lenses, cooled, and turned into liquid droplets (condensation).
The lenses warmed up in the room, and the water in them evaporated.

yechim.ovoz: While he was outside, the lenses got very cold.

yechim.doska: The room air is warm and contains water vapor
yechim.ovoz: The warm room air contains invisible water vapor.

yechim.doska: Water vapor + cold lens → liquid droplets (condensation)
yechim.ovoz: The vapor touches the cold lens, cools, and turns into liquid water droplets.
So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought the air itself turns into water; only the water vapor in the air turns into water, and it comes from the room air.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B assumed there was ice on the lenses; there is no ice in the problem, and the droplets appeared only when he entered the warm room.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused condensation with evaporation; in evaporation, droplets do not appear, they disappear.

variantlar.maslahat: The lens is cold and the room air is warm: what invisible thing is in warm air?

kunikma: Know the definition of a compound: it is formed when atoms of different chemical elements combine
usul: Recall the difference between an element (atoms of the same element), a compound (atoms of different elements chemically combined), and a mixture (substances simply mixed together).

variantlar.savol: How does a compound differ from an element?
javoblar: A compound is a simple mixture of several substances.
A compound is formed when atoms of the same element combine.
A compound is made only of metal atoms.
A compound is formed when atoms of different elements combine chemically.

yechim.doska: Element: atoms of the same element ($\mathrm{O_2}$, $\mathrm{Fe}$)
yechim.ovoz: An element is made of atoms of only one kind, for example oxygen or iron.

yechim.doska: Compound: atoms of different elements combined ($\mathrm{H_2O}$)
yechim.ovoz: In a compound, atoms of different elements are chemically bonded, for example hydrogen and oxygen in water.
In a mixture, the substances do not combine chemically; they are simply mixed together.
So the correct answer is option D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A confused a compound with a mixture; in a mixture, substances do not combine chemically.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B chose the definition of an element; atoms of the same element form an element.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C linked the word "compound" with metals; compounds are often made of nonmetals too, for example water.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember which elements' atoms make up a water molecule.

variantlar.savol: Which of the following substances is a compound?

yechim.doska: Compound = atoms of different elements chemically combined
yechim.ovoz: First, let's recall the definition: in a compound, atoms of different elements are combined.
Ozone is made only of oxygen, and copper only of copper; they are elements.

yechim.doska: Air is a mixture of gases
yechim.ovoz: Air is a mixture of nitrogen, oxygen, and other gases; it is not a single substance.
In table salt, two different elements, sodium and chlorine, are chemically combined.
So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought ozone is a compound because its formula has 3 atoms; if the atoms are of the same element, the substance is an element.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought air is a compound because it consists of several gases; air is a mixture.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought a metal is a compound; copper is an element made of atoms of only one kind.

variantlar.maslahat: Count how many DIFFERENT chemical symbols are in each formula.

kunikma: Justify that only repulsion is reliable evidence that an object is a magnet, and choose an experimental method
usul: A magnet attracts any iron object, so attraction is not enough evidence; repulsion happens only between like poles of two magnets.

variantlar.savol:
Nilufar has two steel rods that look the same. She knows that rod 1 is a magnet, but she does not know about rod 2 (see the picture).
How can she use rod 1 to find out FOR SURE whether rod 2 is a magnet?
variantlar.rasm: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 420 180"><rect x="0" y="0" width="420" height="180" fill="#ffffff"/><g font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#222"><rect x="110.0" y="30.0" width="200.0" height="34.0" fill="#e8f1ff" stroke="#222" stroke-width="2" rx="4"/><text x="210.0" y="84.0" text-anchor="middle">Rod 1 (magnet)</text><rect x="110.0" y="110.0" width="200.0" height="34.0" fill="#fde9c8" stroke="#222" stroke-width="2" rx="4"/><text x="210.0" y="164.0" text-anchor="middle">Rod 2 (unknown)</text><text x="96.0" y="52.0" text-anchor="end">X</text><text x="324.0" y="52.0" text-anchor="start">Y</text><text x="96.0" y="132.0" text-anchor="end">P</text><text x="324.0" y="132.0" text-anchor="start">Q</text></g></svg>
javoblar: She brings rod 1 close to rod 2: if they attract each other, rod 2 is a magnet.
She brings end X of rod 1 close to ends P and Q of rod 2, one at a time: if either end is repelled, rod 2 is a magnet.
She brings end X of rod 1 close to ends P and Q of rod 2: if both ends are attracted, rod 2 is a magnet.
She weighs both rods on a scale: if their masses are equal, rod 2 is a magnet.

yechim.ovoz: A magnet also attracts ordinary, unmagnetized steel, so attraction proves nothing.
Repulsion is observed only when both objects are magnets, between their like poles.

yechim.doska: X → P and Q: if either end is repelled ⇒ rod 2 is a magnet
yechim.ovoz: That is why end X must be brought close to both ends of rod 2; if one of them is repelled, rod 2 is a magnet.
So the correct method is option B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A forgot that a magnet also attracts ordinary steel; attraction is observed even if rod 2 is not a magnet.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C drew the opposite conclusion: if both ends are attracted, this shows that rod 2 is ordinary, unmagnetized steel.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought magnetism depends on mass; a magnetized rod and an unmagnetized rod can have the same mass.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember what a magnet does to an ordinary iron object and when it pushes another object away.

variantlar.savol:
Sardor has a magnet with its north pole marked and a similar iron rod that may or may not be a magnet. He brought the north pole of the magnet close to the two ends of the rod, one at a time.
Which observation PROVES that the rod is a magnet?
javoblar: Both ends of the rod were attracted to the magnet.
One end of the rod was attracted to the magnet; he did not test the other end.
The rod had no effect at all on the magnet.
One end of the rod was repelled by the magnet, and the other end was attracted.

yechim.doska: Iron rod (not a magnet) → both ends are attracted
yechim.ovoz: A magnet attracts ordinary iron at either end, so attraction is not enough evidence.
Repulsion happens only between like poles of two magnets.

yechim.doska: One end was repelled ⇒ it is also a north pole ⇒ the rod is a magnet
yechim.ovoz: The end of the rod that was repelled is a north pole, and the end that was attracted is a south pole; so the rod is a magnet.
So the observation that proves it is option D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought attraction is a sign of magnetism; in fact, if both ends are attracted, it shows the rod is ordinary iron.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B considered a single attraction to be enough; since a magnet also attracts ordinary iron, this proves nothing.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C misinterpreted the observation: an iron rod should at least be attracted to a magnet; if there is no effect, it is not iron.

variantlar.maslahat: Which effect is never observed between a magnet and ordinary iron?

kunikma: Know that when the temperature of a substance changes, the speed of its molecules changes (the number and size of the molecules do not change)
usul: Remember that temperature is a measure of the motion of molecules: when the temperature rises, molecules move faster; when it falls, they move more slowly; their number and size do not change.

variantlar.savol: What happens to the molecules of water in a teapot when the water is heated?

yechim.ovoz: The higher the temperature, the faster the molecules move.
When we heat water, its temperature rises, so the molecules move faster.

yechim.doska: The number and size of the molecules do not change
yechim.ovoz: Heating does not create new molecules or make them bigger.
So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought that the expansion of a substance means the molecules get bigger; in fact, the distance between the molecules increases.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought heating creates new molecules; when the amount of water does not change, the number of molecules does not change either.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused heating with cooling; molecules slow down when they are cooled.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember which property of molecules temperature shows.

variantlar.savol:
Two identical glasses contain equal amounts of water: the first at 20 °C, the second at 70 °C.
Which of the following statements is correct?
javoblar: The water at 70 °C has more molecules.
The molecules of the water at 20 °C are larger.
The molecules of the water at 20 °C do not move at all.
The molecules of the water at 70 °C move faster on average.

yechim.doska: Equal amounts of water → equal numbers of molecules
yechim.ovoz: Both glasses contain the same amount of water, so they also contain the same number of molecules.

yechim.doska: The size of a molecule does not depend on temperature
yechim.ovoz: A water molecule is the same size in hot water and in cold water.
Molecules are in constant motion at any temperature.
In water at a higher temperature, the molecules move faster on average.
So the correct answer is option D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought hot water has more molecules; since the amounts of water are equal, the numbers of molecules are equal too.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought the size of a molecule depends on temperature; temperature does not change the size of a molecule.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought molecules stop in colder water; they just move more slowly.

variantlar.maslahat: Separate out what is the same and what is different about the two glasses.

kunikma: Know the observable signs that a chemical reaction has taken place (gas given off, color change, precipitate, heat, light, smell)
usul: Check whether each observation shows that a new substance has formed: dissolving, crushing, and pouring into a container are physical changes; gas bubbles, color change, a precipitate, heat, and light are signs of a chemical reaction.

variantlar.savol:
Malika poured vinegar onto baking soda in a glass, and a chemical reaction took place.
In which of the following pairs can BOTH observations be signs of a chemical reaction?
javoblar: The soda dissolves in the vinegar; the liquid level rises slightly.
Lots of gas bubbles come out and foam forms; a fizzing sound is heard.
Lots of gas bubbles come out; the soda dissolves in the vinegar.
The vinegar splashes onto the walls of the glass; the soda sinks to the bottom of the glass.

yechim.doska: Chemical reaction → a new substance forms
yechim.ovoz: In a chemical reaction, a new substance forms, and we can tell this from certain signs.

yechim.doska: Dissolving, a rising level, splashing: physical changes
yechim.ovoz: Dissolving or a liquid splashing does not make a new substance; these are physical changes.

yechim.doska: Gas bubbles + foam, fizzing → a gas (carbon dioxide) has formed
yechim.ovoz: The bubbles and the fizzing sound show that a new substance, a gas, is being given off.
The pair in which both observations are signs of a reaction is option B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought dissolving is a chemical reaction; no new substance forms when something dissolves, and a rising liquid level is not a sign of a reaction either.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C was satisfied that one observation in the pair was correct; dissolving is not a sign of a chemical reaction.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused "sinking" with forming a precipitate; the soda itself falling to the bottom is not a new substance.

variantlar.maslahat: Check whether a new substance forms in each observation.

variantlar.savol:
Jasur put a cleaned iron nail into a blue solution of copper sulfate ($\mathrm{CuSO_4}$) and left it for several hours. A chemical reaction took place.
In which of the following pairs can BOTH observations be signs of a chemical reaction?
javoblar: The nail sinks to the bottom of the solution; the temperature of the solution hardly changes.
The surface of the nail turns reddish; the nail sinks to the bottom of the solution.
A reddish layer forms on the surface of the nail; the blue color of the solution fades and turns greenish.
The solution stays blue; the shape of the nail does not change.

yechim.doska: Signs: color change, new solid substance, gas, precipitate, heat
yechim.ovoz: Let's recall the signs of a chemical reaction: a color change, a new substance appearing, a gas, a precipitate, heat.

yechim.doska: The nail sinks to the bottom because iron is heavier (physical)
yechim.ovoz: The nail sinks because it is denser than the solution; this is not a sign of a reaction.

yechim.doska: Reddish layer: copper that has formed; color change: a new substance
yechim.ovoz: The reddish layer on the nail's surface is copper that has come out of the solution, and the change in the solution's color shows that a new substance has formed in it.
The pair in which both observations are signs of a reaction is option C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought the nail sinking is a sign of a reaction; it only shows that iron has a high density.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B was satisfied with one correct observation in the pair; the nail sinking is not a sign of a reaction.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D chose the absence of change as an observation; if nothing changes, there is no visible sign that a reaction took place.

variantlar.maslahat: Look for things that were not there before the reaction and appeared afterward.

kunikma: Know how to position a thermometer correctly to measure the temperature of a liquid accurately
usul: For a thermometer to show the temperature of the liquid itself, its tip (bulb) must be inside the liquid but must not touch the bottom or the walls of the container.

Malika wants to test in which glass hot water cools faster. She poured 150 mL of hot water into each of two glasses and plans to keep measuring the water temperature with a thermometer.
The picture shows four ways of positioning the thermometer. To measure the water temperature ACCURATELY, which picture shows how the thermometer should be positioned?

yechim.doska: What is measured: the temperature of the water
yechim.ovoz: We need the temperature of the water itself, not of the glass or the air.

yechim.doska: The thermometer tip must be in the water
yechim.ovoz: A thermometer shows the temperature of whatever it is touching, so its tip must be fully under the water.

yechim.doska: It must not touch the bottom or the wall
yechim.ovoz: The bottom and wall of the glass can be warmer or cooler than the water, so the thermometer must not touch them.

yechim.doska: D: tip in the middle of the water
yechim.ovoz: Only in picture D is the thermometer tip in the middle of the water, away from the bottom and the wall.
So the correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought that the deeper the thermometer goes, the more accurate it is; in fact, its tip touches the bottom of the glass and shows the temperature of the bottom.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought the thermometer could be above the water; then it measures the temperature of the air above the water.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought it was enough for the tip to be in the water; but it is touching the wall of the glass, and the wall's temperature spoils the result.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about where the thermometer tip must be so that it touches only the water itself.

variantlar.savol:
Nilufar wants to observe how fast milk in a saucepan heats up on a gas stove. To do this, she measures the temperature of the milk with a thermometer every 2 minutes.
What should Nilufar do to measure the temperature of the milk ACCURATELY?
javoblar: Rest the tip of the thermometer against the bottom of the saucepan
Put the tip of the thermometer into the milk so that it does not touch the bottom or the side of the saucepan, and read the thermometer in that position
Hold the thermometer a little above the surface of the milk, in the steam
Dip the thermometer into the milk, take it out right away, and then read it

yechim.doska: Needed: the temperature of the milk
yechim.ovoz: We need to know the temperature of the milk, not of the saucepan or the steam.

yechim.doska: Tip inside the milk, away from the bottom and the side
yechim.ovoz: The bottom of the saucepan is close to the flame and is much hotter than the milk, so the thermometer must not touch the bottom.

yechim.doska: Read the thermometer while it is in the milk
yechim.ovoz: If we take the thermometer out, it starts to cool in the air and the reading changes.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) Put the tip of the thermometer into the milk so that it does not touch the bottom or the side of the saucepan, and read the thermometer in that position
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought it would be more reliable if the thermometer touched the bottom; in fact, the hot bottom is warmer than the milk, so the result is too high.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought the temperature of the steam is the same as the temperature of the milk; in this case the thermometer measures the steam and air, not the milk.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought the thermometer reading does not change after it is taken out; in air it changes quickly.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember that a thermometer shows the temperature of whatever it is touching.

kunikma: Identify the quantity kept the same (controlled) from the description of an experiment
usul: First find the quantity that was deliberately changed in the experiment and the quantity measured as the result; the quantity that was left the same in both trials is the controlled variable.

variantlar.savol:
Malika wants to find out in which cup tea cools more slowly: a steel cup or a porcelain cup. She poured 200 mL of tea from the same teapot into each cup, placed the cups on the same table, and measured the tea temperature every 5 minutes with the same thermometer.
Which of the following did Malika keep the same (control) in her experiment?
javoblar: The volume of tea in each cup

yechim.ovoz: What Malika deliberately changed is what the cup is made of.
As the result, she observes the tea temperature and how quickly it cools.
The same amount of tea, 200 milliliters, was poured into both cups; this is the controlled variable.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) The volume of tea in each cup
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A confused the variable that was changed in the experiment with the controlled variable: the materials were deliberately chosen to be different.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought the measured result was a controlled variable; the temperature may turn out different in the two cups.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D took the result of the experiment, that is, the thing being investigated, as a quantity kept the same.

variantlar.maslahat: Look for something that was prepared in advance to be the same for both cups.

variantlar.savol:
Jasur tested in which color of container water heats up faster in sunlight. He took two identical plastic containers and painted one black and the other white. He poured 1 L of water from the same tap into each one and placed the containers side by side in the yard. Then he measured the water temperature every 10 minutes.
Which of the following was kept the same in Jasur's experiment?
javoblar: The water temperature measured every 10 minutes
The volume of water in the containers
Which container's water heats up faster

yechim.ovoz: Jasur deliberately made only one thing different: the color of the container.
As the result, the water temperature is measured every ten minutes.
The same amount of water, one liter, was poured into both containers; this is the quantity kept the same.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) The volume of water in the containers
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A mistook the very variable that was deliberately changed for one kept the same.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought the temperature was kept the same because the measurement times were the same; but temperature is the measured result.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D took the question (result) of the experiment as a quantity kept the same.

variantlar.maslahat: Find the amount that was made the same for both containers.

kunikma: Use data from a temperature–time graph to conclude which object heated up faster
usul: Compare along which line the temperature rose more in the same amount of time: the object with the steeper line heated up faster.

variantlar.savol:
Aziz heated 1 L of water in an electric kettle and another 1 L of water in a kettle on a gas stove, and measured the water temperature every 2 minutes. He plotted the results on a graph.
According to the graph, which heater heated the water faster?

kunikma: Know that active volcanoes and strong earthquakes are located at the boundaries of lithospheric plates
usul: Volcanoes and earthquakes are connected with movements inside the Earth; these movements are strongest at the boundaries of lithospheric plates.

variantlar.savol:
Hundreds of active volcanoes are arranged in a ring along the coasts and islands that surround the Pacific Ocean. This ring is often called the "Ring of Fire."
What explains why these volcanoes are located in exactly this place?
javoblar: The ocean water is warmest here
Large rivers flow into the ocean here
This region has a tropical climate and very hot weather
The boundaries of lithospheric plates run through here

yechim.doska: Volcano: magma reaching the Earth's surface
yechim.ovoz: A volcano forms when magma from inside the Earth comes to the surface through cracks in the Earth's crust.

yechim.doska: Places with many cracks: plate boundaries
yechim.ovoz: Where lithospheric plates collide or move apart, the Earth's crust cracks.

yechim.doska: Around the Pacific Ocean: plate boundaries
yechim.ovoz: The Ring of Fire runs exactly along the boundary between the Pacific Plate and other plates.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) The boundaries of lithospheric plates run through here
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A linked the heat of volcanoes with the temperature of the water; the heat of volcanoes comes from inside the Earth.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B linked rivers with volcanoes; rivers do not cause volcanoes to form.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C linked volcanoes with a hot climate; volcanoes also exist in cold regions (for example, Iceland and Antarctica).

variantlar.maslahat: Think about where magma could reach the Earth's surface more easily.

variantlar.savol: In which places on the Earth's surface are strong earthquakes and active volcanoes most common?
javoblar: On wide plains in the middle of continents
At boundaries where lithospheric plates collide or move apart
In polar regions covered with glaciers
On the shores of large lakes and seas

yechim.doska: Earthquakes and volcanoes: results of the Earth's internal forces
yechim.ovoz: Both events are connected with the movement of the Earth's crust.

yechim.doska: The lithosphere is made up of several plates
yechim.ovoz: The Earth's hard outer shell, the lithosphere, is divided into several large plates, and they move slowly.

yechim.doska: The strongest movement is at the boundaries
yechim.ovoz: Where plates meet and separate, stress builds up: earthquakes happen and magma comes out.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) At boundaries where lithospheric plates collide or move apart
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A chose the inner, stable part of the plates; on plains, earthquakes and volcanoes are rare.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought it mattered whether a region is cold or hot; these events do not depend on climate.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused the boundary between water and land with plate boundaries; many coasts are not at plate boundaries.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about where the Earth's crust moves and cracks the most.

usul: During an eclipse, all three bodies are in a straight line; the shadow of the body in the middle falls on the third one. In a solar eclipse, the Moon is in the middle; in a lunar eclipse, the Earth is in the middle.

The body that blocks sunlight from reaching the Earth is the Moon.

yechim.doska: Q, Moon, Earth in one line
yechim.ovoz: So the Moon must be between the Sun and the Earth, in a straight line with them.
This arrangement is shown in diagram B.
So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A confused solar and lunar eclipses: in this arrangement, the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon, which is a lunar eclipse.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C did not take into account that all three bodies must be in one line; in this position, the Moon is seen at a quarter phase.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought it was enough for the Moon just to be close to the Sun; the Moon is not on the line between the Sun and the Earth, so its shadow does not fall on the Earth.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about which body could block sunlight from reaching the Earth.

variantlar.savol: How are the Sun, Earth, and Moon positioned during a lunar eclipse?
javoblar: Sun, Moon, Earth in a straight line, with the Moon in the middle
The Sun, Earth, and Moon are positioned at a right angle
Sun, Earth, Moon in a straight line, with the Earth in the middle
Earth, Sun, Moon in a straight line, with the Sun in the middle

yechim.doska: The Moon does not give off its own light
yechim.ovoz: We see the Moon because it reflects sunlight.

yechim.doska: Lunar eclipse: sunlight does not reach the Moon
yechim.ovoz: During a lunar eclipse, sunlight does not reach the Moon, and it darkens.

yechim.doska: What blocks the light: the Earth
yechim.ovoz: The Earth blocks sunlight from the Moon; that is, the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.

yechim.doska: Q, Earth, Moon, with the Earth in the middle
yechim.ovoz: So the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon, in a straight line.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) Sun, Earth, Moon in a straight line, with the Earth in the middle
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A confused a lunar eclipse with a solar eclipse: when the Moon is in the middle, the Sun is eclipsed.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B chose the position for a quarter phase; in that case, no shadow falls on the Moon.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D put the Sun in the middle; the Sun is the source of light and does not cast a shadow, and the Moon would be fully lit.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about which body could block sunlight from reaching the Moon.

kunikma: Identify which characteristic was used as the basis for sorting animals into groups
usul: Check each characteristic: the basis of classification is the characteristic that is the same for all the animals within a group but differs between the two groups.

variantlar.savol:
In the table, some animals are sorted into two groups.
Which characteristic was used as the basis for sorting the animals into groups?

yechim.doska: Group 1: sheep, rabbit, camel: eat plants
yechim.ovoz: All the animals in the first group are herbivores.

yechim.doska: Group 2: wolf, eagle, lizard: eat animals
yechim.ovoz: The animals in the second group feed on other animals: the wolf and the eagle are predators, and the lizard eats insects.
All the animals breathe with lungs, so this characteristic does not separate the groups.

yechim.doska: Reproduction and movement differ within group 2
yechim.ovoz: The wolf gives birth to live young, while the eagle and the lizard lay eggs; the wolf runs and the eagle flies, so these characteristics do not fit either.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) Way of feeding (what it eats)
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A did not check the breathing organs: all the animals in the table breathe with lungs.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B did not take into account that in group 2 the wolf gives birth to live young, while the eagle and the lizard lay eggs.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C ignored that group 2 is a mix of running, flying, and crawling animals.

variantlar.maslahat: Find the characteristic that is the same for all three animals in each group.

variantlar.savol:
In the table, some animals are sorted into two groups.
Which characteristic was used as the basis for sorting the animals into groups?

javoblar: Way of reproducing (lays eggs or gives birth to live young)

yechim.doska: Group 1: chicken, turtle, snake: lay eggs
yechim.ovoz: All the animals in the first group reproduce by laying eggs.

yechim.doska: Group 2: dog, bat, dolphin: give birth to live young
yechim.ovoz: The animals in the second group are mammals; they give birth to live young.

yechim.doska: Food and movement differ within a group
yechim.ovoz: The turtle eats plants and the snake eats animals; the bat flies and the dolphin swims, so these characteristics do not separate the groups.
The dolphin also breathes with lungs, so this characteristic does not differ either.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) Way of reproducing (lays eggs or gives birth to live young)
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A did not take into account that in group 1 the turtle feeds on plants, while the snake feeds on animals.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C ignored that group 2 contains running, flying, and swimming animals.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought the dolphin breathes with gills like a fish; in fact, all the animals in the table breathe with lungs.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember how the animals in each group reproduce.

kunikma: Know that producers use energy from the Sun to make organic matter themselves
usul: Remember where each organism in an ecosystem gets its energy: producers from the Sun (photosynthesis), consumers by eating other organisms, and decomposers by breaking down dead remains.

variantlar.savol:
In a cotton field ecosystem, the cotton plant is a producer.
Why is this so?
javoblar: It gets energy by breaking down rotting plant and animal remains in the soil
It absorbs ready-made organic food from the soil through its roots
It uses energy from the Sun to make organic matter from carbon dioxide and water
It gets energy by eating insects in the field

yechim.ovoz: The word producer means "maker," that is, an organism that creates its own food.
Green plants use light energy to make organic matter from carbon dioxide and water.

yechim.doska: The cotton plant is a green plant
yechim.ovoz: Cotton leaves contain chlorophyll, and the plant carries out photosynthesis, so it is a producer.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) It uses energy from the Sun to make organic matter from carbon dioxide and water
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A confused a producer with a decomposer; remains are broken down by bacteria and fungi.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought a plant gets ready-made food from the soil; the roots take in water and mineral salts, while the leaves make organic matter.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused a producer with a consumer; organisms that eat other organisms are consumers.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember the process by which a green plant makes its own food.

variantlar.savol: Which of the following organisms living in a lake ecosystem is a producer?

yechim.doska: Producer: makes food using energy from the Sun
yechim.ovoz: Producers make their own food through photosynthesis.
Algae are green, and they carry out photosynthesis in sunlight.
Fish and frogs eat other organisms, while decay bacteria break down dead remains.
So the correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought that fish that eat algae make food; fish eat ready-made food, so they are consumers.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought bacteria are producers because they recycle substances; decay organisms are decomposers.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D did not take into account that frogs feed by eating insects and other small animals; they are consumers.

variantlar.maslahat: Find the organism that can carry out photosynthesis.

kunikma: Know that water (moisture) is a necessary condition for a seed to germinate
usul: A seed needs three conditions to germinate: water (moisture), air (oxygen), and a suitable temperature. Light, soil, and fertilizer are not necessary for germination.

variantlar.savol:
Bean seeds germinate equally well in a dark cupboard and on a bright windowsill.
Which of the following is a NECESSARY condition for seeds to germinate?
javoblar: A lot of carbon dioxide gas

yechim.ovoz: A seed needs three main conditions to germinate: water, air, and a suitable temperature.
As the problem says, seeds germinate even in the dark, so light is not necessary.

yechim.doska: Water makes the seed swell and starts its processes
yechim.ovoz: When the seed absorbs water, it swells, the stored food in it dissolves, and the embryo begins to grow.
So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A confused a growing plant's need for light with germination; the problem says that seeds germinate even in the dark.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought a seed cannot germinate without soil; a seed also germinates on wet cotton wool or gauze, because at first its own stored food is enough.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused the gas needed for photosynthesis with germination; a germinating seed respires and needs oxygen.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about why seeds kept in a dry storeroom do not germinate for years.

variantlar.savol:
Nilufar placed pea seeds on dry cotton wool and left them in a warm room. Even after a week, the seeds had not germinated.
What did the seeds lack in order to germinate?

yechim.ovoz: The room has air and is warm, so the conditions of oxygen and a suitable temperature are met.

yechim.doska: Missing: water (the cotton wool is dry)
yechim.ovoz: Because the cotton wool was dry, the seeds could not absorb water.

yechim.doska: Without water, a seed does not swell or germinate
yechim.ovoz: Without water, the life processes inside the seed do not start.
So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought seeds need light to germinate; many seeds germinate even in the dark.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought soil is necessary for germination; seeds germinate well on wet cotton wool too.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D considered fertilizer necessary; during germination, the seed uses its own stored food.

variantlar.maslahat: Determine which condition is met in the warm room and which is not.

kunikma: Know that air (oxygen) and a suitable temperature are necessary for a seed to germinate
usul: Recall the conditions for germination: water, air (oxygen), and a suitable temperature. Determine which condition is not met in the situation, or which condition is being taken into account.

variantlar.savol:
Jasur put wheat seeds into a glass full of water. The seeds stayed completely under water, and even after several days they did not germinate.
What is the main reason the seeds did not germinate?
javoblar: There is no light in water
There is no fertilizer in the water
The seeds took in too much water and became heavy
Not enough air (oxygen) reached the seeds

yechim.doska: Water is present, the room is warm
yechim.ovoz: The seeds have enough water, and the temperature is suitable too.

yechim.doska: A germinating seed respires, so it needs oxygen
yechim.ovoz: A germinating seed respires intensively and uses up oxygen to do this.

yechim.doska: There is very little oxygen under water
yechim.ovoz: There is little oxygen dissolved in water; if a seed stays completely under water, it does not get enough air.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) Not enough air (oxygen) reached the seeds
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought light is necessary for germination; seeds germinate even in the dark.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought fertilizer is a condition for germination; at first, a seed feeds on its own stored food.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought too much water makes the seed heavy; the main problem is a lack of air.

variantlar.maslahat: A germinating seed is alive too; think about what it needs in order to respire.

variantlar.savol:
In spring, farmers sow cotton seeds not right away but after the soil has warmed up enough (to about +12…+14 °C). Cotton seeds sown in cold soil may rot without germinating.
Which condition for seed germination does this depend on?

yechim.ovoz: A seed needs water, air, and a suitable temperature to germinate.

yechim.doska: The point is about the soil warming up
yechim.ovoz: The farmers are waiting for the soil temperature to rise.

yechim.doska: In the cold, germination processes are very slow
yechim.ovoz: At low temperatures, the life processes in the seed slow down, and the seed fails to germinate.
So the correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B linked the bright days of spring with germination; the situation is about soil temperature.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought fertilizer is a condition for germination; fertilizer is needed later for growth, not for germination.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused the gas needed for photosynthesis with germination.

variantlar.maslahat: Pay attention to what change the farmers are waiting for.

kunikma: Know the function of the uterus among the reproductive organs of mammals
usul: Recall the functions of the reproductive organs: the ovary produces egg cells, the oviduct is the passage through which an egg cell travels, and the uterus is where the embryo (fetus) develops.

variantlar.savol:
The uterus is one of the reproductive organs of mammals.
What is the main function of the uterus?
javoblar: To be the place where the embryo (fetus) develops and is protected

yechim.ovoz: Egg cells are produced in the ovary.

yechim.doska: Fertilized egg cell → attaches to the wall of the uterus
yechim.ovoz: The fertilized egg cell moves down into the uterus and attaches to its wall.

yechim.doska: Uterus: the fetus develops and receives food and oxygen
yechim.ovoz: The fetus develops in the uterus and receives food and oxygen from the mother through the placenta.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) To be the place where the embryo (fetus) develops and is protected
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A confused the uterus with the ovary.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B confused a reproductive organ with an excretory organ, the bladder.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused the uterus with the stomach; because the fetus is in the mother's belly, they linked it with a digestive organ.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember where the fetus develops in the mother's body.

variantlar.savol:
A cow carries her calf inside her body for about 9 months.
In which organ of the mother's body does the calf develop?

yechim.ovoz: A cow is a mammal; it gives birth to live young.

yechim.doska: The organ where the fetus develops: the uterus
yechim.ovoz: In mammals, the fertilized egg cell attaches to the wall of the uterus, and the fetus develops there.

yechim.doska: The uterus protects and nourishes the fetus
yechim.ovoz: In the uterus, the fetus is protected and receives food and oxygen from the mother.
So the correct answer is D.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A understood the phrase "in the belly" as meaning the stomach; the stomach is a digestive organ.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B confused the place where egg cells are produced with the place where the fetus develops.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C confused a reproductive organ with an excretory organ, the bladder.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember which reproductive organ is adapted to carry the fetus.

So in each particle, three white circles must be attached to one black circle.

yechim.doska: A: $N_2$ + $H_2$; C: NH; D: separate atoms

kunikma: Identify direct signs that energy was released in a chemical reaction (heat, light, sound)
usul: Direct evidence that energy was released is heat (a rise in temperature), light, or sound given off to the surroundings. Gas bubbles, a color change, and a precipitate are signs of a chemical change, but they do not show that energy was released.

variantlar.savol:
Malika mixed two solutions in a test tube and observed that a reaction was taking place.
Which of the following observations shows that energy was released in this reaction?
javoblar: Gas bubbles appeared in the test tube
The color of the solution changed from blue to colorless
The wall of the test tube became hot, and a thermometer showed that the temperature rose
A white precipitate formed at the bottom of the test tube

yechim.doska: Energy is released → heat, light, sound to the surroundings
yechim.ovoz: When energy is released in a reaction, it often comes out as heat, light, or sound.

yechim.doska: Gas, color, precipitate: signs of a new substance
yechim.ovoz: Gas being given off, a color change, and a precipitate forming show that a new substance has formed, but they tell us nothing about energy.
When the test tube gets hot, we can directly see that the reaction gave off heat to its surroundings.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) The wall of the test tube became hot, and a thermometer showed that the temperature rose
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A thought gas bubbles are a sign of boiling or heat; gas is also given off in reactions that absorb heat.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought a color change means energy was released; it only shows that a new substance has formed.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought the formation of a precipitate is a sign that energy was released; a precipitate is also only a sign of a chemical change.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember the forms in which energy can be given off to the surroundings.

variantlar.savol:
The teacher brought a burning splint close to the mouth of a test tube filled with hydrogen gas.
Which of the following observations is direct evidence that energy was released in this reaction?
javoblar: The gas in the test tube was colorless
A short "pop" sound was heard and a flame flashed
Tiny water droplets appeared on the walls of the test tube
The gas quickly spread out of the test tube

yechim.doska: Signs of energy release: heat, light, sound
yechim.ovoz: We know that energy was released from the heat, light, or sound given off to the surroundings.
Hydrogen reacts with oxygen in the air to form water.

yechim.doska: Sound and flame: energy was released
yechim.ovoz: The sound that was heard and the flame that flashed are sound and light, that is, direct evidence of the energy released.
The water droplets show that a reaction product formed, not energy.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) A short "pop" sound was heard and a flame flashed
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A chose a property of the substance before the reaction; it tells us nothing about the reaction.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought a reaction product is a sign of energy; the formation of water only shows that a new substance appeared.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought the spreading of the gas (diffusion) is a sign of a reaction; it is a physical process.

variantlar.maslahat: Look for forms of energy that you can detect with your eyes and ears.

usul: The current of the whole circuit flows through the part connected in series; at the branching point of a parallel connection, this current divides between the branches. The current divides equally between branches with identical lamps.

variantlar.savol:

Which statement is correct?

xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought extra current is created in the branches; in fact, the sum of the currents in the branches equals the main current.

variantlar.maslahat: Think about what happens to the current at the branching point.

kunikma: Identify heat transfer by conduction in a solid (a metal)
usul: Distinguish the three ways heat is transferred: conduction, through the particles of a solid; convection, with currents in a liquid or gas; and radiation, by rays, even through empty space.

variantlar.savol:
Aziz put a metal spoon into a cup of hot tea. After a while, the handle of the spoon sticking out of the tea also got hot.
By which method did heat reach the spoon handle?

yechim.ovoz: Heat passed through the spoon itself, from the end in the tea to the handle.

yechim.doska: The vibration of particles is passed on
yechim.ovoz: Heated particles make neighboring particles vibrate too, and in this way heat spreads along the spoon.
The transfer of heat through a solid without the substance itself moving is called conduction.
So the correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B was thinking of the warm currents in the tea; convection happens in liquids and gases, not inside a solid spoon.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought the heat came by radiation; the handle was heated through the metal of the spoon, not by radiation from the tea.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D mistook the expansion of a heated object for a method of heat transfer; expansion is a result of heating.

variantlar.maslahat: Determine which substance the heat passed through and whether that substance is a solid, a liquid, or a gas.

variantlar.savol:
The outer bottom of a steel pot on a gas stove is heated by the flame. A little later, the inner bottom of the pot also gets hot.
By which method does heat pass from the outer side of the pot's bottom to the inner side?

yechim.doska: The bottom of the pot is solid metal
yechim.ovoz: Heat passes from the outer side to the inner side through the inside of the steel bottom.

yechim.doska: Metal particles pass heat on to each other
yechim.ovoz: The particles close to the flame vibrate strongly and pass energy on to neighboring particles.
Heat transfer through a solid is conduction.
So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A remembered the circulation of water inside the pot; convection happens in liquids and gases, not inside a metal bottom.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B remembered that a flame gives off radiation; but heat does not pass from one side of a metal bottom to the other by radiation.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought the expansion of a metal when heated is a method of heat transfer.

variantlar.maslahat: Determine whether the substance the heat is passing through is a solid, a liquid, or a gas.

kunikma: Know that the main cause of ocean tides (the regular rise and fall of the water) is the Moon's gravitational pull
usul: Recall that tides are the periodic rise and fall of sea level over the course of a day, and identify the force that causes them: the gravity of the Moon, the large celestial body closest to Earth.

variantlar.savol:
Fishermen living on the seashore notice that the water level rises about twice a day and falls twice a day. This phenomenon is called the tide.
What is the main cause of tides?
javoblar: eruptions of volcanoes on the ocean floor

yechim.doska: Tides: the water level rises and falls ≈ 2 times a day
yechim.ovoz: First, let's identify the phenomenon: it is the regular, periodic rise and fall of ocean water.

yechim.doska: Periodic phenomenon → needs a periodic cause
yechim.ovoz: Random or constant factors, such as a volcano or a river, cannot produce a change that repeats twice every day.

yechim.doska: Earth's revolution around the Sun — 1 year
yechim.ovoz: Earth takes one year to go around the Sun, so this cannot explain daily tides.

yechim.doska: The Moon pulls the water → a water “bulge” forms in the ocean
yechim.ovoz: The Moon pulls on Earth's water; as Earth spins on its axis, the coast passes through these water bulges, and the water rises and falls.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) the Moon's gravitational pull
yechim.ovoz: So the main cause of tides is the Moon's gravitational pull.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A linked the water level only to water being added; rivers flow all the time and do not cause a rise and fall twice a day.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B confused Earth's motions: going around the Sun takes a year and is not the cause of tides.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused tides with a tsunami (a wave caused by a volcano or earthquake); tsunamis are rare, but tides happen every day.

variantlar.maslahat: For an event that repeats regularly every day, think about which celestial body has a constant and the strongest effect.

variantlar.savol: Which of the following celestial bodies has the GREATEST effect on the tides in Earth's oceans?

yechim.doska: Tides are caused by the gravitational pull of a celestial body
yechim.ovoz: Tides happen because the gravitational pull of celestial bodies acts on ocean water.

yechim.doska: The effect depends on mass and, above all, on distance
yechim.ovoz: The tidal effect depends on the body's mass, but it decreases very quickly as distance increases.

yechim.doska: The Moon is the celestial body closest to Earth (≈ 384 000 km)
yechim.ovoz: The Moon is very close to Earth, so its tidal effect is the greatest.

yechim.doska: The Sun's effect is about 2 times smaller than the Moon's; the effect of Mars and Jupiter is tiny
yechim.ovoz: Although the Sun is huge, it is very far away; and the effect of the planets cannot be felt at all.
So the Moon has the greatest effect on the tides.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A looked only at mass: the Sun is huge, but because it is so far away, its tidal effect is about half that of the Moon.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought Mars is close to Earth; in fact Mars is hundreds of times farther away than the Moon, and its effect cannot be felt.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought the largest planet has the strongest effect; Jupiter is very far away, and its effect cannot be felt.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember that the effect of gravity depends not only on mass but also on distance.

kunikma: Identify a landform (a summit) on a topographic map from the contour lines and their elevation labels
usul: Determine whether the elevation values on the contour lines increase or decrease toward the marked point: if they increase inward, it is a hill (summit); if they decrease, it is a depression.

variantlar.savol:
The picture shows a topographic map of Qumtepa Island. The lines on the map are contour lines, that is, lines joining points at the same elevation. The numbers show the height above sea level in meters.
What landform is located at the place marked K on the map?

yechim.doska: Closed contour lines around K: 100 → 200 → 300 → 400 m
yechim.ovoz: Point K is at the center of closed contour lines that lie one inside another.
The outer line is 100 meters and the innermost is 400 meters, so the land gets higher toward the center.

yechim.doska: K is the highest place on the island (above 400 m)
yechim.ovoz: So point K is even higher than 400 meters; it is the highest point on the island.
So there is a hill, that is, a mountain summit, at K.

xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought the closed circles were a hollow and did not notice that the elevation values increase inward.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C took the contour lines for the shorelines of a body of water; a lake is not found at the highest place.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D associated the lines with a river; a valley is a low place, but K is the highest point.

variantlar.maslahat: Look at how the numbers on the contour lines change as you get closer to K.

variantlar.savol:
The picture shows a topographic map of Bodomzor Island. The lines on the map are contour lines, that is, lines joining points at the same elevation. The numbers show the height above sea level in meters.
What landform is located at the place marked M on the map?

yechim.ovoz: We read the elevations of the closed lines around point M from the outside in.
Each inner line is 50 meters higher than the one outside it, so the land rises toward M.

yechim.doska: M is inside the innermost line, above 200 m
yechim.ovoz: M is the highest point on the island, while the second hill is only a little over 100 meters high.
So there is a mountain summit at M.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A was misled by the word “Bay” on the map; the bay is on the coast, while M is in the middle of the island.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B thought closed contour lines always mean a hollow and did not take into account that the values increase inward.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C took the contour lines for flow lines; a river starts in high ground, but the summit itself is not a river.

variantlar.maslahat: Compare whether the value of the innermost contour line is greater or less than that of the outer lines.

kunikma: Knowing that a river flows downhill, from high to low ground, choose and justify the course of a river and its direction of flow on a topographic map
usul: A river starts at a spring and always flows downhill: its course must cross contour lines only from higher to lower, must not climb another hill or run along a contour line, and the arrow must point toward the sea.

variantlar.savol:
The picture shows a topographic map of Lolazor Island. Contour lines are lines joining points at the same elevation; the numbers show elevation in meters. There is a spring at point T; the river that starts there flows into Quiet Bay. Four paths with arrows (1, 2, 3, 4) are drawn on the map.
Which path CORRECTLY shows the course of the river and its direction of flow?

yechim.doska: A river always flows from high to low: T (above 400 m) → bay (0 m)
yechim.ovoz: Under the force of gravity, water flows only downhill, so the river runs down from the summit to the sea.

yechim.doska: Path 1: crosses over a 200 m hill — there is an uphill section ✗
yechim.ovoz: The first path crosses into the contour lines of the small hill, which means the water would have to flow uphill — that is impossible.

yechim.doska: Path 3: winds between the 200 and 300 m contour lines ✗
yechim.ovoz: The third path runs parallel to the contour lines, winding at almost the same height; it does not go down and does not reach the sea.

yechim.doska: Path 4: the arrow points from the bay to the summit ✗
yechim.ovoz: On the fourth path, the water is shown flowing up from the sea to the summit; the direction is reversed.

yechim.doska: Path 2: from T through the low ground between the hills to the bay, only downhill ✓
yechim.ovoz: The second path crosses contour lines only going downhill and reaches the bay through the low ground between two hills.
So the correct course of the river is path 2.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A picked the shortest, straightest path; but this path goes over the 200-meter hill — a river does not flow uphill.
xatolar.2: A student who chose C thought a river flows along a contour line; along a contour line the elevation does not change, but water must flow downhill.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D reversed the direction of flow: water does not flow up from the sea to the summit; it flows down from the spring to the sea.

variantlar.maslahat: As you follow each path, check whether the elevation keeps decreasing and which way the arrow points.

variantlar.savol:
The picture shows a topographic map of Cloudy Island. Contour lines are lines joining points at the same elevation; the numbers show elevation in meters. There is a spring at point Q; the river that starts there flows into Fisherman's Bay. Four paths with arrows (1, 2, 3, 4) are drawn on the map.
Which path CORRECTLY shows the course of the river and its direction of flow?

yechim.doska: A river flows from high to low: Q (above 200 m) → bay (0 m)
yechim.ovoz: The spring is at the highest place and the bay is at sea level — water flows only that way, downhill.

yechim.doska: Path 1: the arrow points from the bay to Q ✗
yechim.ovoz: On the first path the direction of flow is reversed: the water is shown climbing from the sea to the summit.

yechim.doska: Path 2: crosses over a 100 m hill ✗
yechim.ovoz: The second path crosses into the contour lines of the small hill — water cannot flow uphill.

yechim.doska: Path 4: winds between the 100 and 150 m contour lines ✗
yechim.ovoz: The fourth path runs parallel to the contour lines, winding at almost the same height, and does not go down to the sea.

yechim.doska: Path 3: from Q through the low ground between the hills to the bay ✓
yechim.ovoz: The third path crosses contour lines only going downhill and reaches the bay between the hills.
So the correct course of the river is path 3.

xatolar.0: A student who chose A looked at the shape of the path and ignored the direction of the arrow: on this path the water is shown flowing from the sea to the summit.
xatolar.1: A student who chose B picked the straightest path, but it goes over the 100-meter hill — a river does not climb a hill.
xatolar.3: A student who chose D thought the river winds around the summit along a contour line; that way the water never goes down.

variantlar.maslahat: Remember that the values of the contour lines a path crosses must keep decreasing one after another.

Alpha's population will grow, so more land will be needed for housing, roads, and farmland.
Land use in Beta will rise sharply, because its numbers of births and deaths are equal.
Land use in Alpha will decrease, because as the population grows, there is less land per person.

yechim.ovoz: First we see that in Alpha births outnumber deaths — the population grows.

yechim.doska: Beta: $12 - 12 = 0$ → the population stays almost the same
yechim.ovoz: In Beta, the population stays stable.

yechim.doska: More people → more housing, roads, food → more land
yechim.ovoz: When the population grows, people need new homes, roads, and farmland to grow more food.
That is why the amount of land in use increases in Alpha, the country whose population is growing.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) Alpha's population will grow, so more land will be needed
yechim.ovoz: So the best-supported prediction is option B.

xatolar.3: A student who chose D confused less land per person with less land being used overall; in fact, the total land in use increases.

In Delta, however, the population grows quickly.

yechim.doska: More people → more housing and food → more land
yechim.ovoz: A growing population needs land for new homes, schools, roads, and for growing more food.

yechim.doska: New land is developed in Delta

yechim.doska: Answer: C) More land will be developed in Delta

xatolar.3: A student who chose D took today's small harvest to mean a smaller need for land in the future; when the population grows, the need for food, and therefore for farmland, increases.

javoblar: Pollution in Gamma will rise sharply, because its deaths outnumber its births.
Pollution in Delta will decrease, because it now uses little oil.
Pollution will be the same in both countries, because their areas are equal.
Pollution in Delta may increase: as the population grows quickly, waste, transportation, and energy use also increase.

In Delta, the population grows quickly.

yechim.doska: More people → more waste, transportation, energy → more pollution
yechim.ovoz: When there are more people, the need for household waste disposal, cars, and electricity increases.
Even though Delta uses little oil now, consumption and pollution will rise as its population grows.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) Pollution in Delta may increase
yechim.ovoz: So the best-supported prediction is option D.
