kunikma: Determining how the result changes when one variable in a formula changes (inverse proportionality)
usul: t is in the denominator. If the other quantities do not change, the fraction decreases by the same factor as the denominator increases.

variantlar.savol: Botir wants to make the watering time three times as long, while the water volume V and k stay the same. How does D change?

yechim.ovoz: If we make the time three times as long, we write 3t instead of t.
The denominator became 3 times larger and the numerator did not change, so the fraction becomes 3 times smaller.

yechim.doska: D and t are inversely proportional
yechim.ovoz: The longer the time, the fewer drops per minute are needed.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) D becomes 3 times smaller
yechim.ovoz: The correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: t is in the denominator of the fraction. When the denominator increases, the fraction decreases, it does not increase.
xatolar.2: “3 times smaller” and “decreases by 3” are not the same: D is divided by three, not reduced by 3.
xatolar.3: t appears in the formula, so when it changes, D changes too.

kunikma: Expressing an unknown quantity from a formula and substituting values
usul: Express V from the formula: $V = \dfrac{60 \cdot t \cdot D}{k}$, then substitute the numbers.

We substitute the given values.
One tree gets 3 liters of water.

He subtracted one of the prices instead of adding it

If the last zero of the earbuds price is dropped, it becomes 15 700.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) Left out the last digit
yechim.ovoz: The correct answer is C.

kunikma: Expressing a percentage markup with an algebraic formula

4) $u = 0.75s$

kunikma: Calculating a percentage difference in a real-life situation
usul: Find the difference and divide it by the mass of the smaller egg (the one being compared with).

yechim.ovoz: First we find the difference between the masses of the two eggs.
“By what percentage heavier than the first” means compared with the first egg.
The second egg is 25% heavier.

kunikma: Calculating a number by applying a percentage increase and decrease in turn
usul: First find how many chicks were added during the year, then subtract 25% of the total.

variantlar.savol:
Nodira wants to calculate how the size of the colony changes in one year. She made the following assumptions:
• At the beginning of the year, there are 2 000 pelicans (1 000 pairs) in the colony.
• Each pair raises one chick in the spring.
• By the end of the year, 25% of all the pelicans (adults and chicks) die.

How many pelicans (adults and chicks) will there be in the colony at the end of the first year?

yechim.ovoz: Each of the 1 000 pairs raises one chick.
After the spring there are 3 000 pelicans in the colony.
If 25% die, 75% remain.
At the end of the year there will be 2 250 pelicans.

xatolar.umumiy: Common mistakes: taking the number of chicks as 2 000 (one per pelican); subtracting 25% from the adults only (2 500); writing the number of pelicans that died (750) as the answer.

variantlar.maslahat: Carry out successive changes in order: first the increase, then the decrease.

kunikma: Choosing an exponential model that fits the situation
usul: Write what happens in one year as factors: the number of pairs is half the number of pelicans, so the growth factor is 1.5; 25% die, so 0.75 remain.

variantlar.savol:
Nodira assumes that the colony will keep changing in the same way in the following years:
• At the beginning of each year, there are equal numbers of male and female pelicans in the colony, and they form pairs.
• Each pair raises one chick in the spring.
• By the end of each year, 25% of all the pelicans die.
• One-year-old pelicans also raise chicks.

Which formula gives the number of pelicans P after 5 years?

yechim.ovoz: One chick for every two pelicans: the number grows 1.5 times.
At the end of the year, 75% remain.
Each year the number is multiplied by 1.5 · 0.75 = 1.125.
We multiply five years in a row.
The correct formula is B.

xatolar.0: 0.25 is the share of pelicans that die. The share that survives to the next year is 0.75.
xatolar.2: 1.25 is wrong: there is one chick for every two pelicans, so the number grows by half — 1.5 times.
xatolar.3: Both factors are wrong: the growth is 1.5 times, and the surviving share is 0.75.

variantlar.maslahat: For a quantity that is multiplied by the same factor every year, the formula is: starting number · (factor)^years.

kunikma: Analyzing which conclusions follow from the given information
usul: For each statement, find the line you need and calculate. Try converting “95% of the year” into days.

variantlar.savol:

1) Building four turbines costs more than 140 billion soums in total.

Statement 4: the downtime is about 18 days, not 95 days — No.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) Yes, Yes, No, No
yechim.ovoz: The correct row is C.

xatolar.0: 27 : 450 = 6%, so statement 3 is false.
xatolar.1: The maintenance cost is given “per 1 kWh”, so it depends on the energy produced — statement 2 is true.
xatolar.3: 4 · 36 = 144 billion > 140 billion, so statement 1 is true. 95% is a share of time, not 95 days.

kunikma: Setting up and solving a linear equation in context
usul: Covering the construction cost means that the financial profit F equals zero (or more). Solve the equation F = 0.

variantlar.savol:
To evaluate the profit, the district administration proposed the following formula for the financial profit F (billion soums) over y years:

$F = 4y - 36$

(4y is the profit from yearly electricity production, 36 is the construction cost of the turbine)

According to the formula, for at least how many years must the turbine operate to cover the construction cost?

yechim.ovoz: When the cost is covered, the profit equals zero.
We move 36 to the right-hand side.
We divide both sides by 4.
The correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: After 8 years, F = 4 · 8 − 36 = −4 billion — the cost has not been covered yet.
xatolar.2: 32 = 36 − 4 — subtracting the numbers makes no sense. Solve the equation: 4y = 36.
xatolar.3: 40 = 36 + 4 — you need to divide, not add: 36 : 4 = 9.

variantlar.maslahat: “The cost is covered” means the moment when the profit equals zero.

The turbines are planned to be built on a square plot with sides of 600 m. According to the building rules, the distance between two towers must be at least 5 times the blade length. The picture shows the layout proposed by the district administration.

Why does this proposal not meet the rule?

kunikma: Multi-step modeling: circumference, speed and unit conversion
usul: In one revolution, the tip of a blade travels along a circle with a radius of 45 m: $2\pi r$. 15 revolutions per minute gives the distance per minute. Then convert m/min to km/h (× 60 : 1000).

variantlar.savol: When the SH-90 blades move at maximum speed, how many kilometers per hour do their tips travel? Give your answer in km/h, rounded to the nearest whole number ($\pi \approx 3.14$).

yechim.ovoz: The blade tip traces a circle with a radius of 45 m.
It turns 15 times per minute.
There are 60 minutes in an hour.
The blade tips move at about 254 km per hour.

xatolar.umumiy: Common mistakes: using $\pi r$ with the radius instead of the diameter (127); not converting m/min to km/h (4 239); taking the tower height as the radius.

variantlar.maslahat: In circular motion, the distance traveled in one revolution is the circumference $2\pi r$.

kunikma: Calculating a percentage increase in a real-life situation
usul: To increase a quantity by p%, multiply it by (1 + p/100).

variantlar.savol: The kite flies at a height of 100 m. There, the wind speed is about 30% higher than on the deck of the barge. If the wind speed on the deck is 20 km per hour, about how fast is the wind hitting the kite?

yechim.ovoz: First we find the extra speed.
We add it to the speed on the deck.
In one step: multiply by 1.3.
The correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: 6 km/h is only the extra speed. It needs to be added to 20 km/h.
xatolar.1: 3 was added to 20. 30% is 0.3 of 20, that is, 6.
xatolar.3: 20 + 30 = 50: you cannot add a percentage to a unit.

variantlar.maslahat: A number increased by p% = number · (1 + p/100).

variantlar.savol: For the kite to pull the barge at a 45° angle and be at a height of 120 m, about how long should the rope be?

The rope is the hypotenuse.

kunikma: Modeling costs and savings to find the payback period
usul: Find the yearly diesel cost, calculate 15% of it (the savings) and divide the price of the kite by the yearly savings. Ignore unnecessary information.

variantlar.savol:
Information about the barge “Termez-1”:
Length: 85 m
Cargo capacity: 1 500 tonnes
Diesel consumption per year (without a kite): 400 000 liters

1 liter of diesel costs 12 000 soums. The kite reduces diesel consumption by about 15%. Installing a kite on the barge costs 5.4 billion soums.

What is the minimum number of full years needed for the money saved on diesel to fully cover the price of the kite?

yechim.ovoz: The yearly diesel cost without a kite is 4.8 billion soums.
The kite saves 720 million soums a year.
We divide the price of the kite by the yearly savings.
In 7 years the cost is not fully covered yet; in 8 years it is.
At least 8 full years are needed.

xatolar.umumiy: Common mistakes: rounding 7.5 down and writing 7; using the whole diesel cost instead of 15% (1–2 years); mixing up liters and soums.

variantlar.maslahat: Payback period = initial cost : yearly savings. If “full years” are asked for, round up.

kunikma: Scaling up a recipe using a ratio (proportion)
usul: First find how many times larger the new amount is than the old one, then multiply each ingredient by that number.

variantlar.savol: Malika wants to make 300 ml of dressing using this recipe. How many milliliters of yogurt will she need?

yechim.ovoz: The dressing needed is 1.5 times the amount in the recipe.
Each ingredient is also multiplied by 1.5, so the yogurt is 180 ml.
The lemon juice is 75 ml and the oil is 45 ml, 300 ml in total — correct.
Malika needs 180 ml of yogurt.

xatolar.umumiy: A common mistake is to add 100 ml to the yogurt because 100 ml is being added to the total (220 ml), or to add 50 to 120. To keep the ratio the same, every ingredient is multiplied by the same number.

kunikma: Calculating a length from information in a drawing (diameter, radius, height)
usul: The center is one radius below the highest point. Half of the diameter is the radius.

variantlar.savol: In the drawing, the letter M marks the center of the Ferris wheel. How many meters above the water level is point M?

yechim.ovoz: The radius is half the diameter — 30 meters.
The center is one radius below the highest point.
Going one radius up from the lowest point also gives 36 m.
Point M is 36 meters above the water level.

xatolar.umumiy: A common mistake is 66 − 60 = 6 (subtracting the diameter) or 66 : 2 = 33 (dividing the height in half). It cannot be 33 m, because the wheel starts 6 m above the water.

variantlar.maslahat: The center is halfway between the highest and lowest points: (66 + 6) : 2.

kunikma: Finding a position over time in uniform rotation (a fraction of a circle)
usul: Find what fraction of a full turn the given time is, and mark that fraction in the direction of rotation.

variantlar.savol: The Ferris wheel turns at a constant speed and makes one full turn in exactly 24 minutes. Sardor got into a cabin at point P. Where will Sardor be 18 minutes later?

yechim.ovoz: 18 minutes is three quarters of a full turn.
With every quarter turn, the cabin reaches the next letter: Q, R, S.

yechim.doska: In 18 minutes: P → Q → R → S
yechim.ovoz: After three quarters, Sardor will be exactly at point S.
The correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: Point R is reached after half a turn (12 minutes); after 18 minutes the cabin has already gone past it.
xatolar.1: The cabin is between R and S from minute 12 to minute 18; at minute 18 it reaches S exactly.
xatolar.3: Between S and P corresponds to the time between 18 and 24 minutes; in that case the time would have to be more than 3/4 of a turn.

variantlar.maslahat: Write the time as a fraction: 18/24 = 3/4 — that is three quarters of a turn.

kunikma: Visualizing a 3D structure from another side (from above)
usul: From above, only the top die of each column can be seen. Its top face is opposite its bottom face: top = 7 − bottom.

variantlar.savol: How many dots in total can be seen when the structure is viewed from above?

yechim.ovoz: Only the top die of each column is visible; the other 3 are hidden.
Opposite faces add up to 7, so we find the top face.
Column 1: 7−2=5, column 2: 7−6=1, column 3: 7−3=4, column 4: 7−4=3.
In total, 13 dots are visible from above.

xatolar.umumiy: Common mistakes: adding the bottom faces (2+6+3+4 = 15) or counting all 7 dice. From above, only 4 top faces are visible, and they are opposite the bottom faces.

variantlar.maslahat: First count how many dice are visible from above, then for each one subtract the bottom face from 7.

kunikma: Finding a daily average from a total and a range of dates
usul: First count exactly how many days are in the date range (take into account the number of days in each month), then divide the total by the number of days.

variantlar.savol: Every year the trail is open from July 1 to August 31 (both days included). During this period, about 31 000 people climb to the peak. About how many people climb it per day on average?

yechim.ovoz: First we count how many days the trail is open.
We divide the total by the number of days.
On average, 500 people climb it per day.

xatolar.0: 50 — a place value was lost in the division (31 000 : 620).
xatolar.2: 1000 is the result of dividing 31 000 by the 31 days of only one month, but the trail is open for two months.
xatolar.3: 15 500 is the number of people per month (31 000 : 2), not per day.

variantlar.maslahat: If the question asks “per day”, the divisor is the number of days, not months.

kunikma: Finding a start time from two different speeds, a distance and an end time
usul: Calculate the time going up and the time coming down separately (t = s : v), add them, and count back from the end time.

variantlar.savol: The trail to the peak is about 6 km long. Hikers on the 12 km round-trip hike must be back by 19:00. Aziz estimates that he will walk up at an average speed of 1.2 km per hour and come down twice as fast (these speeds include time for rest and meals). What is the latest time Aziz can start the hike to be back by 19:00? (Write the answer as hours:minutes, like 08:15.)

yechim.ovoz: For the time going up, we divide the distance by the speed.
The speed coming down is twice as high, so the time is half as long.
The whole hike takes seven and a half hours.
We count back from the end time.
Aziz must set off at 11:30 at the latest.

xatolar.umumiy: Common mistakes: dividing 12 km by one speed (12 : 1.2 = 10 hours → 09:00), taking the speed coming down as slower instead of twice as fast, or reading 7.5 hours as 7 hours 50 minutes.

variantlar.maslahat: 0.5 hours = 30 minutes. Calculate the times going up and coming down separately.

kunikma: Dividing a length given in kilometers and converting the result to centimeters
usul: First convert the distance to centimeters (1 km = 100 000 cm), then divide by the number of steps.

variantlar.savol: Aziz wore a step counter (pedometer) on the hike. On the 6 km trail to the peak, the pedometer showed 12 000 steps. What was Aziz's average step length on the way up, in centimeters?

yechim.ovoz: We convert the distance to centimeters right away.
We divide the distance by the number of steps.
With half-meter steps we get 6 km — it matches.
The average step length is 50 cm.

xatolar.umumiy: Often the answer is left in meters (0.5) or the units are converted incorrectly (5 or 5000). Remember that 1 m = 100 cm and 1 km = 1000 m.

variantlar.maslahat: Check whether the result is realistic: an adult's step is usually 40–80 cm.

kunikma: Comparing average speeds using distance and time
usul: Calculate the speed for each part in the same units (for example, km/h), or compare the ratios of distance and time.

variantlar.savol: On one trip, Dilnoza rode 3 km in the first 12 minutes and 1.5 km in the next 6 minutes. Which of the following statements is correct?
javoblar: Dilnoza's average speed was greater in the first 12 minutes than in the next 6 minutes.
Dilnoza's average speed was the same in the first 12 minutes and in the next 6 minutes.
Dilnoza's average speed was smaller in the first 12 minutes than in the next 6 minutes.
Nothing can be said about the average speed from the given information.

yechim.ovoz: 12 minutes is one fifth of an hour: 3 · 5 = 15.
6 minutes is one tenth of an hour: 1.5 · 10 = 15.
Half the distance in half the time — the speed did not change.
The correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: 3 km is more than 1.5 km, but the time is also twice as long — you cannot compare speeds using distance alone.
xatolar.2: 6 minutes is a short time, but the distance is also half as long, so the speed neither decreased nor increased.
xatolar.3: The distance and time are known — the average speed can be calculated exactly.

variantlar.maslahat: Speed = distance : time. If both the distance and the time change by a factor of two, the speed does not change.

kunikma: Calculating time from average speed and distance
usul: Time = distance : speed. Convert the result from hours to minutes (1 hour = 60 minutes).

variantlar.savol: Dilnoza rode 5 km to her grandmother's house. The speedometer showed that her average speed for the whole trip was 20 km/h. Which of the following statements is correct?
javoblar: Dilnoza got to her grandmother's house in 4 hours.
Dilnoza got to her grandmother's house in 15 minutes.
Dilnoza got to her grandmother's house in 25 minutes.
It is impossible to determine how long it took Dilnoza to get to her grandmother's house.

yechim.ovoz: To find the time, we divide the distance by the speed.
A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes.
The correct answer is B.

xatolar.0: 4 hours is the result of dividing the speed by the distance (20 : 5); at that rate the cyclist would have been very slow.
xatolar.2: 25 minutes is the result of adding 5 and 20; adding the numbers does not give the time.
xatolar.3: If the average speed and the distance are known, the time can be found exactly.

variantlar.maslahat: Look at the units: if you divide km by km/h, you get hours.

kunikma: Calculating the average speed for a two-part journey from the total distance and total time
usul: Average speed = total distance : total time. Do not take the arithmetic mean of the two speeds.

variantlar.savol: Dilnoza rode her bicycle to the bazaar, 5 km from her home, in 12 minutes. She came home by a shorter 4 km route, which took 8 minutes. What was Dilnoza's average speed for the round trip to the bazaar, in km/h?

yechim.ovoz: We add up the distance for the whole trip.
The total time is 20 minutes, which is one third of an hour.
We divide the total distance by the total time.
The average speed is 27 km/h.

xatolar.umumiy: A common mistake is to take the average of the two speeds: 25 km/h going there and 30 km/h coming back, (25 + 30) : 2 = 27.5. This is wrong, because the parts have different distances and times.

variantlar.maslahat: Always calculate average speed as “total distance : total time”.

kunikma: Calculating a value using a table of several criteria and comparing it with a price
usul: For each criterion, determine which column the value from the listing falls into, then add the base price and the extras.

variantlar.savol:
Kamola contacted a professional appraiser. The appraiser calculates the value of the apartment using the following criteria:

Base price: 9 million soums per 1 m².
Travel time to the center: more than 15 minutes — +0; from 5 to 15 minutes — +20 million; less than 5 minutes — +40 million soums.
Distance to the water (straight line): more than 2 km — +0; 1–2 km — +10 million; 0.5–1 km — +25 million; less than 0.5 km — +40 million soums.
Parking: no — +0; yes — +50 million soums.

If the appraiser's valuation is higher than the price in the listing, the price is considered “very good” for the buyer.

According to the appraiser's criteria, what is the value of the apartment in millions of soums? (Write only the number.)

yechim.ovoz: Base price: we multiply the area by the price per 1 m².
12 minutes is in the 5–15 range, and 800 m is in the 0.5–1 km range.
There is also an extra amount for parking.
The valuation is 527 million, which is more than the 520 million in the listing — the price is “very good”.
The appraiser's valuation is 527 million soums.

xatolar.umumiy: Common mistakes: putting 800 m in the “less than 0.5 km” column (+40), forgetting one of the extras, or stopping at 48 · 9 = 432. Mark each criterion separately.

variantlar.maslahat: 800 m = 0.8 km. Find each criterion in the table separately and write them down as a list.

kunikma: Understanding what an average means and what it does not guarantee
usul: The average is the number you would get if the total days were shared equally among the years. Individual years can be above or below it; if some years are above the average, others must be below it.

variantlar.savol:
“240 days per year on average” is the average number of booked days over the last 8 years (assume a year has 365 days).

1) It can be said for certain that in at least one year the apartment was booked for exactly 240 days.
2) In theory, the apartment could have been booked for more than 240 days in each of the last 8 years.
3) In theory, the apartment could have had no bookings at all in one of the last 8 years.

Does each statement follow from the given information (“Yes”) or not (“No”)? Choose the row with the correct answers.

yechim.ovoz: If the average is 240, the total number of booked days over 8 years is 1920.

yechim.doska: 1) No: for example, years with 230 and 250 days
yechim.ovoz: The average can be 240 even if no single year is exactly 240.
If every year were more than 240, the average would also be more than 240.
The other 7 years can easily cover the 1920 days.
The correct row is B.

xatolar.0: Statement 1 is not guaranteed: even if the average is 240, it is possible that no year is exactly 240; and statement 3 is possible.
xatolar.2: Statement 2 is impossible: if all years were more than 240, the average would also be more than 240.
xatolar.3: Statements 1 and 2 are false and statement 3 is true — this row has everything the other way around.

variantlar.maslahat: Think of the average as “total : number of years” and check each statement against the total of 1920 days.

kunikma: Calculating and comparing numbers in an everyday situation
usul: First subtract the membership card and find the number of visits; then multiply that number by the non-member price.

variantlar.savol: Last year Bekzod was a member of the pool. During the year he spent a total of 560 000 soums, including the membership card. If he had not been a member and had gone to the pool the same number of times, how many soums would he have spent?

yechim.ovoz: First we subtract the price of the membership card.
The rest of the money was spent on visits — 40 visits.
Without membership, each visit costs 15 000 soums.
Bekzod would have spent 600 000 soums.

xatolar.umumiy: Common mistakes: calculating 560 000 : 12 000 without subtracting the membership card, or writing the number of visits (40) as the answer. The question asks for the total cost without membership.

variantlar.maslahat: Total cost = card + visits. First find the number of visits.

kunikma: Comparing two ways of paying and finding the smallest whole number for which one is cheaper
usul: Find the savings per visit and divide the price of the card by those savings; round the result to a whole number that makes sense in the situation.

variantlar.savol: What is the minimum number of times a person must go to the pool in a year for membership to pay off (that is, for a member to pay less than a non-member)?

yechim.ovoz: On each visit, a member saves 3000 soums.
To cover the price of the card, 26.7 visits are needed.
With 26 visits, a member still pays more.
With 27 visits, a member pays less.
You need to go at least 27 times.

xatolar.umumiy: A common mistake is to round 26.7 down and say 26. The number of visits must be a whole number, and to get a benefit you need to round up; with 26 visits a member still pays 2000 soums more.

variantlar.maslahat: After rounding, check your answer with both prices.

kunikma: Finding the whole from a percentage (proportion) using data in a table
usul: Households with a TV are 85% of all households. To find the whole from a part, divide the part by the percentage written as a decimal.

variantlar.savol: According to the table, 85.0% of all households in the Navoi Region have a TV. Which is the closest estimate of the total number of households in the Navoi Region?

yechim.ovoz: 240 thousand is 85 percent of all households.
To find the whole, we divide.
There must be more households in total than households with a TV — it matches.
The correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: 204 thousand is the result of multiplying 240 by 0.85; this number is smaller than 240, but the whole must be larger than the part.
xatolar.1: 255 thousand is as if 15 thousand, not 15%, were added to 240; the percentage must be applied correctly.
xatolar.3: 325 thousand is too large: 85% of 325 is 276 thousand, not 240 thousand.

variantlar.maslahat: If a part is given as a percentage, whole = part : (percentage/100). The whole is always larger than the part.

kunikma: Telling percentages and absolute numbers apart; understanding what whole a percentage refers to
usul: To find the number of subscribers, multiply the percentage by the correct whole — the number of households with a TV — and compare.

variantlar.savol:
Looking at the Fergana and Khorezm regions, Otabek said: “In both regions the percentage of households with a TV is almost the same, and the IPTV percentage is higher in Khorezm. So more households subscribe to IPTV in Khorezm than in Fergana.”

Why is Otabek's reasoning wrong? Choose the best explanation.
javoblar: The reasoning is wrong because the percentage of households with a TV in Fergana (97.0%) is higher than in Khorezm (95.5%).
The reasoning is wrong because the difference between 18% and 15% is only 3%, which is negligible.
The reasoning is wrong because the percentages refer to households with a TV, and Fergana has many more such households: about 121.5 thousand versus 70.2 thousand subscribers.
The reasoning is correct because 18% is greater than 15%.

yechim.ovoz: We calculate the number of subscribers in Fergana.
In Khorezm the percentage is higher, but the whole is much smaller.
Fergana has more subscribers — Otabek made a mistake.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) the percentages are of different wholes
yechim.ovoz: The correct explanation is C.

xatolar.0: The difference of 1.5 percentage points (97.0 and 95.5) is not decisive here; the main reason is the large difference in the number of households with a TV.
xatolar.1: Calling a 3-point difference negligible is also wrong: even when the percentages are equal, the number of subscribers depends on the whole.
xatolar.3: Otabek's reasoning is wrong: even though the percentage is higher, 18 percent of a small whole is less than 15 percent of a large whole.

variantlar.maslahat: Before comparing percentages, always ask: “This is a percentage — of what?”

kunikma: Choosing an item from a table that meets several conditions at the same time
usul: Check each condition in turn and cross out the ones that do not meet it.

yechim.ovoz: Sayyor has 118 000 km on it.
Tulpor was made in 2016.
Lola costs 98 million soums.
Only Bahor meets all three conditions.

xatolar.0: Lola is the newest and has the lowest mileage, but its price is 98 million — more than 90 million.
xatolar.2: Sayyor is cheaper, but it has 118 000 km on it — more than 100 000 km.
xatolar.3: Tulpor is the cheapest, but it was made in 2016 — before 2017.

variantlar.maslahat: Check the conditions one by one: if a car fails one condition, it is out.

kunikma: Comparing decimals and finding the smallest
usul: Write the decimals with the same number of decimal places (1.490; 1.496; 1.520; 1.487) and compare them place by place.

variantlar.savol: Which car has the smallest engine size?

yechim.ovoz: We write all the numbers as decimals with three decimal places.

yechim.doska: Ones and tenths: all are 1.4.. or 1.5..
yechim.ovoz: 1.520 is the largest — it is out.
1.487 has the smallest hundredths digit.
Tulpor has the smallest engine size.

xatolar.0: 1.49 looks small because it is written with fewer digits, but it equals 1.490 and is greater than 1.487.
xatolar.1: 1.496 has more digits, but a longer number is not necessarily larger or smaller: 1.496 > 1.487.
xatolar.2: 1.52 is the largest number, because it has 5 in the tenths place.

variantlar.maslahat: When comparing decimals, add zeros at the end to make the number of decimal places equal.

kunikma: Calculating a percentage (a decimal percentage) of a large number
usul: 3.5% = 0.035. Multiply the price by 0.035, or first find 1% and then 3.5%.

variantlar.savol: To register the car, Shahzoda must pay an extra fee equal to 3.5% of its price. How many soums will the extra fee be for the Lola car?

yechim.ovoz: We write the price in soums.
We divide by one hundred to find one percent.
We multiply one percent by 3.5.
The extra fee is 3 430 000 soums.

xatolar.umumiy: Common mistakes: taking 3.5% as 0.35 (34 300 000) or writing 98 · 3.5 = 343 as soums. The answer is asked for in soums; 3.43 million soums is also correct.

variantlar.maslahat: Converting a percentage to a decimal: 3.5% = 3.5 : 100 = 0.035.

variantlar.savol: The drawing gives the dimensions (in meters) of the shed Ravshan chose. The roof consists of two identical rectangular pieces. Find the total area of the roof (in m²).

kunikma: Calculating income in a piecewise (two-rate) payment model
usul: Split the orders into two parts: the first 40 and the rest; multiply each part by its own rate.

variantlar.savol: Ulugbek delivers an average of 55 orders per week for “Fast Delivery”. How many soums does he earn per week on average?

yechim.ovoz: The first 40 orders are paid at the lower rate.
Another 15 orders are paid at the higher rate.
For them, he gets 75 000 soums.
We add both parts.
Ulugbek earns 195 000 soums per week.

xatolar.umumiy: Common mistakes: multiplying all the orders by one rate (55 · 3000 = 165 000 or 55 · 5000 = 275 000) or calculating 40 · 3000 + 55 · 5000. The higher rate applies only to the orders after the first 40.

variantlar.maslahat: Count the “first 40” orders and the “later” orders separately.

kunikma: Finding an unknown quantity from a linear model (working backward)
usul: Subtract the fixed part from the income and divide the rest by the pay per order.

variantlar.savol: Nodira works for “Easy Courier”. In one week she earned 240 000 soums. How many orders did she deliver that week?

yechim.ovoz: Income = fixed pay + pay for orders.
We subtract the fixed 150 000 soums.
We divide by the pay per order.
Nodira delivered 60 orders.

xatolar.umumiy: A common mistake is to calculate 240 000 : 1500 = 160 without subtracting the fixed 150 000 soums.

variantlar.maslahat: First subtract the fixed part, then divide. Check your answer: 150 000 + 60 · 1500.
