yechim.doska: Price is constant within an interval
yechim.ovoz: For example, 300 g and 480 g cost the same — 15 000 soums.
Each interval is a horizontal segment on the graph.
When you move to the next interval, the price suddenly goes up — this makes a step.
This is graph B.

xatolar.0: A curve means the price rises slowly with every gram, but in fact the price does not change within an interval.
xatolar.2: The points show only the prices of certain masses; the prices of other masses in the intervals are not shown.
xatolar.3: A straight line means the price depends evenly on the mass — but in the table the price changes in jumps.

variantlar.maslahat: When turning a table into a graph, think about the values inside the intervals, not only the boundaries.

kunikma: Finding prices in a table and comparing two options
usul: Calculate the price of each option separately: two separate parcels, and one combined parcel (the sum of the masses).

variantlar.savol: Jasur wants to send his friend two items with masses of 300 g and 800 g. Is it cheaper to send them as two separate parcels or as one parcel? Which calculation is correct?
javoblar: Separately: 12 000 + 19 000 = 31 000 soums; together: 26 000 soums — together is cheaper
Separately: 15 000 + 19 000 = 34 000 soums; together: 38 000 soums — separately is cheaper
Separately: 15 000 + 19 000 = 34 000 soums; together: 26 000 soums — together is cheaper
Separately: 15 000 + 19 000 = 34 000 soums; together: 19 000 soums — together is cheaper

yechim.ovoz: Separately: 300 g is in the 251–500 interval, and 800 g is in the 501–1000 interval.
Two separate parcels cost 34 thousand soums.
1100 g falls in the 1001–2000 interval — 26 thousand soums.
One parcel is 8 thousand soums cheaper.
The correct calculation is C.

xatolar.0: 300 g is not in the “up to 250 g” interval; its price is 15 000 soums.
xatolar.1: 1100 g is in the 1001–2000 g interval, and its price is 26 000 soums, not 38 000.
xatolar.3: Sent together, the mass is 1100 g — that is more than 1000 g, so the price is 26 000 soums.

variantlar.maslahat: Be careful with interval boundaries: 300 g is not in the “up to 250 g” interval.

kunikma: Finding information by linking a date in the text with a value on a graph
usul: First find the year you need in the text, then look for that year on the horizontal axis of Figure 1 and read the height of the curve.

variantlar.savol: What was the approximate surface area of the Aral Sea in the year it split into two parts?
javoblar: The text and figures give no information about this

yechim.doska: Text: “In 1989, the sea split into two parts”
yechim.ovoz: First we find in the text the year the sea split in two: 1989.
Now we find the 1990 mark in Figure 1; 1989 is just slightly to the left of it.

yechim.doska: Height of the curve ≈ 40 thousand km²
yechim.ovoz: At that point the curve is close to 40, which means about 40 thousand square kilometers.
The information is there; you just had to combine it from two places: the text and the graph.

xatolar.1: 68 thousand km² is the area of the sea in 1960, before it began to shrink. The question is about 1989.
xatolar.2: 13 thousand km² is the value for about 2010. You read the wrong part of the graph.
xatolar.3: The information is there: the year is in the text, and the area is in Figure 1. You need to use them together.

variantlar.maslahat: If the question does not state the year, look for it in the text first, then go to the graph.

kunikma: Finding an unlabeled point by continuing the scale divisions on a graph axis
usul: Find the step between neighboring labels on the horizontal axis and count back to the left from the first label by that step.

variantlar.savol: In approximately what year does the graph in Figure 1 begin? Write the year as a number.

yechim.ovoz: The first year labeled on the horizontal axis is 1970. But the graph starts a little to the left of it.
The difference between neighboring marks is ten years.
The unlabeled mark one step to the left of 1970 corresponds to 1960.
So the graph begins in 1960.

xatolar.umumiy: Many students write the first label on the axis, 1970. The graph does not begin at a labeled mark but at the point one division to its left; you need to continue the step of the divisions.

variantlar.maslahat: When you are asked where a graph begins, look at the actual start of the line, not at the first number written.

kunikma: Using the text to evaluate why the author started the graph at this particular point
usul: Find what the text says about the year the graph begins, and think about what the author wants to show.

variantlar.savol: Why did the author start the graph in Figure 1 in this particular year?
javoblar: Because the Aral Sea came into being that year
Because the sea had its smallest area that year
Because from that year the water reaching the sea decreased and the sea began to shrink; before that, its area had hardly changed
Because flounder was brought to the sea that year

yechim.doska: Text: until the 1960s, area ≈ 68 thousand km²
yechim.ovoz: The text says that until the 1960s the area hardly changed.

yechim.doska: From that time, river water was diverted to the fields
yechim.ovoz: It was exactly then that water was diverted to the fields and the sea began to shrink.

yechim.doska: Purpose: to show the shrinking process from the start
yechim.ovoz: The author starts the graph at the point where the change began, to show the whole process.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) When the shrinking began
yechim.ovoz: The other options contradict the text or the graph.

xatolar.0: The Aral did not appear in 1960; it was a large lake even before that, as the text says.
xatolar.1: On the graph, the area in 1960 is the largest, not the smallest.
xatolar.3: Flounder was brought in the 1980s, not in 1960.

variantlar.maslahat: For a question about the author’s choice, ask yourself: “What changed before and after this point?”

kunikma: Identifying the hidden assumption a diagram is based on
usul: Read what source Figure 2 was made from, and think about what you must believe for that source to be accurate.

variantlar.savol: What assumption is Figure 2 based on?
javoblar: A fish species recorded in the reports really lived in the sea in those years
The fishermen were very experienced and skillful
The fishermen sailed to all parts of the sea
No one tried to breed these fish artificially

yechim.ovoz: Figure 2 is based on the species recorded in fishermen’s catches.

yechim.doska: In the report → assumed to be in the sea
yechim.ovoz: The figure relies on the idea that “if a species is in the report, it lived in the sea that year.”

yechim.doska: The others are not needed for the figure
yechim.ovoz: The fishermen’s skill or attempts at breeding do not affect what the figure shows.

yechim.doska: Answer: A) A recorded species lived in the sea
yechim.ovoz: Without this assumption, the bars in Figure 2 would mean nothing.

xatolar.1: The text says nothing about skill, and the figure does not depend on it.
xatolar.2: The figure title refers only to the southern part, not to all parts.
xatolar.3: Artificial breeding does not matter for the logic of the figure; in fact, flounder was brought in by people.

variantlar.maslahat: An “assumption” is an idea the author accepts as true without proving it. Ask what the diagram is based on.

kunikma: Drawing a conclusion by combining data from two diagrams over time
usul: First use Figure 2 to find when the fish disappeared, then find that year in Figure 1 and see what state the sea was in.

variantlar.savol: Use Figures 1 and 2 together for this question. When did carp, catfish, and roach disappear from the reports?
javoblar: In the year the sea began to shrink
In the middle of the period when the sea was at its largest
After the sea split into two parts
After the area of the sea had been decreasing for more than twenty years

yechim.ovoz: In Figure 2, the bars for these three species end shortly after 1980.
According to Figure 1, the sea has been shrinking since 1960.
So when the fish disappeared, the sea had been shrinking for more than twenty years.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) After more than 20 years of shrinking
yechim.ovoz: The split into two parts happened in 1989, after the fish had disappeared.

xatolar.0: The shrinking began in 1960, but the fish were recorded until the early 1980s.
xatolar.1: The sea was at its largest at the start of the graph, in 1960. The fish disappeared much later.
xatolar.2: The sea split in 1989, but these species are missing from the reports after 1982; the order is reversed.

variantlar.maslahat: When linking two graphs, use the shared axis, the years: find the same year in both figures.

kunikma: Finding specific information about the program in the notice
usul: Compare each option with the “When and where?” section of the notice: choose the one the text states exactly.

variantlar.savol: Which of the following is a feature of the school flu vaccination program?
javoblar: Sports sessions will be held every day during the winter
The vaccination will take place during school hours
People who get vaccinated will receive a small cash reward
The school doctor will give the vaccinations

yechim.doska: We read the “When and where?” section
yechim.ovoz: The features of the program are described in the “When and where?” section of the notice.

yechim.doska: “The vaccination will take place during school hours”
yechim.ovoz: The text contains exactly this sentence.

yechim.doska: A clinic nurse gives the vaccinations
yechim.ovoz: It is not a doctor but a nurse from the district clinic who gives the vaccinations; nothing is said about rewards or sports sessions.
Only this option is stated directly in the notice.

xatolar.0: The notice recommends being active, but it does not say the school will hold sessions.
xatolar.2: The vaccination is free, but nothing is written about a cash reward.
xatolar.3: The vaccinations are given by a nurse from the clinic, not by the school doctor.

variantlar.maslahat: Check every word in the option (who? when? where?) against the text: if even one word differs, the option is wrong.

kunikma: Evaluating the style and design of a text, not its content
usul: First decide whether the option is about WHAT the text says (content) or HOW it is written (style, picture, layout).

variantlar.savol: Dilnoza wanted the style of the notice to be friendly and encouraging. Which of the following statements best shows that the STYLE of the notice (not its content) is like this?
javoblar: The notice says the vaccination is free and takes place during lessons, which makes people interested
The notice gives a clear list of who should not be vaccinated
The notice uses warm appeals such as “Let’s … together,” headings in the form of questions, and a picture of a smiling Grandfather Frost
The notice can be trusted because it was written by a human resources officer

yechim.ovoz: Content is what the notice is about; style is the words, pictures, and structure used to write it.

yechim.doska: A and B are about content
yechim.ovoz: A free vaccination or a list is information, not style.

yechim.doska: C: tone of address, headings, picture
yechim.ovoz: Option C points to specific features of style: a warm tone, question headings, and a cheerful picture.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) Warm appeal, headings, picture
yechim.ovoz: Option D is about trusting the author, not about style.

xatolar.0: This is about the CONTENT of the notice: free and convenient timing is information. The question asks about style.
xatolar.1: A list is content; it shows clarity, not friendliness.
xatolar.3: Who the author is has nothing to do with style and does not show friendliness.

variantlar.maslahat: For a question about style, choose the answer that points to a specific feature of the text (words, headings, picture, layout).

kunikma: Drawing a conclusion from the relationship between two parts of a text
usul: Notice the words used to connect a healthy lifestyle and vaccination in the notice (“extra,” “the most reliable defense”).

variantlar.savol: According to the notice, what is vaccination like for someone who wants to avoid the flu?
javoblar: More effective than healthy eating and exercise, but more dangerous
A useful extra, but it does not replace healthy eating and exercise
As effective as a healthy lifestyle, and easier
Not needed at all if you exercise a lot and eat properly

yechim.doska: “The most reliable defense is a strong body”
yechim.ovoz: The notice presents a healthy body as the main protection.
Vaccination is called an extra option, which means it is not a replacement.

yechim.doska: So: useful, but not a replacement
yechim.ovoz: If we combine the two sentences, vaccination turns out to be a useful extra.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) An extra, not a replacement
yechim.ovoz: The other options compare the two methods incorrectly.

xatolar.0: The notice does not say vaccination is more effective, nor that it is dangerous; on the contrary, its side effects are mild.
xatolar.2: Vaccination is not described as equal or easier; it is presented as an extra.
xatolar.3: The notice recommends vaccination for everyone; it does not say it is unnecessary for healthy people.

variantlar.maslahat: Linking words such as “extra” or “in addition” show the relationship between two ideas.

kunikma: Finding an internal contradiction in a text to show that a sentence is misleading
usul: Compare the criticized sentence with other parts of the notice: does it contradict something said elsewhere?

variantlar.savol: The notice says: “Who can be vaccinated? Anyone who wants to be protected from the flu.” A colleague said this sentence is misleading. Which statement best supports what she said?
javoblar: Vaccination is voluntary, so no one can be ordered to get it
Later the notice says that some people (pregnant women, people allergic to eggs) should not be vaccinated, and “anyone” contradicts this
Some people are afraid of injections, so they will not be interested
The word “virus” should have been used instead of “flu”

yechim.ovoz: The sentence gives the impression that everyone can be vaccinated.

yechim.doska: The “Who should not be vaccinated?” section
yechim.ovoz: But further down it says that pregnant women, people with allergies, and people with a fever should not be vaccinated.

yechim.doska: Contradiction → the reader may be misled
yechim.ovoz: The two parts contradict each other, so the sentence really is misleading.
The other options do not explain the word “misleading.”

xatolar.0: The sentence is about a possibility, not an order; the style of the notice has been misunderstood.
xatolar.2: Fear of injections has nothing to do with whether the sentence is misleading.
xatolar.3: The choice of word does not change the meaning; the main problem is the internal contradiction.

variantlar.maslahat: To call something “misleading,” you need to find a clearly contradicting statement elsewhere in the text.

kunikma: Applying the conditions in the notice to specific situations and choosing the correct conclusion
usul: Compare each staff member’s situation with the rules in the notice: who exactly is advised to contact Dilnoza?

variantlar.savol: According to the notice, which of the following staff members should contact Dilnoza?
javoblar: Bahodir, the physics teacher: he does not want to be vaccinated and says his body will fight the flu on its own
Gulnora, the librarian: she wants to know whether vaccination is compulsory
Malika, the English teacher: she wants to be vaccinated, but she is expecting a baby in two months
Rustam aka, the security guard: he wants to be vaccinated, but he will be on vacation on November 14–18

yechim.doska: Notice: tell Dilnoza even if you cannot come
yechim.ovoz: The notice says that those who want to be vaccinated but cannot come that week should let Dilnoza know.

yechim.doska: Rustam aka is in exactly this situation
yechim.ovoz: He wants to be vaccinated and will be on vacation, so he should let her know about an extra day.

yechim.doska: Gulnora’s answer is in the text: “voluntary”
yechim.ovoz: The notice itself answers Gulnora’s question; Malika is pregnant, so she should not be vaccinated.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) Rustam aka, the security guard
yechim.ovoz: Bahodir does not want to be vaccinated, so he does not need to contact her.

xatolar.0: Bahodir does not want to be vaccinated, so he does not need to sign up with Dilnoza.
xatolar.1: The notice says that vaccination is voluntary; Gulnora can find the answer by reading it.
xatolar.2: Pregnant women should not be vaccinated; Malika needs a doctor’s advice, not to sign up.

variantlar.maslahat: In a situation question, check each person separately against the rule in the text and ask: “What does the text say for this person?”

kunikma: Identifying the shared purpose of texts
usul: Look at how both letters end: is the author urging us to do something or just giving information?

variantlar.savol: The purpose of both letters is to
javoblar: express an opinion about phones at school
show that phones are popular among students
say how much lost phones cost

yechim.ovoz: Madina expresses her opinion and asks the administration for a ban.
Jasur argues against the ban and makes his own proposal.

yechim.doska: In common: both express an opinion
yechim.ovoz: The letters disagree, but both have the same purpose: to state an opinion.
The other options are either just a small detail of the letters or not in them at all.

xatolar.0: The letters say nothing about how a phone works.
xatolar.2: The letters mention that phones are used a lot, but that is an example, not the purpose.
xatolar.3: Lost phones are one of Madina’s arguments, and no price is mentioned.

variantlar.maslahat: For a question about purpose, look at the concluding part of the text: what is the author asking for?

kunikma: Understanding the role of a comparison the author makes
usul: Read what Jasur says right after he talks about the calculator: what is he comparing the calculator to?

variantlar.savol: Why does Jasur mention the calculator?
javoblar: To say that calculators should also be banned at school
To tell the story of his grandfather’s school years
To show that, just as a device that was once banned later became an ordinary tool in lessons, a phone can also be useful
To prove that a phone has a calculator in it

yechim.doska: The calculator was also banned at first
yechim.ovoz: Jasur quotes his grandfather: calculators were also banned at first.

yechim.doska: Today it is essential in lessons
yechim.ovoz: Now it is impossible to imagine physics and chemistry lessons without one.
This comparison is an argument against banning phones: today’s ban may also turn out to be wrong later.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) Arguing against the ban through comparison
yechim.ovoz: It is a way of strengthening Jasur’s main idea.

xatolar.0: Jasur is not calling for calculators to be banned; on the contrary, he is showing how useful they are.
xatolar.1: His grandfather is only the source of the argument; the purpose is not to tell a memory.
xatolar.3: The letter does mention that a phone has a calculator, but here the calculator is brought up for comparison.

variantlar.maslahat: When asked “why does the author mention” something, look for a similarity between that thing and the main topic.

kunikma: Evaluating whether a personal opinion is supported with the text’s content in the student’s own words
usul: The task has two requirements: (1) use the CONTENT of the letter, (2) explain IN YOUR OWN WORDS. Find the answer that does both.

variantlar.savol: Students were given this task: “Which author do you agree with? Explain in your own words, using the ideas in the letters.” Which answer fully completes the task?
javoblar: “With Madina. School is a place for learning and making friends.”
“I agree with Jasur because he is right.”
“Madina’s letter is better because it is short and clearly written.”
“With Jasur: rather than banning phones completely, it is better to set out when and how they can be used in lessons; after all, they also have useful apps.”

yechim.doska: Requirement: use the content + own words
yechim.ovoz: The answer must be based on the content of the letter and express it in the student’s own words.
Answer A copies Madina’s sentence word for word; there is no opinion of the student’s own.

yechim.doska: B has no reason, C is about style
yechim.ovoz: B gives no argument at all, and C evaluates the writing style rather than the content.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) Supported in own words
yechim.ovoz: D restates Jasur’s proposal and argument in the student’s own words.

xatolar.0: Just a sentence copied word for word from the text is not an explanation in your own words.
xatolar.1: “He is right” is not an argument; it does not refer to any idea in the letter.
xatolar.2: This answer evaluates how the letter is written, but the question asks who you agree with.

variantlar.maslahat: Supporting an opinion is not just saying “I agree”: restate a specific argument from the letter in your own words.

kunikma: Evaluating a text by its writing style and structure, not its content
usul: Decide whether the answer is about agreeing with the author or about HOW the letter is written (structure, examples, tone).

variantlar.savol: Regardless of who you agree with, which letter is BETTER WRITTEN? Which of the following answers correctly evaluates a letter based on its writing style?
javoblar: “Jasur’s is better, because I also think banning phones is wrong.”
“Madina’s is better: she starts with specific scenes she has seen herself, gives her arguments one by one, and ends with a clear demand to the administration.”
“Jasur’s is better, because phones really are useful in lessons.”

yechim.ovoz: Here the question is not “who is right?” but “who wrote better?”

yechim.doska: A and D: agreeing with the content
yechim.ovoz: A and D say they agree with the author’s opinion; they do not evaluate the writing.

yechim.doska: B: structure and order of arguments
yechim.ovoz: B points to specific features of style: starting with an example, a sequence of arguments, and a clear conclusion.
C gives no reason at all.

xatolar.0: This is agreeing with an opinion, not a comment on how the letter is written.
xatolar.2: There is a judgment, but no reason for it.
xatolar.3: This is again about content, the usefulness of phones, not about writing style.

variantlar.maslahat: When evaluating style, answer the question “how?”: how does it begin, how does it present arguments, how does it end?

kunikma: Identifying the main division from the structure of a tree diagram
usul: Look at the two branches that come directly out of the top box.

variantlar.savol: Into which two main groups is the working-age population divided?
javoblar: Working age and outside working age

yechim.ovoz: At the top of the diagram is the working-age population: 1 980 thousand people.

yechim.doska: Two branches come out of it
yechim.ovoz: Two boxes come directly out of it: economically active and economically inactive.
Employed and unemployed is only the division of the economically active, one level lower.
The main division is the division at the top level.

xatolar.0: Employed and unemployed is a division within the economically active, not the main division.
xatolar.1: The diagram shows only people of working age; people outside that age are not in it.
xatolar.2: The division by full-time and part-time applies only to the employed, three levels lower.

variantlar.maslahat: In a tree diagram, the “main” division is the branches coming out of the top box.

kunikma: Reading a number in a diagram together with the unit given in a note
usul: Take the number from the box you need, then read the notes: what unit are the numbers given in?

variantlar.savol: How many people of working age were economically inactive? (Write the number of people, not the percentage.)

yechim.ovoz: In the diagram, the box for the economically inactive shows the number 673.2.
But according to Note 1, all the numbers are given in thousands.
So we multiply the number by a thousand: six hundred seventy-three thousand two hundred.
There are 673 200 economically inactive people.

xatolar.umumiy: The most common mistake is to write the number 673.2 from the box as it is. The note says the numbers are in thousands, so it must be multiplied by 1000. And 34.0% is a share, not a number of people.

variantlar.maslahat: In tables and diagrams, always check the unit in the title and notes (“thousand,” “million,” “%”).

kunikma: Applying the categories of a diagram and the definitions in its notes to real people
usul: For each person, ask in turn: (1) Are they aged 16–60? (2) Do they work? (3) If not, are they looking for work?

variantlar.savol:
Which part of the diagram does each of the following people belong to?
1) A 45-year-old businesswoman who works 60 hours a week.
2) A 20-year-old full-time student who is not looking for work.
3) A 30-year-old man who recently sold his shop and is looking for work.
4) A 52-year-old woman who has never worked outside the home and does not want to.
5) A 75-year-old grandmother who works a few hours a day in the family shop at the bazaar.
Key: B — “Active: employed,” I — “Active: unemployed,” N — “Not active (inactive),” X — “Does not belong to any category.” In which row are all of them correct?

yechim.doska: 1 works → B; 2 not seeking work → N
yechim.ovoz: The businesswoman is employed. The student is not looking for work, so according to the note she is inactive.
The man who sold his shop and is looking for work is unemployed, which means he is in the active group.
The 52-year-old woman is of working age but does not want to work, so she is inactive.
Even though the grandmother works, according to Note 2 she is outside working age, so she does not belong to any category.
Only in row C are all five people placed correctly.

xatolar.0: The grandmother works, but she is 75; according to Note 2 she is not part of the working-age population at all.
xatolar.1: The student is not looking for work, so she is not unemployed but inactive (see Note 3).
xatolar.3: The man looking for work is unemployed (active), and the 52-year-old woman is of working age, so she is inactive, not “does not belong.”

variantlar.maslahat: In a classification question, the definitions in the notes (the age limit, “not looking for work”) are the main key.

kunikma: Evaluating which parts of a diagram stay the same and which change
usul: Imagine you are making the diagram again every year: what would you rewrite, and what would stay the same?

variantlar.savol: Suppose a diagram like this is made every year. Which parts of the diagram would you expect to change from year to year?
javoblar: The labels in the boxes and the numbers
Everything: labels, numbers, percentages, and notes

yechim.ovoz: The labels in the boxes and the notes define the structure of the diagram; they do not change.
The number of people changes every year.

yechim.doska: Percentages are calculated from the numbers
yechim.ovoz: Since the percentages are calculated from the numbers, they change too.
So what changes is the numbers and the percentages.

xatolar.0: If the numbers change, the percentages calculated from them change too.
xatolar.2: If the labels changed, the years could not be compared; they stay the same.
xatolar.3: The notes give the definitions, which must be the same every year.

variantlar.maslahat: Learn to separate the data (numbers) from its “template” (labels, definitions).

kunikma: Evaluating a form of presenting information (a tree diagram) according to its purpose
usul: How is a tree diagram different from other forms (a line graph, a pie chart)? What does it show well?

variantlar.savol: This information could also have been presented as text, a pie chart, a graph, or a table. A tree diagram was probably chosen because it is especially useful for showing what?
javoblar: The total population of the region

yechim.doska: The diagram shows a single year
yechim.ovoz: The diagram is only about 2024; it does not show change over time.

yechim.doska: The total population is only in the text
yechim.ovoz: The total population, 3.2 million, is given in the text, not in the diagram.
Each branch of the tree divides a group into subgroups; this is its main advantage.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) Subgroups within a group
yechim.ovoz: Size is better shown by a pie chart or a bar chart.

xatolar.0: The diagram covers only one year; change is shown by a line graph.
xatolar.1: The total population is not in the diagram at all; it is in the text.
xatolar.3: The boxes are all the same size, so you cannot compare group sizes by eye.

variantlar.maslahat: When evaluating a form of presenting data, ask: “What does this form show better than the others?”

kunikma: Drawing a general conclusion by comparing one column of a table with the others
usul: Look down the Takhtakupyr column from top to bottom and compare it with the neighboring columns.

variantlar.savol: According to the table, how did the foundation’s activity in Takhtakupyr district in 2024 compare with the other districts?
javoblar: There was much less activity in Takhtakupyr
There was much more activity in Takhtakupyr
It was about the same as in the other districts
There was a lot in the “Living Conditions” section and little in the other sections

yechim.ovoz: In nine of the ten rows of the Takhtakupyr column, there is a zero.
Only one row, training mahalla activists, has a number: 86.

yechim.doska: In the other districts, all rows are filled
yechim.ovoz: In the other districts, almost every row has numbers.
So the activity in Takhtakupyr was very low compared with the others.

xatolar.1: The Takhtakupyr column has zeros almost everywhere; there was little activity, not a lot.
xatolar.2: The other districts have figures in the hundreds and thousands, but Takhtakupyr has almost none.
xatolar.3: Even in “Living Conditions” only one row is filled; the other three rows show zero.

variantlar.maslahat: Before drawing a conclusion about one column in a table, compare it row by row with the neighboring columns.

kunikma: Combining data from a table with an additional fact to evaluate a logical explanation of a situation
usul: Take all three pieces of information into account: (1) there was little activity, (2) the district is in great need, (3) the ONLY work done was training mahalla activists. Choose the explanation that fits all of them.

variantlar.savol: Suppose that in 2024 Takhtakupyr was the district most in need of help among these districts. Considering this fact and the data in the table, which explanation best accounts for the foundation’s activity in Takhtakupyr?
javoblar: Little work was done in Takhtakupyr because it needed help less than the other districts
The foundation may have only just started working in Takhtakupyr: it trained local activists first and plans to move on to other projects in the following years
The foundation should have given more help to Takhtakupyr
In Takhtakupyr, the foundation only trained mahalla activists

yechim.ovoz: We know from the first question that there was very little activity in Takhtakupyr.

yechim.doska: 2) The district is most in need (given)
yechim.ovoz: The question states that the district was most in need, so the reason cannot be “no help was needed.”
The only work done was training local activists; this is usually the first stage of a project.

yechim.doska: B: an explanation that fits all three facts
yechim.ovoz: Option B links all three pieces of information and offers a logical reason.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) The work had only just begun
yechim.ovoz: A contradicts the given information, C is an opinion rather than an explanation, and D just repeats the table.

xatolar.0: The question says Takhtakupyr was most in need; this explanation contradicts that.
xatolar.2: This is not an explanation but a personal opinion: it does not explain why little was done.
xatolar.3: This repeats a fact from the table and does not explain the reason.

variantlar.maslahat: In an “explain” question, the answer must not contradict any of the given facts and must answer the question “why?”

kunikma: Finding specific information in a comparison the author makes
usul: Read the section “Same ingredients, different proportions”: what exactly does it say makes the plovs different from each other?

variantlar.savol: To explain the pollen in honey, the author uses plov as an example. According to the article, how are different plovs different from each other?
javoblar: In the proportions of the ingredients
In the size of the pot
In the color of the ingredients

yechim.ovoz: The section heading itself points to the answer.
The text says that the plovs are made from the same ingredients but in different proportions.

yechim.doska: Same number: rice, meat, carrots, onions
yechim.ovoz: The number of ingredients is the same, four; nothing is said about the pot or color.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) In the proportions of the ingredients
yechim.ovoz: In the same way, honeys differ in the proportions of pollen types.

xatolar.0: The ingredients are said to be the same, so their number is the same too.
xatolar.2: The article says nothing about a pot.
xatolar.3: The text is about proportions, not color; the shape of pollen is mentioned in a different section.

variantlar.maslahat: For a question about a comparison, find the sentence where the comparison is made and read it word for word.

kunikma: Identifying the role of a separate section (box) in a text
usul: Look at what each sentence in the box is doing: is it a definition, a story, or a sequence of steps?

variantlar.savol: What is the purpose of the box “How is pollen analysis carried out?” What does it explain?
javoblar: How a honey sample is tested to find out its pollen content
How to prove that the seller is guilty

yechim.ovoz: The box describes the steps the lab technician carries out one after another.

yechim.doska: The result is compared with reference samples
yechim.ovoz: At the end, the result is compared with reference honeys.
The box explains how honey is tested and its pollen content determined.
The definition of pollen is elsewhere, in the side box.

xatolar.0: What pollen is appears in the side box and in the section “Honey is the signature of flowers,” not in this box.
xatolar.1: Plov is mentioned in another section, only as a comparison.
xatolar.3: On the contrary, the article says that a single analysis does not fully prove guilt.

variantlar.maslahat: To identify the role of a section, look at its heading and the general type of its sentences (steps, definition, example).

kunikma: Identifying the author’s main purpose
usul: What is the author doing in the article: frightening, amusing, explaining, or persuading the reader to do something?

variantlar.savol: What is the main purpose of the author of the article?

yechim.ovoz: This is a popular science article; it explains a method step by step.
The author tells us what pollen is, how it is tested, and what the limitations of the method are.
It does not urge anyone to do anything and does not frighten anyone.
The main purpose is to give the reader new knowledge.

xatolar.0: There is a story about fake honey, but the article focuses on explaining a method, not on warning about a danger.
xatolar.1: The plov comparison is interesting, but the purpose of the article is not to amuse.
xatolar.3: The author does not try to win the reader over to a view; on the contrary, he objectively points out the method’s limitations too.

variantlar.maslahat: To identify the author’s purpose, look at what most of the text is devoted to.

kunikma: Identifying which part of a text answers the question asked in the introduction
usul: Find what method is described in detail in the sections after the question in the introduction.

variantlar.savol: The introduction ends with the question “How can this be proven?” According to the article, what is done to find the answer to this question?
javoblar: The pollen in the honey is analyzed in a laboratory
The seller is questioned again and again
The taste of the honey is compared with honey from another bazaar

yechim.ovoz: The introduction ends with a question.

yechim.doska: The following sections: pollen and analysis
yechim.ovoz: The rest of the article is about pollen analysis.
The article says nothing about asking customers or comparing taste.
So the answer is pollen analysis in a laboratory.

xatolar.0: The article says nothing about other customers.
xatolar.2: The seller’s words are quoted once; nothing is said about questioning him.
xatolar.3: The article says plov can be told apart by taste, but that is only a comparison; honey is tested by its pollen, not its taste.

variantlar.maslahat: The question in an introduction usually announces the topic of the whole text; the answer comes in the following sections.

kunikma: Identifying the main idea of a text
usul: Look at the headline, the conclusion in the introduction, and the common topic of the sections of the article.

variantlar.savol: What does the author want to show in this article?
javoblar: That today’s backpacks are much better made than earlier ones
That younger students should be banned from carrying books
That most of the students at the school are ill
That it is very important for students to choose the right backpack and wear it properly

yechim.doska: Introduction: “what matters most is prevention and the right backpack”
yechim.ovoz: The author states the main idea right in the introduction.

yechim.doska: Sections: harm, criteria for choosing, daily habit
yechim.ovoz: The following sections are about the harm of a heavy load, the criteria for a good backpack, and daily advice.
All the sections show how important the right backpack and wearing it properly are.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) The right backpack matters
yechim.ovoz: The other options are not in the text or are not the main idea.

xatolar.0: The article says nothing about backpacks becoming better made.
xatolar.1: No ban is proposed; the article only advises not taking extra books.
xatolar.2: The article does not say that most students are ill; it only mentions the danger of a heavy load.

variantlar.maslahat: To find the main idea, pay attention to the headline and the conclusion in the introduction.

kunikma: Finding specific cause-and-effect information in a text
usul: In the section “Big or small?” find the sentence that begins with “If a backpack is too big.”

variantlar.savol: According to the article, why should a backpack not be too big?
javoblar: The books do not fit in it
Unnecessary things get put into it, so it becomes heavy and pulls the body backward
Its thin straps dig into the shoulders
The child has to carry some of the books by hand

yechim.ovoz: The place we need is the first sentence of the section “Big or small?”

yechim.doska: “…unnecessary things keep getting put into it, it gets heavier”
yechim.ovoz: Extra things get put into a big backpack; it gets heavy and pulls the body backward.

yechim.doska: “If it is too small…” is a different case
yechim.ovoz: Books not fitting and carrying them by hand are the problems of a small backpack.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) It gets heavy and pulls the body
yechim.ovoz: The point about straps belongs to a different criterion.

xatolar.0: This is the problem of a backpack that is too SMALL, not too big.
xatolar.2: Straps are discussed in the second criterion; they have nothing to do with the size of the backpack.
xatolar.3: Carrying books by hand also happens when a small backpack cannot hold them.

variantlar.maslahat: When a text describes two opposite cases (too big / too small), make sure you know which one the question is about.

kunikma: Finding the criteria listed in a text completely and correctly
usul: Find the sentences that begin with “First,” “Second,” “Third,” and “Finally,” and pick out the main idea of each.

variantlar.savol: The article says, “A good backpack should meet four requirements.” Which row gives these four requirements correctly?
javoblar: Size that matches height; wide, padded straps; firm, padded back panel; even distribution of the load
Packing only the next day’s books; wearing it on both shoulders; a waist belt; no more than 10 percent of body weight
Size that matches height; top edge not above the shoulders; bottom edge not below the waist; wide straps
Light weight; low price; attractive look; waterproof

yechim.ovoz: The first requirement is that the backpack should match the child’s height.
The second requirement is that the shoulder straps should be wide and padded.
The third requirement is that the back panel should have a firm base and soft padding.

yechim.doska: Finally: even distribution of the load
yechim.ovoz: The fourth requirement is distributing the load evenly.
In row C, one requirement is split into three parts, and row B gives other pieces of advice.

xatolar.1: These are other pieces of advice from the article (the daily habit, the 10 percent rule), not the four requirements.
xatolar.2: The shoulder and waist edges are details of the first requirement, not separate requirements; the fourth requirement is missing.
xatolar.3: None of these is mentioned in the article at all.

variantlar.maslahat: In a numbered list, separate the main idea of each item from its details.

kunikma: Identifying the logical relationship between two parts of a sentence
usul: Compare what the first part says (a problem?) and what the second part says (what to do about it?).

variantlar.savol:
The last sentence of the article is divided into two parts:
“To avoid small but annoying problems such as back and shoulder pain and getting tired quickly…” (first part)
“…every evening you should check your timetable, pack only the books for the next day’s lessons, and wear your backpack on both shoulders.” (second part)
What role does the second part play in relation to the first part?
javoblar: It states an idea that contradicts the first part
It repeats the first part in other words
It gives an example of the problem stated in the first part
It gives a solution to the problem stated in the first part

yechim.ovoz: The first part lists problems: pain and tiredness.
The words “to avoid” signal that a solution will follow.
The second part names specific actions; this is the solution.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) A solution to the problem
yechim.ovoz: There is no contradiction, repetition, or example.

xatolar.0: The second part does not deny the first; on the contrary, it continues it.
xatolar.1: The second part contains new information, what to do; it is not a repetition.
xatolar.2: The second part is not an example of the problem but measures against it.

variantlar.maslahat: Linking words such as “to…,” “so,” and “because” show the relationship between parts of a sentence.

kunikma: Understanding the situation at the beginning of a story
usul: Read only the first two paragraphs, and do not mix up the events that happen later with the situation at the start.

variantlar.savol: What situation is Grandma in at the beginning of the story?
javoblar: She has been hungry for several days, so she has no strength to leave the house
She is defending herself from a wild animal
Her house is snowed in and cut off from the outside world
An avalanche has destroyed her house

yechim.doska: Paragraph 1: “no road, and the phone was silent”
yechim.ovoz: The first paragraph says it has been snowing for three days and the road is closed.

yechim.doska: Paragraph 2: snow up to the windowsill
yechim.ovoz: The snowdrift has risen to the windowsill: the house is buried in snow.

yechim.doska: The wolf and hunger come later
yechim.ovoz: The wolf arrives in the middle of the night, and hunger is mentioned at noon; these are not the starting situation.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) Snowed in and cut off
yechim.ovoz: The story says nothing about the house collapsing.

xatolar.0: Grandma is hungry, but that is mentioned later, and it is the snow, not hunger, that keeps her from leaving the house.
xatolar.1: The wolf appears in the middle of the night, not at the beginning of the story.
xatolar.3: The house is still standing; nothing is said about an avalanche.

variantlar.maslahat: When the question says “at the beginning,” set aside later events and rely only on the first paragraphs.

kunikma: Working out the meaning of a character’s words from the context
usul: Think about when Grandma said these words, what she was holding at that moment, and what she planned to do afterward.

variantlar.savol: What did Grandma mean when she said, “first I’ll eat, and then I’ll take care of you too”?
javoblar: That she believed the wolf would not harm her
That she wanted to scare the wolf away
That she wanted to shoot the wolf
That she wanted to give the wolf some food too

yechim.doska: Context: in the morning she fired and missed
yechim.ovoz: Before these words, Grandma had tried to shoot the wolf but missed.

yechim.doska: After the meal: “picked up the rifle again”
yechim.ovoz: After the meal she picks up the rifle again: her plan has not changed.

yechim.doska: “Take care of you” here = finish you off
yechim.ovoz: Here the phrase means finishing something off; in this case, shooting the wolf.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) She wanted to shoot it
yechim.ovoz: The idea of feeding the wolf comes later, unexpectedly.

xatolar.0: Her hand trembles, which means she did not think the wolf was harmless.
xatolar.1: Grandma is not thinking about scaring the wolf off but about finishing it off for good.
xatolar.3: Later she does give it meat, but when she said these words she meant something else: the phrase “without quite understanding what she was doing” shows this.

variantlar.maslahat: To find the meaning of a phrase, look at what the character did before and after saying it.

kunikma: Evaluating how well the ending of a story fits the idea of the whole work
usul: The best answer links the last sentence not just to an event but to the main idea of the story (two hungry, lonely creatures understanding each other; generosity).

variantlar.savol: Four students commented on the last sentence of the story (“And on the threshold lay a piece of bone, gnawed clean and white”). Which comment explains most deeply how the last sentence is connected to the meaning of the story?
javoblar: “Yes, it fits: the white bone is a symbol showing that the wolf accepted Grandma’s generosity and that both of them survived hunger and loneliness, as if the “guest” in the title had left a sign for its host.”
“Yes, it fits: we find out that the wolf ate the meat.”
“No, it is too short: the rest of the story is written in detail, but the ending breaks off suddenly.”
“Yes, it fits: this sentence shows that it was all Grandma’s dream.”

yechim.doska: Idea of the story: two hungry, lonely creatures
yechim.ovoz: In the story, both Grandma and the wolf are hungry and alone; in the end, Grandma takes pity on it.

yechim.doska: The bone: a sign that generosity was accepted
yechim.ovoz: The bone, gnawed clean and white, means the wolf took the gift and left alive.

yechim.doska: B is only an event; C is only about style
yechim.ovoz: B only states an event, C is only about style, and D contradicts the story.

yechim.doska: Answer: A) Linked to a symbolic meaning
yechim.ovoz: A links the sentence to the main idea and the title of the story.

xatolar.1: This is true, but it only states the event, what happened; it does not explain the meaning of the sentence or its link to the idea.
xatolar.2: This evaluates the ending in terms of style, but does not connect it to the meaning and idea of the story.
xatolar.3: There is no hint of a dream in the story: the tracks and the bone show that the events really happened.

variantlar.maslahat: When evaluating an ending, ask yourself: “What does this sentence add to the main idea of the story?”

kunikma: Working out the literal meaning of a figurative expression
usul: Find the paragraph the sentence is in, and think about what “rose” means when it is said about a snowdrift.

variantlar.savol: “The snowdrift by the door rose to the windowsill in a single night.” What happened at this point in the story?
javoblar: The snow melted and turned into water
The snowdrift grew as high as the window
The door broke under the weight of the snow
A tree grew up beside the window

yechim.ovoz: Here “rose” means grew taller, grew.
The sentence is about the snowdrift: it grew during the night and reached the windowsill.

yechim.doska: Melting, breaking, a tree: not in the text
yechim.ovoz: At this point there is nothing about snow melting, the door breaking, or a tree.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) The snow piled up to window height
yechim.ovoz: This is personification: the snow is compared to a living thing that grows.

xatolar.0: On the contrary, the snow kept falling and piled up.
xatolar.2: This sentence says nothing about the door.
xatolar.3: The idea of growing might make you think of a tree, but the sentence is about the snowdrift.

variantlar.maslahat: In figurative expressions, identify who or what is being talked about (the subject).

kunikma: Understanding why the author chose particular descriptive language
usul: Notice the words used to describe the wolf’s sound (“as if … weeping,” “painful,” “weak and tired”), and remember how Grandma treated the wolf at the end of the story.

variantlar.savol: The wolf is first described in the story like this: “a long, painful sound, as if someone far away were moaning and weeping”; “weak and tired.” Considering the rest of the story, why did the author introduce the wolf with exactly this description?
javoblar: To make the reader feel pity for the wolf and to prepare for Grandma’s later kindness
To frighten the reader and show how evil the wolf is
To describe accurately that wolves really make this kind of sound
To tell the story from the wolf’s point of view

yechim.ovoz: These words suggest human suffering; they make us feel sorry, not afraid.

yechim.doska: Later: Grandma gives the wolf meat
yechim.ovoz: At the end of the story, Grandma takes pity on the wolf and gives it food.
So from the very beginning the author presents the wolf as deserving pity, preparing for the ending.

yechim.doska: Answer: A) To make us feel pity
yechim.ovoz: The idea of frightening the reader does not fit these words.

xatolar.1: Words such as “weeping” and “tired” express suffering, not evil.
xatolar.2: The description may be realistic, but the question asks about the author’s intention, its link to the rest of the story.
xatolar.3: The story is told from Grandma’s point of view, not the wolf’s.

variantlar.maslahat: Pay attention to the emotional tone of the words the author chose (pity, fear, joy), and compare it with the ending.

kunikma: Identifying the hidden reason for a character’s action
usul: Find what Grandma whispered after she threw the meat: in what way does she compare herself to the wolf?

variantlar.savol: According to the story, why did Grandma give the meat to the wolf?
javoblar: Because she thought that if she fed it, it would go away
Because she was very afraid of the wolf
Because she felt sorry for it and knew herself what it was like to be hungry
Because she wanted to tame the wolf and make it a pet

yechim.ovoz: Before giving the meat, Grandma’s fear had already disappeared.

yechim.doska: “I’ve been hungry for three days too”
yechim.ovoz: Grandma compares her own hunger with the wolf’s hunger.
So she fed the wolf because she felt sorry for it and sympathized with it.
The other options contradict the evidence in the text.

xatolar.0: The text does not say Grandma fed the wolf to make it leave; she gave the meat “without quite understanding what she was doing.”
xatolar.1: At that moment her fear had “vanished,” so it was not fear.
xatolar.3: There is no hint at all of making it a pet.

variantlar.maslahat: To find a character’s hidden reason, read their words and feelings before and after the action.

kunikma: Finding suitable evidence in a text for two opposing opinions
usul: In each pair, check two things: does evidence 1 really show cruelty, does evidence 2 show kindness, and are both actually in the story?

variantlar.savol:
Two students who read the story had an argument.
Student 1: “Grandma is a hard-hearted, cruel person.”
Student 2: “No, she is a very kind person.”
In which row is correct evidence from the story given for both opinions?
javoblar: Student 1: Grandma locked the wolf on the porch. Student 2: Grandma let it in through the door
Student 1: Grandma laughed as she thought about shooting the wolf. Student 2: Grandma promised to feed the wolf when she said, “then I’ll take care of you too”
Student 1: Grandma fired at the wolf from the window. Student 2: Grandma gave the wolf the last of her meat
Student 1: Grandma did not leave the village. Student 2: Grandma cried when she remembered her neighbors

yechim.doska: Evidence for opinion 1: she fired a shot
yechim.ovoz: The evidence for cruelty is that Grandma fired at the wolf from the window.

yechim.doska: Evidence for opinion 2: she gave the meat
yechim.ovoz: The evidence for kindness is that she gave the last of her meat to the hungry wolf.

yechim.doska: A, B, D: wrong or irrelevant
yechim.ovoz: The events in A are not in the story, the second piece of evidence in B misunderstands the phrase, and D is not evidence of cruelty.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) Fired a shot / gave meat
yechim.ovoz: In C, both pieces of evidence are in the story and fit the opinions.

xatolar.0: Locking the wolf out would be natural for her own safety, and letting it in through the door does not happen in the story at all.
xatolar.1: The first piece of evidence is correct, but the second is wrong: by “take care of you” she meant shooting the wolf, not feeding it.
xatolar.3: Not leaving the village does not show cruelty, so opinion 1 is not supported.

variantlar.maslahat: The evidence for each opinion must (1) be clearly in the story and (2) support that exact opinion.

kunikma: Understanding the main action of a dramatic excerpt (a character’s plan)
usul: Read the summary together with Malika’s lines: what does she want, and what does she ask Dildora to do to achieve it?

variantlar.savol: What is the excerpt about? Malika comes up with a plan ...
javoblar: to take Dildora on as an apprentice in the workshop.
to get her father-in-law to go back to selling pottery at the bazaar.
to use Dildora’s song to bring the master out of his grief and back to his work.
to persuade Dildora to stay and live in her house.

yechim.doska: Summary: the master has stopped turning the wheel
yechim.ovoz: First we read the summary: the master stopped working after his wife died.

yechim.doska: Malika: “wants to bring her father-in-law back to his work”
yechim.ovoz: Malika’s goal is stated openly here.

yechim.doska: Means: Dildora should sing “Among the Gardens”
yechim.ovoz: The plan is to have Dildora sing the song in her voice, which sounds like the late wife’s.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) bring the master back to work through the song
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is C.

xatolar.0: The excerpt says nothing about taking on an apprentice: Dildora is only asked to sing.
xatolar.1: The bazaar is only connected with Dildora’s job; there is no plan to send the master to the bazaar.
xatolar.3: The invitation to stay comes at the end of the excerpt, because the last bus has gone — it is not the aim of the plan.

variantlar.maslahat: The “Summary” section of a play is the key to understanding the events — don’t skip it.

kunikma: Analyzing the form of a text (structure of a play, stage directions)
usul: Stage directions are instructions for the actors and the technical crew. Look for how the lines in which no character speaks, and only actions or the setting are described, are set apart in the text.

variantlar.savol: Besides the words the actors say, the text of a play also contains instructions for the actors and the technical crew (stage directions). How can you recognize these instructions in Text 1?
javoblar: They are written in capital letters.
They are given in quotation marks.
They always start on a new line with the name of a character.

yechim.ovoz: In a stage direction nobody speaks; it only describes what is happening.

yechim.doska: (A courtyard. ... The sun is setting.) — in brackets
yechim.ovoz: The first stage direction is in brackets.
The small instructions within the lines are also in brackets.
Capital letters show who is speaking, not a stage direction.
The correct answer is A.

xatolar.1: The characters’ names (DILDORA, MALIKA) are written in capital letters — these are not stage directions.
xatolar.2: The quotation marks are used for the name of the song (“Among the Gardens”) and the title of the play.
xatolar.3: The lines that start with a character’s name are what the actors say (their lines).

variantlar.maslahat: Pay attention to the form of the text: the font, brackets and capital letters are the author’s signals to the reader.

kunikma: Connecting two texts: matching stage directions with the right theater job
usul: Use Text 2 to find the duties of each job (props master — objects that are moved, sound — effects, lighting — lighting), then find the matching stage direction in Text 1.

variantlar.savol: Various technical staff take part in preparing the production. In which row is each staff member matched with the correct stage direction from Text 1?
javoblar: Props master — “in the middle, a small supa”; sound operator — “turtle doves coo”; lighting operator — “the sun is setting”.
Props master — “picks up her little basket”; sound operator — “Dildora sings softly”; lighting operator — “it becomes completely dark”.
Props master — “picks up her little basket”; sound operator — “the creak of the potter’s wheel”; lighting operator — “it becomes completely dark”.
Props master — “the creak of the potter’s wheel”; sound operator — “the lid of a tandir oven clatters”; lighting operator — “the sun is setting”.

yechim.doska: Prop = an object that is picked up
yechim.ovoz: According to Text 2, the props master finds objects such as a basket or a teacup.
Dildora picks up her little basket — that is a prop.
The wheel is not seen on stage; only its sound is heard — that is a sound effect.
Creating darkness with lights is the lighting operator’s job.
All three pairs are correct only in row C.

xatolar.0: The supa is part of the scenery, made by the set designer; Text 2 says that scenery is not props.
xatolar.1: The actor sings Dildora’s song herself — that is not a sound effect.
xatolar.3: The creaking of the wheel is a sound effect, not a prop (an object that is picked up).

variantlar.maslahat: In a two-text task, first take the “key” from the text with the definitions, then apply it to the main text.
