The body heats up when running, and faster breathing is the main way to cool the body.

yechim.doska: Muscle: glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + energy
yechim.ovoz: In muscles, energy is released through cellular respiration.

yechim.doska: During exercise, O₂ use and CO₂ production increase
yechim.ovoz: When there is a lot of work, a lot of oxygen is used and a lot of CO₂ is produced.

yechim.doska: Fast breathing: more O₂ in, CO₂ out
yechim.ovoz: Breathing speeds up to meet this need.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) more O₂ is needed, more CO₂ is removed
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: “More air” is too general: what matters is that the body needs more oxygen and must remove more CO₂.
xatolar.1: A faster heartbeat is also a result of the same need; it is not the cause of faster breathing.
xatolar.3: The human body cools mainly through sweat; the main reason for faster breathing is gas exchange.

variantlar.maslahat: In questions about breathing, name the specific gases — oxygen and carbon dioxide — not just “air.”

kunikma: Distinguishing the variable that is deliberately changed (independent) from the variable that is measured
usul: What did the researchers deliberately make different in the two parts of the field, and what did they only count?

variantlar.savol:
Were the following factors deliberately changed in the study?
1) The number of insects in the fields.
2) The type of herbicide used.

yechim.doska: Two parts: new herbicide / usual herbicide
yechim.ovoz: Each part of the field was deliberately sprayed with a different herbicide.

yechim.doska: The number of insects is the result; it was counted
yechim.ovoz: The researchers did not change the number of insects; they measured it.
So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: The number of insects is a measured result; no one changed it deliberately.
xatolar.1: It is the other way around: the type of herbicide was deliberately changed, and the number of insects was measured.
xatolar.3: The type of herbicide was deliberately made different in the parts of the field.

variantlar.maslahat: The factor that is changed is chosen by the researcher; the factor that is measured is observed in the result.

kunikma: Understanding why a study is repeated in many places
usul: Soil, climate and irrigation are not the same in different regions. How does this help to generalize the results?

variantlar.savol: Why did the scientists plant the cotton not in one field, but in 150 fields in different regions?
javoblar: So that more farmers could try GM cotton.
To find out how much cotton can be grown.
To include the different conditions (soil, climate) in which cotton grows.
To cover as much land as possible with GM cotton.

yechim.doska: One field → the result might be due to chance
yechim.ovoz: The result from one field may depend on the special conditions of that place.

yechim.doska: Many places → different soils and climates
yechim.ovoz: Different regions cover different conditions.

yechim.doska: The result is more reliable and can be generalized
yechim.ovoz: Then the conclusion can be applied to the whole country.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) to include different growing conditions
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: The purpose of the study was not to introduce farmers to the cotton, but to test the effect on insects.
xatolar.1: Crop yield was not measured — what was measured was the number of insects.
xatolar.3: Increasing the area of land is not a scientific goal.

variantlar.maslahat: The results of an experiment repeated in many places are more reliable and can be applied more widely.

kunikma: Counting direct food sources from a food web diagram
usul: Count the arrows coming into each animal — each arrow is one direct food source.

variantlar.savol: In food web A, only two animals have three direct food sources each. Which two animals are they?

yechim.ovoz: The number of arrows coming into an animal equals the number of its food sources.
Three arrows come into the Sparrow.
The Fox also has three; the Snake, Spider, Lizard and Ladybug have two each.
So the correct answer is option D.

xatolar.0: The Snake has two food sources: the Lizard and the Sparrow.
xatolar.1: The Spider feeds only on the Grasshopper and the Aphid — two sources.
xatolar.2: The Lizard (Spider, Grasshopper) and the Ladybug (Aphid, Caterpillar) — two each.

variantlar.maslahat: Pay attention to the direction of the arrow: it points from “what is eaten → what eats it.”

kunikma: Predicting and justifying the effect of the loss of one species in a food web
usul: Check whether, in each web, the animals that eat the Aphid would still have another food source if the Aphid disappeared.

variantlar.savol: Food webs A and B are in different places. Imagine that the Aphid has disappeared in both places. Which is the best prediction and explanation of the effect on the food webs?
javoblar: The effect will be greater in web A, because in web A the Ladybug has only one food source.
The effect will be greater in web B, because in web B the Ladybug has only one food source.
The effect will be greater in web A, because in web A the Ladybug has several food sources.
The effect will be greater in web B, because in web B the Ladybug has several food sources.

yechim.ovoz: In web A, even if the Aphid disappears, the Ladybug can feed on the Caterpillar.
In web B, the Ladybug has no other food — it may disappear too.

yechim.doska: In B, the effect spreads along the chain
yechim.ovoz: If the Ladybug disappears, this also affects the Sparrow, which eats it.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) greater in B: the Ladybug has 1 source
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option B.

xatolar.0: In web A, the Ladybug has two food sources (the Aphid and the Caterpillar), not one.
xatolar.2: Having many food sources does not make the effect greater; it softens it, so the effect in A is weaker.
xatolar.3: In web B, the Ladybug feeds only on the Aphid — there are not several sources.

variantlar.maslahat: The more alternative food pathways there are, the more stable an ecosystem is when one species disappears.

kunikma: Applying inertia to an everyday situation
usul: When the bus suddenly starts moving forward, the water in the cup tends to keep its previous state (being at rest).

variantlar.savol: Sanjar pulled away from the stop sharply (the bus began to speed up quickly). What is most likely to happen to the water in the cup?
javoblar: The water spills over side 1 (the back).
The water spills over side 2 (the front).
The water spills, but it is impossible to say on which side.

yechim.ovoz: The cup is pulled forward together with the bus.

yechim.doska: Because of inertia, the water tends to stay in place
yechim.ovoz: The water tends to keep its previous state of rest and shifts backward relative to the cup.

yechim.doska: The water rises up the back wall (1) and spills
yechim.ovoz: That is why the water spills over side 1.
So the correct answer is option B.

xatolar.0: While speeding up, the water surface tilts; it stays horizontal only during uniform motion.
xatolar.2: Spilling over the front happens when the bus brakes sharply, not when it pulls away.
xatolar.3: The direction of acceleration is known, so the side where it spills can be stated exactly.

variantlar.maslahat: Inertia: an object “resists” a change in its speed — it shifts backward when speeding up and forward when braking.

kunikma: Evaluating an environmental claim by taking the energy production chain into account
usul: Follow all the way back where the electricity for an electric car comes from.

variantlar.savol: Supporters of electric cars say: “Electric cars do not pollute the environment at all.” Are they right?
javoblar: Yes, because an electric car has no exhaust pipe.
Yes, because electricity comes through wires and nothing burns.
No, because an electric car goes faster than a gasoline car.
No, because the power plants that produce the electricity burn gas or coal and pollute the air.

yechim.doska: The electric car itself does not emit gases
yechim.ovoz: On the street, an electric car really does not emit exhaust gases.

yechim.doska: Source of electricity: power plants burning gas/coal
yechim.ovoz: But according to the text, electricity comes mainly from plants that burn gas and coal.

yechim.doska: The pollution happens where the power plant is
yechim.ovoz: So the pollution does not disappear; it just moves to another place.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) no, power plants burn gas/coal
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option D.

xatolar.0: Having no exhaust pipe only explains the situation on the street; the power plant that produces the electricity still pollutes the air.
xatolar.1: The electricity coming through the wires was produced by burning fuel at a power plant.
xatolar.2: Speed is not related to pollution; the answer is right, but the explanation is wrong.

variantlar.maslahat: When evaluating environmental claims, consider the whole path of the energy — from production to use.

kunikma: Giving scientific evidence based on data in a diagram
usul: Which bar is the longest, and in which direction does it point? The evidence must be based on the diagram and must support reducing CO₂ specifically.

variantlar.savol: Based on the data in the figure, choose the strongest argument in favor of reducing the CO₂ released by human activity.
javoblar: Particles cool the Earth, so instead of reducing CO₂ we should release more particles into the air.
If the temperature rises, it will be bad for the Earth, so CO₂ must be reduced.
The warming effect of CO₂ is the largest of all the factors, so reducing it will contribute the most to slowing down warming.
Each methane molecule warms more strongly than a CO₂ molecule, so CO₂ is not important.

yechim.ovoz: In the diagram, the CO₂ bar extends farthest to the right.
The effects of methane and nitrous oxide are much smaller.

yechim.doska: Reducing the biggest warming factor is the most effective
yechim.ovoz: So reducing CO₂ emissions will give the biggest result.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) the effect of CO₂ is the largest
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: Particles are harmful to health, and their effect is very uncertain; this is not an argument for reducing CO₂.
xatolar.1: This statement does not use the data in the figure and does not show why it should be CO₂ specifically.
xatolar.3: The effect per molecule is not given in the figure; the figure shows the total effect, and CO₂ has the largest.

variantlar.maslahat: An argument based on a graph is built like this: “According to the figure, ... is the largest/smallest, so ...”

kunikma: Planning a controlled experiment to test a hypothesis
usul: In the experiment, only one factor — the age of the solution — should differ. The type of insect and whether the insects have been exposed to the insecticide before must be the same.

variantlar.savol: Which of the following experiments is the best way to test Rustam’s hypothesis that “the solution has gone bad over time”?
javoblar: Send the old solution to a laboratory every month and have its composition analyzed once, but not compare it with anything.
Spray freshly made solution on the whiteflies in the greenhouse and compare the result with last year’s results.

Divide whiteflies of one kind that have never been exposed to the insecticide into two groups, spray one group with the old solution and the other with a new solution, and compare the proportion that die.
Spray the old solution on the whiteflies in the greenhouse and on the whiteflies at a neighboring farm, and compare the results.

yechim.doska: Variable: the age of the solution (old/new)
yechim.ovoz: The factor being tested is whether the solution has aged.

yechim.doska: The same: whitefly type and no previous exposure
yechim.ovoz: The whiteflies must be of one kind and must not have been sprayed before; otherwise resistance gets mixed in.
If the old solution kills fewer than the new one, the hypothesis is confirmed.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) old and new solution, the same kind of whiteflies
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: There is no comparison: a single analysis does not show that the solution has changed over time.
xatolar.1: The whiteflies in the greenhouse have been sprayed many times before — they may be resistant; also, there is no comparison with the old solution at the same time.
xatolar.3: Here it is the group of whiteflies that is changed, not the age of the solution; the old and new solutions are not compared.

variantlar.maslahat: In a good experiment, only one factor changes and the others are kept the same.

kunikma: Finding alternative scientific explanations for an observed phenomenon (natural selection and other factors)
usul: The reason for the drop in the insecticide’s effectiveness could lie in the solution, in the insects or in the spraying conditions. Each explanation must account for the insecticide killing fewer insects.

variantlar.savol: Choose the most reasonable pair of explanations that account for the drop in the insecticide’s effectiveness by causes other than the solution going bad.
javoblar: 1) The whiteflies were multiplying.  2) New, unsprayed whiteflies flew in from a neighboring farm.
1) Each time it was sprayed, the insecticide had less effect.  2) If there is a lot of solution in the container, it is stronger.
1) The whiteflies smelled the insecticide and flew away during spraying.  2) The tomatoes absorbed the insecticide.
1) Whiteflies resistant to the insecticide survived and passed the resistance on to their offspring.  2) Warmer weather or a change in the spraying method reduced the effect of the insecticide.

yechim.doska: With each spraying, the resistant ones survive
yechim.ovoz: Each time, the most resistant whiteflies survive and multiply.

yechim.doska: Resistance is passed from generation to generation
yechim.ovoz: With each generation, the proportion of resistant insects in the population increases — this is natural selection.
The second explanation depends on changed conditions: heat, or too little or uneven spraying.
So the correct answer is option D.

xatolar.0: The whiteflies multiplying, or new unsprayed whiteflies arriving, does not explain why the insecticide kills FEWER of them: unsprayed whiteflies would actually be sensitive.
xatolar.1: The first only repeats the observation itself (it does not explain the cause), and the second has no basis.
xatolar.2: Neither explanation is supported by evidence; tomatoes “absorbing” the insecticide and protecting the whiteflies was not observed.

variantlar.maslahat: To prevent resistance in pests, it is recommended to alternate between different insecticides.

kunikma: Identifying the main idea (scientific question) tested in an experiment
usul: What was the result of the experiment (four cloned kids)? The main idea must be a question that this result confirms.

variantlar.savol: The results of the experiment confirmed the main idea being tested. Which main idea could have been tested in this experiment?
javoblar: Will the wide use of cloning bring economic benefits to livestock farmers?
Are all the cells of a goat the same?
Is it possible to produce goats with identical genetic material (clones) using the nuclei of embryo cells?
Do surrogate goats pass their genes on to the kids?

yechim.doska: Result: 4 kids with identical genetic material
yechim.ovoz: At the end of the experiment, cloned kids were born.
It confirms that clones can be produced from the nuclei of embryo cells.

yechim.doska: Economic benefit is a later assumption
yechim.ovoz: Economic benefit is the researcher’s opinion; the experiment did not measure it.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) whether clones can be produced from embryo nuclei
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: Costs or income were not measured in the experiment; this is only the researcher’s later opinion.
xatolar.1: The experiment did not test whether the cells are the same; it tested whether clones can be produced.
xatolar.3: The genes of surrogate goats are not passed on to the kids, and this was not the purpose of the experiment.

variantlar.maslahat: To find the main idea, ask: “Which question does the result of the experiment answer directly?”

kunikma: Evaluating conclusions about genetically identical organisms
usul: Which characteristics depend only on genes, and which are also affected by conditions in the mother’s womb and by nutrition?

variantlar.savol:
Which of the following statements are correct?
1) All four kids have the same genes in their nuclei.
2) All four kids are the same sex.
3) All four kids were born with exactly the same weight.

yechim.doska: Nuclei from one embryo → same genes
yechim.ovoz: All the nuclei were taken from the cells of one embryo.

yechim.doska: The sex chromosomes are the same too → same sex
yechim.ovoz: Sex is determined by the sex chromosomes in the nucleus, and these are also identical.

yechim.doska: Weight also depends on conditions in the womb
yechim.ovoz: The kids were carried by different goats, so their birth weights may differ.
So the correct answer is option B.

xatolar.0: Sex is determined by the sex chromosomes in the nucleus — these are also identical, so statement 2 is also correct.
xatolar.2: Birth weight also depends on the nutrition and health of the surrogate mother — it does not have to be exactly the same.
xatolar.3: Statement 3 is incorrect: even if the genes are the same, the environment affects weight.

variantlar.maslahat: Characteristics = genes + environment. Even genetic copies can differ from one another because of the environment.

kunikma: Comparing combustion and cellular respiration (oxidation)
usul: Look at each statement separately: does this also happen during respiration in an organism's cells? Recall what combustion and respiration have in common and how they differ.

variantlar.savol:
Bakhtiyor compares straw burning in a stove with straw inside a cow's body. When straw burns, the following things happen. Do the same things happen when the nutrients in straw are broken down during respiration in the cow's cells?
1) Oxygen is used up.
2) Carbon dioxide is produced.
3) A flame appears and the temperature rises to several hundred degrees.
Decide "Yes" or "No" for each statement and choose the correct sequence.

yechim.ovoz: In cellular respiration, nutrients are oxidized with the help of oxygen, which means oxygen is used up.
One of the products of respiration is carbon dioxide; the cow releases it when it breathes out.
In cells, oxidation happens slowly, step by step, with the help of enzymes; there is no flame, and body temperature stays at about 38–39 °C.
So the correct answer is option B.

xatolar.0: Statement 3 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": in cells, oxidation happens slowly, step by step, with the help of enzymes; there is no flame, and body temperature stays at about 38–39 °C.
xatolar.2: Statement 1 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": in cellular respiration, nutrients are oxidized with the help of oxygen, which means oxygen is used up.
xatolar.3: Statement 2 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": one of the products of respiration is carbon dioxide; the cow releases it when it breathes out.

variantlar.maslahat: Respiration is "slow burning": oxygen is used up and CO₂ and energy are released, but without a flame and at a low temperature.

kunikma: Knowing the substances involved in photosynthesis
usul: Recall the general equation of photosynthesis: from which substances does a plant make glucose and oxygen in the light?

variantlar.savol:
Bakhtiyor said that plants absorb CO₂ and release oxygen. In this process (photosynthesis), more than just these two substances take part. It can be written like this:

carbon dioxide + ☐ —(light)→ glucose + oxygen

Which substance goes in the empty box? (one word)

yechim.ovoz: In photosynthesis, a plant uses light energy to make glucose from simple substances.

yechim.doska: Glucose contains C, H and O
yechim.ovoz: Glucose contains carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. The carbon comes from CO₂, but the hydrogen must come from another substance.
A plant absorbs water through its roots; the oxygen it releases comes from the water molecules.
So the word "water" goes in the box.

xatolar.umumiy: A common mistake is to write "sun" or "light". Light is not a substance; it is a source of energy. "Chlorophyll" is not used up in the reaction either. The substance needed is water.

variantlar.maslahat: Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. The number of atoms must be the same on both sides.

kunikma: Identifying what additional information is needed to draw a conclusion
usul: The table only shows "how strongly the same mass of a gas heats the Earth". Remember that the total effect depends both on strength and on amount.

variantlar.savol:
The ecologist found the following table (IPCC data, rounded):

Warming effect on the Earth of the same mass of gas over 100 years (CO₂ = 1)
Carbon dioxide (CO₂) — 1
Methane (CH₄) — 28
Nitrous oxide (N₂O) — 265
Sulfur hexafluoride (SF₆) — 23 500

From this table alone, it is impossible to tell which gas contributes most to increased global warming. What other information does the ecologist need?
javoblar: Information about how much of each gas is released into and builds up in the atmosphere
Information about the size of each gas molecule
Information about the color and smell of the gases
Information about the boiling points of the gases

yechim.ovoz: The total warming effect of a gas depends both on the strength of one unit of the gas and on its total amount in the atmosphere.

yechim.doska: SF₆ is strong but very scarce
yechim.ovoz: For example, SF₆ is very strong, but there is very little of it in the atmosphere; CO₂ is weak, but billions of tons of it are released.
That is why we need to know how much of each gas is released and how much builds up.
So the correct answer is option A.

xatolar.1: The numbers in the table already include the warming strength related to the molecule; molecule size does not tell you how much of the gas there is.
xatolar.2: Color and smell have nothing to do with the warming effect; most of these gases are colorless.
xatolar.3: The boiling point does not help determine how much a gas in the atmosphere contributes to warming.

variantlar.maslahat: For the question "Which contributes the most?" you always need two things: the effect of one unit and the number of units (the amount).

kunikma: Explaining the natural purification of groundwater
usul: Imagine where groundwater comes from and which layers it passes through before it gets there.

variantlar.savol: In many villages, people drink well or spring water, that is, groundwater. Why does groundwater usually contain fewer bacteria and muddy particles than river or ditch water?
javoblar: Because it is very hot underground, the bacteria are boiled to death
As the water seeps through layers of soil, sand and gravel, it is filtered naturally
Groundwater contains a lot of oxygen, which kills bacteria
Groundwater always flows very fast, so nothing sticks to it

yechim.doska: Groundwater = water that has seeped down
yechim.ovoz: Rain and snowmelt soak into the ground and seep downward between the layers.
As the water passes through tiny pores, muddy particles and many microbes are trapped.
In addition, groundwater is not exposed: dust and animal and human waste do not get into it directly.
So the correct answer is option B.

xatolar.0: The temperature of groundwater is usually about 10–15 °C, which is very far from boiling.
xatolar.2: On the contrary, groundwater usually contains little dissolved oxygen; oxygen does not kill bacteria.
xatolar.3: Groundwater moves very slowly between the layers; fast flow is not the reason it is clean.

variantlar.maslahat: Sand and gravel are nature's own filter. The sand filters at water treatment plants are based on the same principle.

kunikma: Understanding the idea behind settling (sedimentation)
usul: What happens to heavy particles in water when the water is still or flows very slowly? Think of a glass of muddy water.

variantlar.savol: In the second stage, the water flows very slowly through the settling tank for several hours. How does this stage clean the water?
javoblar: Harmful bacteria in the water die in the dark
Heavy particles such as clay and sand sink to the bottom of the basin
Oxygen from the air is added to the water
Salts dissolved in the water separate out

yechim.ovoz: When the water is almost still, there is no current to stir it.
Grains of clay and sand, which are denser than water, sink to the bottom because of gravity.
So the correct answer is option B.

xatolar.0: Bacteria do not die in the dark; chlorine is added later to get rid of them.
xatolar.2: The job of a settling tank is not to add oxygen; that is a different method (aeration).
xatolar.3: Dissolved salts are spread evenly through the water and are not removed by settling.

variantlar.maslahat: If you leave muddy water in a glass, after a few hours clay collects at the bottom — a settling tank works the same way.

kunikma: Knowing the purpose of chlorinating water
usul: Which kinds of pollution did the earlier stages remove, and which remained? What is the invisible danger?

variantlar.savol: In the fourth stage, a small amount of chlorine is added to the water. Why is this needed?
javoblar: To soften the water, that is, to remove the calcium salts in it
To give the water a pleasant taste
To kill bacteria and other microbes in the water

yechim.doska: Microbes get through the filter too
yechim.ovoz: The screen, settling tank and filter trap particles, but some very tiny microbes can get through.
Chlorine is a strong oxidizing agent; it kills bacteria and viruses.
So the correct answer is option D.

xatolar.0: Chlorine does not remove water hardness (calcium and magnesium salts).
xatolar.1: The water becomes clear in the earlier stages, in the settling tank and the filter.
xatolar.2: Chlorine does not improve the taste; in fact, it can give the water a slight distinctive smell.

variantlar.maslahat: Chlorination is the most widely used way to disinfect drinking water and make it free of microbes.

kunikma: Choosing a way to disinfect water against bacteria at home
usul: Which method actually kills or removes bacteria? What do cooling and settling do?

variantlar.savol: Laboratory staff found that there were still dangerous bacteria in the water after treatment. What should residents do at home before drinking this water?
javoblar: Let the water stand in a container for a day
Cool the water well in the refrigerator

yechim.ovoz: The problem is living bacteria that cannot be seen.
Boiling water for a few minutes kills most dangerous bacteria.
So the correct answer is option B.

xatolar.0: Bacteria are very tiny and light; when water is left to settle, they neither sink nor die.
xatolar.2: In the cold, bacteria multiply more slowly, but they do not die.
xatolar.3: The holes in gauze are thousands of times larger than bacteria; bacteria pass through gauze easily.

variantlar.maslahat: In emergencies, boiling water before drinking it is the simplest and most reliable home method.

kunikma: Knowing waterborne diseases
usul: Recall the cause of each disease and how it spreads: does it enter through the mouth with contaminated water?

variantlar.savol:
Can drinking contaminated water cause the following diseases?
1) Cholera
2) Nearsightedness (myopia)
3) Hepatitis A (jaundice)
Decide "Yes" or "No" for each statement and choose the correct sequence.

yechim.ovoz: Cholera bacteria spread through contaminated water and food.
Myopia is a condition related to the structure of the eye; it is not an infectious disease.
The hepatitis A virus spreads mainly through contaminated water and food.
So the correct answer is option A.

xatolar.1: Statement 2 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": myopia is a condition related to the structure of the eye; it is not an infectious disease.
xatolar.2: Statement 1 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": cholera bacteria spread through contaminated water and food.
xatolar.3: Statement 3 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": the hepatitis A virus spreads mainly through contaminated water and food.

variantlar.maslahat: Waterborne diseases are usually intestinal infections: cholera, typhoid fever, dysentery and hepatitis A.

kunikma: Using a text and a diagram to identify the role of bacteria in a process
usul: Above which arrow in the diagram are the bacteria? What do they turn into what?

variantlar.savol: What is the role of bacteria in making yogurt?
javoblar: Bacteria increase the fat in the milk

yechim.ovoz: In the diagram, the bacteria are at the stage where lactose is turned into lactic acid.
Casein curdling is the result of the acid; the bacteria do not make protein.
So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: Lactose is already present in milk; the bacteria do not produce it, they consume it.
xatolar.1: Casein is milk's own protein; the bacteria do not make it, the acid makes it curdle.
xatolar.3: The text says nothing about fat; the bacteria do not increase the fat.

variantlar.maslahat: Read the arrows in the diagram in order: who turns what into what — that is the "role".

kunikma: Using a scatter plot to identify the relationship between two quantities
usul: How are the points arranged from left to right — do they rise or fall? Rule out statements based on information that is not in the graph.

variantlar.savol:
Students asked 10 families at what temperature they set their yogurt and how many hours it took to thicken, and they plotted the results on a graph. Each point is one family.

Which of the following statements is supported by the data in the graph?
javoblar: Yogurt set at a warmer temperature tastes better
Families are setting yogurt faster year after year
Yogurt set faster in families that bought more milk
Within the range of 30–43 °C, the higher the setting temperature, the faster the yogurt usually thickened

yechim.doska: x is temperature, y is setting time
yechim.ovoz: The horizontal axis shows temperature, and the vertical axis shows thickening time.

yechim.doska: The points fall toward the right
yechim.ovoz: At 30 °C it takes about 11.5 hours, while at 42–43 °C it takes 4.5–5 hours.
So as the temperature increased, the setting time usually got shorter. Taste, years and amount of milk are not shown in the graph.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) the higher the temperature, the faster it sets
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option D.

xatolar.0: The graph contains no information about taste.
xatolar.1: There are no years in the graph — all the data were collected at the same time.
xatolar.2: The amount of milk is not shown in the graph.

variantlar.maslahat: When drawing conclusions from a graph, you can only talk about the quantities shown on the axes.

kunikma: Identifying questions that can be answered by a scientific experiment
usul: Can the question be measured and compared in an experiment? Questions about price, fairness or whether something "should" be done depend on values or agreement.

variantlar.savol:
In one neighborhood, homemade yogurt often sets very slowly. Can the following questions be answered by a scientific experiment?
1) Does boiling and cooling milk before setting it affect how long the yogurt takes to set?
2) How much should one liter of yogurt cost at the bazaar?
Decide "Yes" or "No" for each statement and choose the correct sequence.

yechim.doska: 1) Effect of boiling on setting time → Yes
yechim.ovoz: You can boil half of the same milk and leave the other half unboiled, set both under the same other conditions, and measure the time.

yechim.doska: 2) Price of one liter of yogurt → No
yechim.ovoz: Price is a matter of economics and agreement; it cannot be measured in an experiment.
So the correct answer is option A.

xatolar.1: Statement 2 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": price is a matter of economics and agreement; it cannot be measured in an experiment.
xatolar.2: Statement 1 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": you can boil half of the same milk and leave the other half unboiled, set both under the same other conditions, and measure the time.
xatolar.3: Statement 1 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": you can boil half of the same milk and leave the other half unboiled, set both under the same other conditions, and measure the time. Statement 2 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": price is a matter of economics and agreement; it cannot be measured in an experiment.

variantlar.maslahat: In a question that can be answered by an experiment, the quantity you change and the quantity you measure are clear.

kunikma: Understanding thermal equilibrium and the difference between temperature and thermal conductivity
usul: What happens to the temperature of objects that stay in one place for a long time? Remember that "feeling hot" is not about temperature but about how fast heat is transferred.

variantlar.savol:
Are the following statements about the items in the trunk true after several hours?
1) The water, the wrenches and the ruler are at the same temperature (about the air temperature).
2) The wrenches are at a higher temperature than the ruler, so they feel hotter when you touch them.
3) The water in the bottle starts to boil.
Decide "Yes" or "No" for each statement and choose the correct sequence.

yechim.ovoz: Objects that stay in the same surroundings for a long time reach thermal equilibrium — their temperatures become equal.
The temperatures are the same; metal feels hotter because it transfers heat to your hand faster.
Water boils at 100 °C; 55 °C is not enough.
So the correct answer is option A.

xatolar.1: Statement 2 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": the temperatures are the same; metal feels hotter because it transfers heat to your hand faster.
xatolar.2: Statement 1 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": objects that stay in the same surroundings for a long time reach thermal equilibrium — their temperatures become equal. Statement 2 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": the temperatures are the same; metal feels hotter because it transfers heat to your hand faster.
xatolar.3: Statement 2 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": the temperatures are the same; metal feels hotter because it transfers heat to your hand faster. Statement 3 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": water boils at 100 °C; 55 °C is not enough.

variantlar.maslahat: Temperature is a property of an object, while "feeling hot" is about how fast heat passes to your hand. Metal conducts heat well; wood conducts it poorly.

kunikma: Understanding that objects cool down or warm up toward the temperature of their surroundings
usul: Each drink changes toward room temperature (24 °C). Neither goes past room temperature, and neither fully reaches it in 10 minutes.

variantlar.savol: At lunch, Jasur poured hot tea at 85 °C into one mug and cold ayran at 4 °C into an identical second mug. The two drinks have the same volume. He left the mugs in a room where the temperature is 24 °C. About what temperature will the tea and the ayran be after 10 minutes?

yechim.ovoz: The tea is hotter than the room, so it gives off heat and cools, but in 10 minutes it does not drop to 24 °C.
The ayran is colder than the room, so it warms up, but it cannot go above 24 °C.
The difference between the tea and the room is large (61 °C), so the tea changes faster; for the ayran the difference is 20 °C.
So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: The temperature will definitely change within 10 minutes — the mugs are not insulated.
xatolar.1: The ayran cannot become warmer than room temperature (24 °C): heat only flows from a warmer object to a colder one.
xatolar.3: Reaching the same temperature completely takes much longer; 10 minutes is not enough.

variantlar.maslahat: Any object gradually approaches the temperature of its surroundings, but it does not "jump past" it.

kunikma: Explaining that a mutation can give an organism new characteristics
usul: Which insect a fungus infects depends on its genes. What can happen if the genes change?

variantlar.savol: Critics worry that the modified fungus could also infect insects other than locusts. Which reason best explains this concern?
javoblar: The genes of the fungus and the genes of honeybees are the same
A mutation could turn locusts and honeybees into a single species
This fungus has the same number of genes as other fungi
A mutation in the fungus's DNA could make it able to infect other insects too

yechim.doska: Whom it infects depends on genes
yechim.ovoz: Which insect a fungus can attach to and enter is determined by its genes.
A random change in DNA — a mutation — could allow the fungus to infect a new host.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) a mutation could let it infect a new host
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option D.

xatolar.0: A fungus and an insect are completely different organisms; their genes are not the same.
xatolar.1: A mutation in the fungus cannot change the species of insects.
xatolar.2: It is not the number of genes but the genes themselves (what they contain) that determines which insect is infected.

variantlar.maslahat: When judging the risk of a genetically modified organism, ask: "Could it mutate again later and change its properties?"

kunikma: Evaluating the consequences of losing one link in a food chain
usul: Think in two directions: who eats locusts, and what do locusts eat? Remember animals whose diet does not depend on just one food source.

variantlar.savol:
If the fungus spread and completely wiped out the locusts in an area, could the following consequences occur?

2) Domestic chickens are left without food and die out.
3) Wild grasses that locusts eat increase for a while.
Decide "Yes" or "No" for each statement and choose the correct sequence.

yechim.ovoz: Locusts are food for many birds and lizards; if locusts disappear, the food chains are disrupted.
Domestic chickens are mainly fed grain and feed; they do not depend on locusts.
If an insect that eats grass disappears, the grass may increase, at least for a while.
So the correct answer is option A.

xatolar.1: Statement 2 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": domestic chickens are mainly fed grain and feed; they do not depend on locusts.
xatolar.2: Statement 1 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": locusts are food for many birds and lizards; if locusts disappear, the food chains are disrupted.
xatolar.3: Statement 3 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": if an insect that eats grass disappears, the grass may increase, at least for a while.

variantlar.maslahat: If one link in a food chain disappears, both its consumers and its food sources are affected.

kunikma: Identifying questions that must be researched before using a new biological agent
usul: Is each question about safety, effectiveness or how the agent is applied? These things must be known before it is released into the field.

2) How long will it take for locusts to become resistant to the fungus?
3) Which method of spreading the fungal spores over the field works best?
Decide "Yes" or "No" for each statement and choose the correct sequence.

If resistance appears quickly, the agent will stop working; this must be known in advance.
The method affects both how well it works and the risk of reaching other organisms.

xatolar.1: Statement 2 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": if resistance appears quickly, the agent will stop working; this must be known in advance. Statement 3 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": the method affects both how well it works and the risk of reaching other organisms.
xatolar.2: Statement 3 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": the method affects both how well it works and the risk of reaching other organisms.
xatolar.3: Statement 1 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": this is the most important safety question: useful insects must not be harmed.

variantlar.maslahat: Before using a biological agent, you need to know three things: is it safe, does it work, and how is it applied?

kunikma: Identifying the research question of an experiment (variable and measured quantity)
usul: What was changed in the experiment (the independent variable) and what was counted (the dependent variable)? The right question must link the two.

kunikma: Knowing the function of the circulatory system
usul: How does nicotine get from the mouth to the brain? Think about which organ each function in the options actually belongs to.

variantlar.savol: After nicotine passes from the lining of the mouth into the blood, it reaches the brain within a few minutes. Which of the following is a function of blood?
javoblar: Carrying oxygen, nutrients and other substances to all the organs of the body
Carrying nerve signals from the brain to the muscles

yechim.doska: Blood is a means of transport
yechim.ovoz: Blood circulates through the blood vessels and carries oxygen, nutrients and hormones.

yechim.doska: Nicotine travels in the blood too
yechim.ovoz: Foreign substances that enter the blood, such as nicotine, reach the brain the same way.

yechim.doska: Answer: A) carrying substances to the organs
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option A.

xatolar.2: No organ turns CO₂ into oxygen; the blood carries CO₂ to the lungs, where it is breathed out.
xatolar.3: Nerve signals are carried by nerves, not by blood.

variantlar.maslahat: Blood is the body's "transport system": it delivers both useful and harmful substances to all the organs.

kunikma: Distinguishing diseases whose risk naswar use increases from those it does not
usul: Is the disease linked to constant irritation of the tissues of the mouth, or is it caused by a virus infection?

variantlar.savol:
Does using naswar increase the risk of getting the following diseases?
1) Mouth cancer
2) Measles
3) Gum disease (periodontal disease)
Decide "Yes" or "No" for each statement and choose the correct sequence.

yechim.ovoz: As the text says, naswar users have a higher risk of mouth cancer.
Measles is a disease caused by a virus that spreads through the air in droplets; naswar does not increase its risk.
Lime and tobacco constantly irritate the gums and lead to gum diseases.
So the correct answer is option A.

xatolar.1: Statement 2 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": measles is a disease caused by a virus that spreads through the air in droplets; naswar does not increase its risk.
xatolar.2: Statement 1 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": as the text says, naswar users have a higher risk of mouth cancer.
xatolar.3: Statement 3 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": lime and tobacco constantly irritate the gums and lead to gum diseases.

variantlar.maslahat: The harm from naswar shows up first where it is in direct contact — in the mouth.

kunikma: Choosing an experimental design with a control group and random assignment
usul: To see the effect of the gum, you need to compare a group that gets it with a group that does not. What should be done so that the groups are alike in every other way?

variantlar.savol: To test how well a nicotine gum helps people quit naswar, 120 people who want to quit were selected at random. They will be followed for 6 months. Effectiveness will be judged by the number of people who have not gone back to naswar at the end of the 6 months. Which experimental design is best?
javoblar: Each person chooses whether or not to chew the gum
A randomly chosen half chews nicotine gum, and the other half chews gum that looks and tastes the same but has no nicotine
Everyone except one person chews nicotine gum

yechim.ovoz: If we do not know what the result would be without the gum, we cannot judge how much the gum helps.
Dividing people into groups at random makes sure the groups are alike in other ways.
Both groups chew gum, and only the nicotine is different — so it becomes clear that the effect is due to the nicotine itself.

yechim.doska: Answer: C) random half + gum without nicotine
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: If everyone gets the gum, there is no group to compare with — it remains unknown how many people would quit without the gum.
xatolar.1: People who choose for themselves may be different (for example, have stronger willpower); the difference could come from that, not from the gum.
xatolar.3: One person is far too small a control group; no reliable conclusion can be drawn from it.

variantlar.maslahat: A good experiment has a control group, the groups are formed at random, and only one factor is different.

kunikma: Distinguishing technology-based measures from social and legal measures
usul: Technology means creating a new product or device. Price, taxes and bans are economic and legal measures.

Various measures are used to encourage people to give up naswar. Are the following measures based on technology?
1) Producing nicotine gum
2) Raising the excise tax on naswar sales
3) Banning the sale of tobacco products near schools
Decide "Yes" or "No" for each statement and choose the correct sequence.

This is an economic measure; no technology is used.
This is a legal measure.
So the correct answer is option A.

xatolar.1: Statement 2 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": this is an economic measure; no technology is used.
xatolar.2: Statement 1 was marked "No", but it is actually "Yes": this means creating a new product, that is, a technological solution.
xatolar.3: Statement 2 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": this is an economic measure; no technology is used. Statement 3 was marked "Yes", but it is actually "No": this is a legal measure.

kunikma: Explaining the effect of light pollution on sky watching
usul: What is the biggest difference between the sky over a city and over a village? Where — at what height above the Earth — do meteors burn up?

variantlar.savol: Why can more meteors be seen in a mountain village than in the city?
javoblar: The mountains are closer to the meteors, so they look bigger
City lights brighten the sky, so faint meteors cannot be seen
Because the city air is warm, meteors burn up before they reach the sky above the city
The Moon looks brighter in the city and blocks the meteors

yechim.ovoz: Street, building and advertising lights light up the air and make the background of the sky brighter.
Against a bright background, faint meteors and stars "disappear"; in a dark village sky they are visible.
So the correct answer is option B.

xatolar.0: Meteors burn up at a height of about 80–100 km; a mountain's height of 1–2 km makes almost no difference.
xatolar.2: Meteors burn up in the upper atmosphere; the temperature of the air near the ground does not affect this.
xatolar.3: The Moon is just as bright in the city as in the village.

variantlar.maslahat: Light pollution is the main enemy of sky watching in cities. That is why observatories are built far from cities.

kunikma: Understanding that the light-gathering ability of an optical instrument depends on the lens diameter
usul: Both pairs of binoculars magnify the same amount, so the difference is not in magnification. What is the advantage of a lens with a large diameter?

variantlar.savol:
Malika tried two pairs of binoculars to observe faint stars:
• "10×25" — magnifies 10 times, objective lens diameter 25 mm;
• "10×50" — magnifies 10 times, objective lens diameter 50 mm.

With the "10×50" binoculars, much fainter stars could also be seen. What is the main reason for this?
javoblar: A large lens shows a wider part of the sky
A lens with a larger diameter gathers more light
A large lens can also detect the dark colors of stars

yechim.ovoz: Both pairs of binoculars magnify 10 times, so that is not the reason.
The area of a lens is proportional to the square of its diameter: a 50 mm lens collects 4 times as much light.
When more of the small amount of light coming from a faint star is collected, the star becomes visible to the eye.
So the correct answer is option C.

xatolar.0: The problem says that both pairs of binoculars magnify 10 times.
xatolar.1: The field of view does not make faint stars visible; it only determines how much of the sky is seen at once.
xatolar.3: Stars do not have "dark colors"; the issue is the amount of light.

variantlar.maslahat: To see faint objects with a telescope or binoculars, the most important thing is the objective diameter (the light-gathering area).

kunikma: Understanding that time must be measured to find distance by the echo method
usul: How are distance, speed and time related? If the speed is known, what other quantity is needed to find the distance?

variantlar.savol: To build the image, the machine calculates the distance from the probe to each part of the heart. The speed of ultrasound is known. What else must the machine measure to calculate the distance?
javoblar: The frequency of the sound wave
The strength (amplitude) of the returning wave
The time from when the wave is sent until the echo returns

yechim.ovoz: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.
The speed is known to be 1540 m/s, so the time must be measured.
The wave travels to the heart and back, so the distance found is divided by two.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) the echo return time
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option D.

xatolar.0: Frequency affects image quality, but time is what is needed to calculate distance.
xatolar.1: The strength of the returning wave helps tell types of tissue apart, but it does not give the distance.
xatolar.2: Body temperature is not needed to calculate the distance.

variantlar.maslahat: In all instruments that measure distance by echo (echo sounders, bats, ultrasound scanners), the key measurement is the round-trip time.

kunikma: Explaining the danger of ionizing radiation to a growing organism
usul: How are X-rays different from ultrasound? What can they do to a cell, especially a rapidly dividing cell?

variantlar.savol: The chest can also be examined using X-rays. However, doctors try to avoid X-ray examinations for children and pregnant women whenever possible. What is the main reason for this?
javoblar: X-ray images of children are not clear enough
X-rays can damage the DNA of rapidly dividing, growing cells
X-rays heat the body and burn the skin
X-rays are sound waves and damage the ears

yechim.ovoz: X-rays are high-energy electromagnetic waves; they can ionize molecules.

yechim.doska: Rapidly dividing cells are at risk
yechim.ovoz: In a growing organism (a child or an unborn baby), cells divide quickly and are sensitive to DNA damage.
Ultrasound is a mechanical wave; it does not ionize, so it is safer.
So the correct answer is option B.

xatolar.0: How clear an X-ray image is does not depend on age; the reason is the health risk.
xatolar.2: A medical X-ray dose does not noticeably heat the body; the danger is ionization inside the cells.
xatolar.3: X-rays are not sound; they are electromagnetic waves.

variantlar.maslahat: Ionizing radiation (X-rays, gamma rays) can damage DNA, while ultrasound and ordinary light do not ionize.

kunikma: Evaluating what an ultrasound examination can and cannot do
usul: Ultrasound shows only structure and movement — shape, size, thickness and motion. It does not give chemical information such as the composition of the blood.

variantlar.savol:
Can a heart ultrasound answer the following questions?
1) How much cholesterol is in the blood?
2) Do the heart valves close completely?
3) Is the thickness of the heart wall normal?

kunikma: Analyzing data in a table to choose the most suitable location
usul: For a turbine, it is important both that the wind is strong and that it blows steadily all year. Also look at each location's weakest season.

variantlar.savol:
To build a wind power plant, the average wind speed by season was measured at four locations (m/s):

Location 1: winter 9.0; spring 5.0; summer 1.5; fall 4.0
Location 2: winter 7.5; spring 8.0; summer 7.0; fall 7.5
Location 3: winter 3.0; spring 3.5; summer 2.5; fall 3.0
Location 4: winter 1.5; spring 12.0; summer 2.0; fall 2.5

The turbine blades turn only when the wind speed is above 3 m/s. Which location is most suitable for producing electricity?

yechim.ovoz: For the turbine to work all year, the wind must be strong enough in every season.
The yearly average speed is greatest at location 2: (7.5 + 8.0 + 7.0 + 7.5) : 4 = 7.5 m/s.
At location 2, the speed does not drop below 7 m/s in any season; at the other locations, the turbine would stand still for long periods.
So the correct answer is option B.

xatolar.0: The wind is strong in winter, but in summer it is 1.5 m/s — the turbine hardly works.
xatolar.2: The wind is steady but very weak; much of the time it does not even reach 3 m/s.
xatolar.3: It is strong only in spring; in the other three seasons the turbine is almost always stopped.

variantlar.maslahat: When choosing a location for a wind power plant, do not look only at the largest value; look at how steady the wind is throughout the year.

kunikma: Explaining the effect of air density on wind energy
usul: The wind gives energy to the blades through the mass of moving air. Is the mass of a given volume of cold air different from that of warm air?

variantlar.savol: Observations showed that at the same wind speed, a turbine produces slightly more electricity in winter than in summer. What is the best explanation for this?
javoblar: The Earth's gravity is stronger in winter
Because the days are short in winter, the turbine heats up less
The air is more humid in winter, and humid air is heavier
Cold air is denser, so at the same speed a greater mass of air hits the blades and gives them more energy

yechim.ovoz: The kinetic energy of moving air depends on its mass.
When the temperature drops, air density increases: the same volume holds a greater mass of air.
At the same speed, denser air turns the blades more strongly.

yechim.doska: Answer: D) cold air is denser
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option D.

xatolar.0: Gravity does not change noticeably with the seasons.
xatolar.1: The length of the day does not directly affect wind energy.
xatolar.2: On the contrary, humid air is slightly lighter than dry air (a water vapor molecule is lighter than nitrogen and oxygen molecules); besides, cold air usually holds little moisture.

variantlar.maslahat: Wind energy is directly proportional to air density: air in cold, low-lying places is denser, and air in high mountains is thinner.

kunikma: Evaluating the advantages and disadvantages of wind power compared with coal and oil
usul: Check both parts of each pair: is the advantage really an advantage, and is the disadvantage really a disadvantage of wind power?

variantlar.savol: Choose the pair that correctly states an advantage and a disadvantage of producing electricity with wind compared with fuels such as coal and oil.
javoblar: Advantage: it gives the same power day and night. Disadvantage: birds may fly into the blades
Advantage: it releases no CO₂ when producing electricity. Disadvantage: if there is no wind, no electricity is produced
Advantage: it uses no fuel. Disadvantage: it releases a lot of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere
Advantage: it releases more toxic smoke than coal. Disadvantage: the turbines are noisy

yechim.ovoz: Nothing is burned while the turbine is running, so no CO₂ or toxic smoke is released.
Wind speed cannot be controlled; on windless days, no electricity is produced.
Only one pair has both a correct advantage and a correct disadvantage.

yechim.doska: Answer: B) no CO₂; depends on the wind
yechim.ovoz: So the correct answer is option B.

xatolar.0: The advantage is wrong: wind speed keeps changing, so the power changes too.
xatolar.2: The disadvantage is wrong: a wind turbine releases no carbon dioxide while it is running.
xatolar.3: "More toxic smoke" is not an advantage and is simply wrong; a wind turbine releases no smoke.

variantlar.maslahat: Wind energy is clean and inexhaustible, but variable. That is why it is used together with other sources or with energy storage.
